3.5.d: प्रत्यग्निरुषसश्चेकितानोऽबोधि विप्रः पदवीः कवीनाम् । पृथुपाजा देवयद्भिः समिद्धोऽप द्वारा तमसो वह्निरावः ॥
3.5.e: AGNI who shines against the Dawns is wakened. The holy Singer who precedes the sages.  With far-spread lustre, kindled by the pious, the Priest hath thrown both gates of darkness open.

3.5.d: प्रेद्वग्निर्वावृधे स्तोमेभिर्गीर्भिः स्तोतॄणां नमस्य उक्थैः । पूर्वीर्ऋतस्य संदृशश्चकानः सं दूतो अद्यौदुषसो विरोके ॥
3.5.e: Agni hath waxen mighty by laudations, to be adored with hymns of those who praise him.  Loving the varied shows of holy Order at the first flush of dawn he shines as envoy.

3.5.d: अधाय्यग्निर्मानुषीषु विक्ष्व१पां गर्भो मित्र ऋतेन साधन् । आ हर्यतो यजतः सान्वस्थादभूदु विप्रो हव्यो मतीनाम् ॥
3.5.e: Amid men's homes hath Agni been established, fulfilling with the Law, Friend, germ of waters.  Loved and adored, the height he hath ascended, the Singer, object of our invocations.

3.5.d: मित्रो अग्निर्भवति यत्समिद्धो मित्रो होता वरुणो जातवेदाः । मित्रो अध्वर्युरिषिरो दमूना मित्रः सिन्धूनामुत पर्वतानाम् ॥
3.5.e: Agni is Mitra when enkindled duly, Mitra as Priest, Varuṇa, Jātavedas;  Mitra as active minister, and House-Friend, Mitra of flowing rivers and of mountains.

3.5.d: पाति प्रियं रिपो अग्रं पदं वेः पाति यह्वश्चरणं सूर्यस्य । पाति नाभा सप्तशीर्षाणमग्निः पाति देवानामुपमादमृष्वः ॥
3.5.e: The Earth's, the Bird's dear lofty place he guardeth, he guardeth in his might the course of Sūrya,  Guardeth the Seven-headed in the centre, guardeth sublime the Deities enjoyment.

3.5.d: ऋभुश्चक्र ईड्यं चारु नाम विश्वानि देवो वयुनानि विद्वान् । ससस्य चर्म घृतवत्पदं वेस्तदिदग्नी रक्षत्यप्रयुच्छन् ॥
3.5.e: The skilful God who knows all forms of knowledge made for himself a fair form, meet for worship.  This Agni guards with care that never ceases the Soma's skin, the Bird's place rich in fatness.

3.5.d: आ योनिमग्निर्घृतवन्तमस्थात्पृथुप्रगाणमुशन्तमुशानः । दीद्यानः शुचिर्ऋष्वः पावकः पुनःपुनर्मातरा नव्यसी कः ॥
3.5.e: Agni hath entered longingly the longing shrine rich with fatness, giving easy access.  Resplendent, pure, sublime and purifying, again, again he renovates his Mothers.

3.5.d: सद्यो जात ओषधीभिर्ववक्षे यदी वर्धन्ति प्रस्वो घृतेन । आप इव प्रवता शुम्भमाना उरुष्यदग्निः पित्रोरुपस्थे ॥
3.5.e: Born suddenly, by plants he grew to greatness, when tender shoots with holy oil increased him,  Like waters lovely when they hasten downward may Agni in his Parents' lap protect us.

3.5.d: उदु ष्टुतः समिधा यह्वो अद्यौद्वर्ष्मन्दिवो अधि नाभा पृथिव्याः । मित्रो अग्निरीड्यो मातरिश्वा दूतो वक्षद्यजथाय देवान् ॥
3.5.e: Extolled, the Strong shone forth with kindled fuel to the earth's centre, to the height of heaven.  May Agni, Friend, adorable Mātariśvan, as envoy bring the Gods unto our worship.

3.5.d: उदस्तम्भीत्समिधा नाकमृष्वो३ऽग्निर्भवन्नुत्तमो रोचनानाम् । यदी भृगुभ्यः परि मातरिश्वा गुहा सन्तं हव्यवाहं समीधे ॥
3.5.e: Best of all luminaries lofty Agni supported with his flame the height of heaven,  When, far from Bhṛgus, Mātariśvan kindled the oblation-bearer where he lay in secret.

3.5.d: इळामग्ने पुरुदंसं सनिं गोः शश्वत्तमं हवमानाय साध । स्यान्नः सूनुस्तनयो विजावाग्ने सा ते सुमतिर्भूत्वस्मे ॥
3.5.e: As holy food, Agni to thine invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels.  To us be born a son and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-word.

3.6.d: प्र कारवो मनना वच्यमाना देवद्रीचीं नयत देवयन्तः । दक्षिणावाड्वाजिनी प्राच्येति हविर्भरन्त्यग्नये घृताची ॥
3.6.e: URGED on by deep devotion, O ye singers, bring, pious ones, the God-approaching ladle.  Borne onward to the right it travels eastward, and, filled with oil, to Agni bears oblation.

3.6.d: आ रोदसी अपृणा जायमान उत प्र रिक्था अध नु प्रयज्यो । दिवश्चिदग्ने महिना पृथिव्या वच्यन्तां ते वह्नयः सप्तजिह्वाः ॥
3.6.e: Thou at thy birth didst fill both earth and heaven, yea, Most Adorable, thou didst exceed them.  Even through the heaven's and through the earth's expanses let thy swift seventongued flames roll on, O Agni.

3.6.d: द्यौश्च त्वा पृथिवी यज्ञियासो नि होतारं सादयन्ते दमाय । यदी विशो मानुषीर्देवयन्तीः प्रयस्वतीरीळते शुक्रमर्चिः ॥
3.6.e: Both Heaven and Earth and Gods who should be worshipped establish thee as Priest for every dwelling,  Whenever human families, God-devoted, bringing oblations; laud thy splendid lustre.

3.6.d: महान्त्सधस्थे ध्रुव आ निषत्तोऽन्तर्द्यावा माहिने हर्यमाणः । आस्क्रे सपत्नी अजरे अमृक्ते सबर्दुघे उरुगायस्य धेनू ॥
3.6.e: Firm in the Gods’ home is the Mighty seated, between vast Heaven and Earth the well-beloved-  Those Cows who yield, unharmed, their nectar, Spouses of the Far-Strider, everyoung, united.

3.6.d: व्रता ते अग्ने महतो महानि तव क्रत्वा रोदसी आ ततन्थ । त्वं दूतो अभवो जायमानस्त्वं नेता वृषभ चर्षणीनाम् ॥
3.6.e: Great are the deeds of thee, the Great, O Agni: thou by thy power hast spread out earth and heaven.  As soon as thou wast born thou wast an envoy, thou, Mighty One, was Leader of the people.

3.6.d: ऋतस्य वा केशिना योग्याभिर्घृतस्नुवा रोहिता धुरि धिष्व । अथा वह देवान्देव विश्वान्त्स्वध्वरा कृणुहि जातवेदः ॥
3.6.e: Bind to the pole with cords of holy Order the long-maned ruddy steeds who sprinkle fatness.  Bring hithier, O thou God, all Gods together: provide them noble worship, Jātavedas.

3.6.d: दिवश्चिदा ते रुचयन्त रोका उषो विभातीरनु भासि पूर्वीः । अपो यदग्न उशधग्वनेषु होतुर्मन्द्रस्य पनयन्त देवाः ॥
3.6.e: Even from the sky thy brilliant lights shone hither: still hast thou beamed through many a radiant morning,  That the Gods praised their joyous Herald's labour eagerly burning, Agni, in the forests.

3.6.d: उरौ वा ये अन्तरिक्षे मदन्ति दिवो वा ये रोचने सन्ति देवाः । ऊमा वा ये सुहवासो यजत्रा आयेमिरे रथ्यो अग्ने अश्वाः ॥
3.6.e: The Gods who take delight in air's wide region, or those the dwellers in heaven's realm of brightness,  Or those, the Holy, prompt to hear, our helpers, who, carborne, turn their horses hither, Agni—-

3.6.d: ऐभिरग्ने सरथं याह्यर्वाङ्नानारथं वा विभवो ह्यश्वाः । पत्नीवतस्त्रिंशतं त्रीँश्च देवाननुष्वधमा वह मादयस्व ॥
3.6.e: With these, borne on one ear, Agni, approach us, or borne on many, for thy steeds are able.  Bring, witb their Dames, the Gods, the Three and-Thirty, after thy Godlike nature, and be joyful.

3.6.d: स होता यस्य रोदसी चिदुर्वी यज्ञंयज्ञमभि वृधे गृणीतः । प्राची अध्वरेव तस्थतुः सुमेके ऋतावरी ऋतजातस्य सत्ये ॥
3.6.e: He is the Priest at whose repeated worship even wide Heaven and Earth sing out for increase.  They fair and true and holy coming forward stand at his sacrifice who springs from Order.

3.6.d: इळामग्ने पुरुदंसं सनिं गोः शश्वत्तमं हवमानाय साध । स्यान्नः सूनुस्तनयो विजावाग्ने सा ते सुमतिर्भूत्वस्मे ॥
3.6.e: As holy food, Agni, to thine invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels.  To us be born a son and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to usward.

3.7.d: प्र य आरुः शितिपृष्ठस्य धासेरा मातरा विविशुः सप्त वाणीः । परिक्षिता पितरा सं चरेते प्र सर्स्राते दीर्घमायुः प्रयक्षे ॥
3.7.e: THE seven tones risen from the whitebacked viand have made their way between the pair of Mothers.  Both circumjacent Parents come together to yield us length of days they hasten forward.

3.7.d: दिवक्षसो धेनवो वृष्णो अश्वा देवीरा तस्थौ मधुमद्वहन्तीः । ऋतस्य त्वा सदसि क्षेमयन्तं पर्येका चरति वर्तनिं गौः ॥
3.7.e: The Male who dwells in heaven hath Mares and Milchkine: he came to Goddesses who bring sweet treasure.  To thee safe resting in the seat of Order the Cow alone upon her way proceedeth.

3.7.d: आ सीमरोहत्सुयमा भवन्तीः पतिश्चिकित्वान्रयिविद्रयीणाम् । प्र नीलपृष्ठो अतसस्य धासेस्ता अवासयत्पुरुधप्रतीकः ॥
3.7.e: Wise Master, wealthy finder-out of riches, he mounted those who may with case be guided.  He, dark-backed, manifold with varied aspect, hath made them burst forth from their food the brush-wood.

3.7.d: महि त्वाष्ट्रमूर्जयन्तीरजुर्यं स्तभूयमानं वहतो वहन्ति । व्यङ्गेभिर्दिद्युतानः सधस्थ एकामिव रोदसी आ विवेश ॥
3.7.e: Strength-giving streams bear hither him eternal, fain to support the mighty work. of Tvaṣṭar.  He, flashing in his home with all his members, hath entered both the worlds as they were single.

3.7.d: जानन्ति वृष्णो अरुषस्य शेवमुत ब्रध्नस्य शासने रणन्ति । दिवोरुचः सुरुचो रोचमाना इळा येषां गण्या माहिना गीः ॥
3.7.e: They know the red Bull's blessing, and are joyful under the flaming-coloured Lord's dominion:  They who give shine from heavenwith fair effulgence, whose lofty song like Iḷā must be honoured.

3.7.d: उतो पितृभ्यां प्रविदानु घोषं महो महद्भ्यामनयन्त शूषम् । उक्षा ह यत्र परि धानमक्तोरनु स्वं धाम जरितुर्ववक्ष ॥
3.7.e: Yea, by tradition from the ancient sages they brought great strength from the two mighty Parents,  To where the singer's Bull, the night's dispeller, after his proper law hath waxen stronger.

3.7.d: अध्वर्युभिः पञ्चभिः सप्त विप्राः प्रियं रक्षन्ते निहितं पदं वेः । प्राञ्चो मदन्त्युक्षणो अजुर्या देवा देवानामनु हि व्रता गुः ॥
3.7.e: Seven holy singers guard with five Adhvaryus the Bird's beloved firmly-settled station.  The willing Bulls, untouched by old, rejoice them: as Gods themselves the ways of Gods they follow.

3.7.d: दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा न्यृञ्जे सप्त पृक्षासः स्वधया मदन्ति । ऋतं शंसन्त ऋतमित्त आहुरनु व्रतं व्रतपा दीध्यानाः ॥
3.7.e: I crave the grace of heaven's two chief Invokers: the seven swift steeds joy in their wonted manner.  These speak of truth, praising the Truth Eternal, thinking on Order as the guards of Order.

3.7.d: वृषायन्ते महे अत्याय पूर्वीर्वृष्णे चित्राय रश्मयः सुयामाः । देव होतर्मन्द्रतरश्चिकित्वान्महो देवान्रोदसी एह वक्षि ॥
3.7.e: The many seek the great Steed as a stallion: the reins obey the Lord of varied colour.  O heavenly Priest, most pleasant, full of wisdom, bring the great Gods to us, and Earth and Heaven.

3.7.d: पृक्षप्रयजो द्रविणः सुवाचः सुकेतव उषसो रेवदूषुः । उतो चिदग्ने महिना पृथिव्याः कृतं चिदेनः सं महे दशस्य ॥
3.7.e: Rich Lord, the Mornings have gleamed forth in splendour, fair-rayed, fair-speaking, worshipped with all viands,  Yea, with the glory of the earth, O Agni. Forgive us, for our weal, e’en sin cornmitted.

3.7.d: इळामग्ने पुरुदंसं सनिं गोः शश्वत्तमं हवमानाय साध । स्यान्नः सूनुस्तनयो विजावाग्ने सा ते सुमतिर्भूत्वस्मे ॥
3.7.e: As holy food, Agni, to thine invoker, give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels.  To us be born a son, and spreading offspring Agni, be this thy gracious will to usward.

3.8.d: अञ्जन्ति त्वामध्वरे देवयन्तो वनस्पते मधुना दैव्येन । यदूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठा द्रविणेह धत्ताद्यद्वा क्षयो मातुरस्या उपस्थे ॥
3.8.e: GOD-SERVING men, O Sovran of the Forest, with heavenly meath at sacrifice anoint thee.  Grant wealth to us when thou art standing upright as when reposing on this Mother's bosom.

3.8.d: समिद्धस्य श्रयमाणः पुरस्ताद्ब्रह्म वन्वानो अजरं सुवीरम् । आरे अस्मदमतिं बाधमान उच्छ्रयस्व महते सौभगाय ॥
3.8.e: Set up to eastward of the fire enkindled, accepting prayer that wastes not, rich in hero.  Driving far from us poverty and famine, lift thyself up to bring us great good fortune.

3.8.d: उच्छ्रयस्व वनस्पते वर्ष्मन्पृथिव्या अधि । सुमिती मीयमानो वर्चो धा यज्ञवाहसे ॥
3.8.e: Lord of the Forest, raise. thyself up on the loftiest spot of earth.  Give splendour, fixt and measured well, to him who brings the sacrifice.

3.8.d: युवा सुवासाः परिवीत आगात्स उ श्रेयान्भवति जायमानः । तं धीरासः कवय उन्नयन्ति स्वाध्यो३ मनसा देवयन्तः ॥
3.8.e: Well-robed, enveloped he is come, the youthful: springing to life his glory waxeth greater.  Contemplative in mind and God-adoring, sages of high intelligence upraise him.

3.8.d: जातो जायते सुदिनत्वे अह्नां समर्य आ विदथे वर्धमानः । पुनन्ति धीरा अपसो मनीषा देवया विप्र उदियर्ति वाचम् ॥
3.8.e: Sprung up he rises in the days' fair weather, increasing in the men-frequented synod.  With song the wise and skilful consecrate him: his voice the God-adoring singer utters.  6, Ye whom religious men have firmly planted; thou Forest Sovran whom the axe hath fashioned,—  Let those the Stakes divine which here are standing be fain to grant us wealth with store of children.

3.8.d: यान्वो नरो देवयन्तो निमिम्युर्वनस्पते स्वधितिर्वा ततक्ष । ते देवासः स्वरवस्तस्थिवांसः प्रजावदस्मे दिधिषन्तु रत्नम् ॥
3.8.e: , Ye whom religious men have firmly planted; thou Forest Sovran whom the axe hath fashioned,– Let those the Stakes divine which here are standing be fain to grant us wealth with store of children.

3.8.d: ये वृक्णासो अधि क्षमि निमितासो यतस्रुचः । ते नो व्यन्तु वार्यं देवत्रा क्षेत्रसाधसः ॥
3.8.e: O men who lift the ladles up, these hewn and planted in the ground,  Bringing a blessing to the field, shall bear our precious gift to Gods.

3.8.d: आदित्या रुद्रा वसवः सुनीथा द्यावाक्षामा पृथिवी अन्तरिक्षम् । सजोषसो यज्ञमवन्तु देवा ऊर्ध्वं कृण्वन्त्वध्वरस्य केतुम् ॥
3.8.e: Ādityas, Rudras, Vasus, careful leaders, Earth, Heaven, and Prthivi and Air's mid-region,  Accordant Deities shall bless our worship and make our sacrifice's ensign lofty.

3.8.d: हंसा इव श्रेणिशो यतानाः शुक्रा वसानाः स्वरवो न आगुः । उन्नीयमानाः कविभिः पुरस्ताद्देवा देवानामपि यन्ति पाथः ॥
3.8.e: Like swan's that flee in lengthened line, the Pillars have come to us arrayed in brilliant coIour.  They, lifted up on high, by sages, eastward, go forth as Gods to the God's dwelling-places.

3.8.d: शृङ्गाणीवेच्छृङ्गिणां सं ददृश्रे चषालवन्तः स्वरवः पृथिव्याम् । वाघद्भिर्वा विहवे श्रोषमाणा अस्माँ अवन्तु पृतनाज्येषु ॥
3.8.e: Those Stakes upon the earth with rings that deck them seem to the eye like horns of horned creatures;  Or, as upraised by priests in invocation, let them assist us in the rush to battle.

3.8.d: वनस्पते शतवल्शो वि रोह सहस्रवल्शा वि वयं रुहेम । यं त्वामयं स्वधितिस्तेजमानः प्रणिनाय महते सौभगाय ॥
3.8.e: Lord of the Wood, rise with a hundred branches. with thousand branches may we rise to greatness,  Tlou whom this hatchct, with an edge well whetted for great felicity, hath brought before us.

3.9.d: सखायस्त्वा ववृमहे देवं मर्तास ऊतये । अपां नपातं सुभगं सुदीदितिं सुप्रतूर्तिमनेहसम् ॥
3.9.e: WE as thy friends have chosen thee, mortals a God, to be our help,  The Waters’ Child, the blessed, the resplendent One, victorious and beyond compare.

3.9.d: कायमानो वना त्वं यन्मातॄरजगन्नपः । न तत्ते अग्ने प्रमृषे निवर्तनं यद्दूरे सन्निहाभवः ॥
3.9.e: Since thou delighting in the woods hast gone unto thy mother streams,  Not to be scorned, Agni, is that return of thine when from afar thou now art here.

3.9.d: अति तृष्टं ववक्षिथाथैव सुमना असि । प्रप्रान्ये यन्ति पर्यन्य आसते येषां सख्ये असि श्रितः ॥
3.9.e: O'er pungent smoke host thou prevailed, and thus art thou benevolent.  Some go before, and others round about thee sit, they in whose friendship thou hast place.

3.9.d: ईयिवांसमति स्रिधः शश्वतीरति सश्चतः । अन्वीमविन्दन्निचिरासो अद्रुहोऽप्सु सिंहमिव श्रितम् ॥
3.9.e: Him who had passed beyond his foes, beyond continual pursuits, Him the unerring Ones, observant, found in floods, couched like a lion in his lair.

3.9.d: ससृवांसमिव त्मनाग्निमित्था तिरोहितम् । ऐनं नयन्मातरिश्वा परावतो देवेभ्यो मथितं परि ॥
3.9.e: Him wandering at his own free will, Agni here hidden from our view,  Him Mātariśvan brought to us from far away produced by friction, from the Gods.

3.9.d: तं त्वा मर्ता अगृभ्णत देवेभ्यो हव्यवाहन । विश्वान्यद्यज्ञाँ अभिपासि मानुष तव क्रत्वा यविष्ठ्य ॥
3.9.e: O Bearer of Oblations, thus mortals received thee from the Gods,  Whilst thou, the Friend of man, guardest each sacrifice with thine own power, Most Youthful One.

3.9.d: तद्भद्रं तव दंसना पाकाय चिच्छदयति । त्वां यदग्ने पशवः समासते समिद्धमपिशर्वरे ॥
3.9.e: Amid thy wonders this is good, yea, to the simple is it clear,  When gathered round about thee, Agni, lie the herds where thou art kindled in the morn.

3.9.d: आ जुहोता स्वध्वरं शीरं पावकशोचिषम् । आशुं दूतमजिरं प्रत्नमीड्यं श्रुष्टी देवं सपर्यत ॥
3.9.e: Offer to him who knows fair rites, who burns with purifying glow,  Swift envoy, active, ancient, and adorable: serve ye the God attentively.

3.9.d: त्रीणि शता त्री सहस्राण्यग्निं त्रिंशच्च देवा नव चासपर्यन् । औक्षन्घृतैरस्तृणन्बर्हिरस्मा आदिद्धोतारं न्यसादयन्त ॥
3.9.e: Three times a hundred Gods and thrice a thousand, and three times ten and nine have worshipped Agni,  For him spread sacred grass, with oil bedewed him, and stablished him as Priest and Sacrificer.

3.10.d: त्वामग्ने मनीषिणः सम्राजं चर्षणीनाम् । देवं मर्तास इन्धते समध्वरे ॥
3.10.e: THEE Agni, God, Imperial Lord of all mankind, do mortal men  With understanding kindle at the sacrifice.

3.10.d: त्वां यज्ञेष्वृत्विजमग्ने होतारमीळते । गोपा ऋतस्य दीदिहि स्वे दमे ॥
3.10.e: They laud thee in their solemn rites, Agni, as Minister and Priest,  Shine forth in thine own home as guardian of the Law.

3.10.d: स घा यस्ते ददाशति समिधा जातवेदसे । सो अग्ने धत्ते सुवीर्यं स पुष्यति ॥
3.10.e: He, verily, who honours thee with fuel, Knower of all life,  He, Agni! wins heroic might, he prospers well.

3.10.d: स केतुरध्वराणामग्निर्देवेभिरा गमत् । अञ्जानः सप्त होतृभिर्हविष्मते ॥
3.10.e: Ensign of sacrifices, he, Agni, with Gods is come to us,  Decked by the seven priests, to him who bringeth gifts.

3.10.d: प्र होत्रे पूर्व्यं वचोऽग्नये भरता बृहत् । विपां ज्योतींषि बिभ्रते न वेधसे ॥
3.10.e: To Agni, the Invoking Priest, offer your best, your lofty speech,  To him Ordainer-like who brings the light of songs.

3.10.d: अग्निं वर्धन्तु नो गिरो यतो जायत उक्थ्यः । महे वाजाय द्रविणाय दर्शतः ॥
3.10.e: Let these our hymns make Agni grow, whence, meet for laud, he springs to life,  To mighty strength and great possession, fair to see.

3.10.d: अग्ने यजिष्ठो अध्वरे देवान्देवयते यज । होता मन्द्रो वि राजस्यति स्रिधः ॥
3.10.e: Best Sacrificer, bring the Gods, O Agni, to the pious man:  A joyful Priest, thy splendour drive our foes afar

3.10.d: स नः पावक दीदिहि द्युमदस्मे सुवीर्यम् । भवा स्तोतृभ्यो अन्तमः स्वस्तये ॥
3.10.e: As such, O Purifier, shine on us heroic glorious might:  Be nearest Friend to those who laud thee, for their weal.

3.10.d: तं त्वा विप्रा विपन्यवो जागृवांसः समिन्धते । हव्यवाहममर्त्यं सहोवृधम् ॥
3.10.e: So, wakeful, versed in sacred hymns, the holy singers kindly thee.  Oblation-bearer, deathless, cherisher of strength.

3.11.d: अग्निर्होता पुरोहितोऽध्वरस्य विचर्षणिः । स वेद यज्ञमानुषक् ॥
3.11.e: AGNI is Priest, the great High Priest of sacrifice, most swift in act:  He knows the rite in constant course.
Oblation-bearer, deathless, well inclined, an eager messenger,  Agni comes nigh us with the thought.

3.11.d: अग्निर्धिया स चेतति केतुर्यज्ञस्य पूर्व्यः । अर्थं ह्यस्य तरणि ॥
3.11.e: Ensign of sacrifice from of old, Agni well knoweth with his thought  To prosper this man's aim and hope.

3.11.d: अग्निं सूनुं सनश्रुतं सहसो जातवेदसम् । वह्निं देवा अकृण्वत ॥
3.11.e: Agni, illustrious from old time, the Son of Strength who knows all life,  The Gods have made to their Priest.

3.11.d: अदाभ्यः पुरएता विशामग्निर्मानुषीणाम् । तूर्णी रथः सदा नवः ॥
3.11.e: Infallible is Agni, he who goes before the tribes of men,  A chariot swift and ever new.
Strength of the Gods which none may harm, subduing all his enemies,  Agni is mightiest in fame.

3.11.d: अभि प्रयांसि वाहसा दाश्वाँ अश्नोति मर्त्यः । क्षयं पावकशोचिषः ॥
3.11.e: By offering sacred food to him the mortal worshipper obtains.  A home from him whose light makes pure.

3.11.d: परि विश्वानि सुधिताग्नेरश्याम मन्मभिः । विप्रासो जातवेदसः ॥
3.11.e: From Agni, by our hymns, may we gain all things that bring happiness,  Singers of him who knows all life.

3.11.d: अग्ने विश्वानि वार्या वाजेषु सनिषामहे । त्वे देवास एरिरे ॥
3.11.e: O Agni, in our deeds of might may we obtain all precious things:  Tle Gods are centred all in thee.

3.12.d: इन्द्राग्नी आ गतं सुतं गीर्भिर्नभो वरेण्यम् । अस्य पातं धियेषिता ॥
3.12.e: MOVED, Indra-Agni, by our hymn, come to the juice, the precious dew:  Drink ye thereof, impelled by song.

3.12.d: इन्द्राग्नी जरितुः सचा यज्ञो जिगाति चेतनः । अया पातमिमं सुतम् ॥
3.12.e: O Indra-Agni, with the man who lauds you comes the wakening rite:  So drink ye both this juice assured.

3.12.d: इन्द्रमग्निं कविच्छदा यज्ञस्य जूत्या वृणे । ता सोमस्येह तृम्पताम् ॥
3.12.e: Through force of sacrifice I choose Indra-Agni who love the wise:  With Soma let these sate them here.

3.12.d: तोशा वृत्रहणा हुवे सजित्वानापराजिता । इन्द्राग्नी वाजसातमा ॥
3.12.e: Indra and Agni I invoke, joint-victors, bounteous, unsubdued,  Foe-slayers, best to win the spoil.

3.12.d: प्र वामर्चन्त्युक्थिनो नीथाविदो जरितारः । इन्द्राग्नी इष आ वृणे ॥
3.12.e: Indra and Agni, singers skilled in melody hymn you, bringing lauds:  I choose you for the sacred food.

3.12.d: इन्द्राग्नी नवतिं पुरो दासपत्नीरधूनुतम् । साकमेकेन कर्मणा ॥
3.12.e: Indra and Agni, ye cast down the ninety forts which Dāsas held,  Together, with one mighty deed.

3.12.d: इन्द्राग्नी अपसस्पर्युप प्र यन्ति धीतयः । ऋतस्य पथ्या३ अनु ॥
3.12.e: To Indra-Agni reverent thoughts go forward from the holy task  Along the path of sacred Law.

3.12.d: इन्द्राग्नी तविषाणि वां सधस्थानि प्रयांसि च । युवोरप्तूर्यं हितम् ॥
3.12.e: O Indra-Agni, powers are yours, and dwellings and delightful food  Good is your readiness to act.

3.12.d: इन्द्राग्नी रोचना दिवः परि वाजेषु भूषथः । तद्वां चेति प्र वीर्यम् ॥
3.12.e: Indra and Agni, in your deeds of might ye deck heaven's lucid realms:  Famed is that hero strength of yours.

3.13.d: प्र वो देवायाग्नये बर्हिष्ठमर्चास्मै । गमद्देवेभिरा स नो यजिष्ठो बर्हिरा सदत् ॥
3.13.e: To Agni, to this God of yours I sing aloud with utmost power.  May he come to us with the Gods, and sit, best Offerer, on the grass.

3.13.d: ऋतावा यस्य रोदसी दक्षं सचन्त ऊतयः । हविष्मन्तस्तमीळते तं सनिष्यन्तोऽवसे ॥
3.13.e: The Holy, whose are earth and heaven, and succour waits upon his strength;  Him men who bring oblations laud, and they who wish to gain, for grace.

3.13.d: स यन्ता विप्र एषां स यज्ञानामथा हि षः । अग्निं तं वो दुवस्यत दाता यो वनिता मघम् ॥
3.13.e: He is the Sage who guides these men, Leader of sacred rites is he.  Him your own Agni, serve ye well, who winneth and bestoweth wealth.

3.13.d: स नः शर्माणि वीतयेऽग्निर्यच्छतु शंतमा । यतो नः प्रुष्णवद्वसु दिवि क्षितिभ्यो अप्स्वा ॥
3.13.e: So may the gracious Agni grant most goodly shelter for our use;  Whence in the heavens or in the floods he shall pour wealth upon our lands.

3.13.d: दीदिवांसमपूर्व्यं वस्वीभिरस्य धीतिभिः । ऋक्वाणो अग्निमिन्धते होतारं विश्पतिं विशाम् ॥
3.13.e: The singers kindle him, the Priest, Agni the Lord of tribes of men,  Resplendent and without a peer through his own excellent designs.

3.13.d: उत नो ब्रह्मन्नविष उक्थेषु देवहूतमः । शं नः शोचा मरुद्वृधोऽग्ने सहस्रसातमः ॥
3.13.e: Help us, thou Brahman, best of all invokers of the Gods in song.  Beam, Friend of Maruts, bliss on us, O Agni, a most liberal God.

3.13.d: नू नो रास्व सहस्रवत्तोकवत्पुष्टिमद्वसु । द्युमदग्ने सुवीर्यं वर्षिष्ठमनुपक्षितम् ॥
3.13.e: Yea, grant us treasure thousandfold with children and with nourishment,  And, Agni, splendid hero strength, exalted, wasting not away.

3.14.d: आ होता मन्द्रो विदथान्यस्थात्सत्यो यज्वा कवितमः स वेधाः । विद्युद्रथः सहसस्पुत्रो अग्निः शोचिष्केशः पृथिव्यां पाजो अश्रेत् ॥
3.14.e: THE pleasant Priest is come into the synod, true, skilled in sacrifice, most wise, Ordainer.  Agni, the Son of Strength, whose car is lightning, whose hair is flame, hath shown on earth his lustre.

3.14.d: अयामि ते नमउक्तिं जुषस्व ऋतावस्तुभ्यं चेतते सहस्वः । विद्वाँ आ वक्षि विदुषो नि षत्सि मध्य आ बर्हिरूतये यजत्र ॥
3.14.e: To thee I offer reverent speech: accept it: to thee who markest it, victorious, faithful!  Bring, thou who knowest, those who know, and seat thee amid the sacred grass, for help, O Holy.

3.14.d: द्रवतां त उषसा वाजयन्ती अग्ने वातस्य पथ्याभिरच्छ । यत्सीमञ्जन्ति पूर्व्यं हविर्भिरा वन्धुरेव तस्थतुर्दुरोणे ॥
3.14.e: The Two who show their vigour, Night and Morning, by the wind's paths shall haste to thee O Agni.  When men adorn the Ancient with oblations, these seek, as on two chariot-seats, the dwelling.

3.14.d: मित्रश्च तुभ्यं वरुणः सहस्वोऽग्ने विश्वे मरुतः सुम्नमर्चन् । यच्छोचिषा सहसस्पुत्र तिष्ठा अभि क्षितीः प्रथयन्त्सूर्यो नॄन् ॥
3.14.e: To thee, strong Agni! Varuṇa and Mitra and all the Maruts sang a song of triumph,  What time unto the people's lands thou camest, spreading them as the Sun of men, with lustre.

3.14.d: वयं ते अद्य ररिमा हि काममुत्तानहस्ता नमसोपसद्य । यजिष्ठेन मनसा यक्षि देवानस्रेधता मन्मना विप्रो अग्ने ॥
3.14.e: Approaching with raised hands and adoration, we have this day fulfilled for thee thy longing.  Worship the Gods with most devoted spirit, a Priest with no unfriendly thought, O Agni.

3.14.d: त्वद्धि पुत्र सहसो वि पूर्वीर्देवस्य यन्त्यूतयो वि वाजाः । त्वं देहि सहस्रिणं रयिं नोऽद्रोघेण वचसा सत्यमग्ने ॥
3.14.e: For, Son of Strength, from thee come many succours, and powers abundant that a God possesses.  Agni, to us with speech that hath no falsehood grant riches, real, to be told in thousands.

3.14.d: तुभ्यं दक्ष कविक्रतो यानीमा देव मर्तासो अध्वरे अकर्म । त्वं विश्वस्य सुरथस्य बोधि सर्वं तदग्ने अमृत स्वदेह ॥
3.14.e: Whatever, God, in sacrifice we mortals have wrought is all for thee, strong, wise of purpose!  Be thou the Friend of each good chariot's master. All this enjoy thou here, immortal Agni.

3.15.d: वि पाजसा पृथुना शोशुचानो बाधस्व द्विषो रक्षसो अमीवाः । सुशर्मणो बृहतः शर्मणि स्यामग्नेरहं सुहवस्य प्रणीतौ ॥
3.15.e: RESPLENDENT with thy wide-extending lustre, dispel the terrors of the fiends who hate us  May lofty Agni be my guide and shelter, the easily-invoked, the good Protector.

3.15.d: त्वं नो अस्या उषसो व्युष्टौ त्वं सूर उदिते बोधि गोपाः । जन्मेव नित्यं तनयं जुषस्व स्तोमं मे अग्ने तन्वा सुजात ॥
3.15.e: Be thou To us, while now the morn is breaking, be thou a guardian when the Sun hath mounted..  Accept, as men accept a true-born infant, my laud, O Agni nobly born in body.

3.15.d: त्वं नृचक्षा वृषभानु पूर्वीः कृष्णास्वग्ने अरुषो वि भाहि । वसो नेषि च पर्षि चात्यंहः कृधी नो राय उशिजो यविष्ठ ॥
3.15.e: Bull, who beholdest men, through many mornings, among the dark ones shine forth red, O Agni.  Lead us, good Lord, and bear us over trouble: Help us who long, Most Youthful God, to riches.

3.15.d: अषाळ्हो अग्ने वृषभो दिदीहि पुरो विश्वाः सौभगा संजिगीवान् । यज्ञस्य नेता प्रथमस्य पायोर्जातवेदो बृहतः सुप्रणीते ॥
3.15.e: Shine forth, a Bull invincible, O Agni, winning by conquest all the forts and treasures,  Thou Jātavedas who art skilled in guiding, the chief high saving sacrifice's Leader.

3.15.d: अच्छिद्रा शर्म जरितः पुरूणि देवाँ अच्छा दीद्यानः सुमेधाः । रथो न सस्निरभि वक्षि वाजमग्ने त्वं रोदसी नः सुमेके ॥
3.15.e: Lighting Gods hither, Agni, wisest Singer, bring thou to us many and flawless shelters.  Bring vigour, like a car that gathers booty: bring us, O Agni, beauteous Earth and Heaven.

3.15.d: प्र पीपय वृषभ जिन्व वाजानग्ने त्वं रोदसी नः सुदोघे । देवेभिर्देव सुरुचा रुचानो मा नो मर्तस्य दुर्मतिः परि ष्ठात् ॥
3.15.e: Swell, O thou Bull and give those powers an impulse, e’en Earth and Heaven who yield their milk in plenty,  Shining, O God, with Gods in clear effulgence. Let not a mortal's evil will obstruct us.

3.15.d: इळामग्ने पुरुदंसं सनिं गोः शश्वत्तमं हवमानाय साध । स्यान्नः सूनुस्तनयो विजावाग्ने सा ते सुमतिर्भूत्वस्मे ॥
3.15.e: Agni, as holy food to thine invoker, give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels.  To us be born a son and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-ward.

3.16.d: अयमग्निः सुवीर्यस्येशे महः सौभगस्य । राय ईशे स्वपत्यस्य गोमत ईशे वृत्रहथानाम् ॥
3.16.e: THIS Agni is the Lord of great felicity and hero Strength;  Lord of wealth in herds of kine; Lord of the battles with the foe.

3.16.d: इमं नरो मरुतः सश्चता वृधं यस्मिन्रायः शेवृधासः । अभि ये सन्ति पृतनासु दूढ्यो विश्वाहा शत्रुमादभुः ॥
3.16.e: Wait, Maruts, Heroes, upon him the Prosperer in whom is bliss-increasing wealth;  Who in fights ever conquer evil-hearted men, who overcome the enemy.

3.16.d: स त्वं नो रायः शिशीहि मीढ्वो अग्ने सुवीर्यस्य । तुविद्युम्न वर्षिष्ठस्य प्रजावतोऽनमीवस्य शुष्मिणः ॥
3.16.e: As such, O Agni, deal us wealth and hero might, O Bounteous One!  Most lofty, very glorious, rich in progeny, free from disease and full of power.

3.16.d: चक्रिर्यो विश्वा भुवनाभि सासहिश्चक्रिर्देवेष्वा दुवः । आ देवेषु यतत आ सुवीर्य आ शंस उत नृणाम् ॥
3.16.e: He who made all that lives, who passes all in might, who orders service to the Gods,  He works among the Gods, he works in hero strength, yea, also in the praise of men.

3.16.d: मा नो अग्नेऽमतये मावीरतायै रीरधः । मागोतायै सहसस्पुत्र मा निदेऽप द्वेषांस्या कृधि ॥
3.16.e: Give us not up to indigence, Agni, nor want of hero sons,  Nor, Son of Strength, to lack of cattle, nor to blame. Drive. thou our enemies away.

3.16.d: शग्धि वाजस्य सुभग प्रजावतोऽग्ने बृहतो अध्वरे । सं राया भूयसा सृज मयोभुना तुविद्युम्न यशस्वता ॥
3.16.e: Help us to strength, blest Agni! rich in progeny, abundant, in our sacrifice.  Flood us with riches yet more plenteous, bringing weal, with high renown, most Glorious One!

3.17.d: समिध्यमानः प्रथमानु धर्मा समक्तुभिरज्यते विश्ववारः । शोचिष्केशो घृतनिर्णिक्पावकः सुयज्ञो अग्निर्यजथाय देवान् ॥
3.17.e: DULY enkindled after ancient customs, bringing all treasures, he is balmed with unguents,—  Flame-haired, oil-clad, the purifying Agni, skilled in fair rites, to bring the Gods for worship.

3.17.d: यथायजो होत्रमग्ने पृथिव्या यथा दिवो जातवेदश्चिकित्वान् । एवानेन हविषा यक्षि देवान्मनुष्वद्यज्ञं प्र तिरेममद्य ॥
3.17.e: As thou, O Agni, skilful Jātavedas, hast sacrificed as Priest of Earth, of Heaven,  So with this offering bring the Gods, and prosper this sacrifice today as erst for Manu.

3.17.d: त्रीण्यायूंषि तव जातवेदस्तिस्र आजानीरुषसस्ते अग्ने । ताभिर्देवानामवो यक्षि विद्वानथा भव यजमानाय शं योः ॥
3.17.e: Three are thy times of life, O Jātavedas, and the three mornings are thy births, O Agni.  With these, well-knowing, grant the Gods’ kind favour, and help in stir and stress the man who worships.

3.17.d: अग्निं सुदीतिं सुदृशं गृणन्तो नमस्यामस्त्वेड्यं जातवेदः । त्वां दूतमरतिं हव्यवाहं देवा अकृण्वन्नमृतस्य नाभिम् ॥
3.17.e: Agni most bright and fair with song we honour, yea, the adorable, O Jātavedas.  Thee, envoy, messenger, oblation-bearer, the Gods have made centre of life eternal.

3.17.d: यस्त्वद्धोता पूर्वो अग्ने यजीयान्द्विता च सत्ता स्वधया च शम्भुः । तस्यानु धर्म प्र यजा चिकित्वोऽथा नो धा अध्वरं देववीतौ ॥
3.17.e: That Priest before thee, yet more skilled in worship, stablished of old, health-giver by his nature,—  After his custom offer, thou who knowest, and lay our sacrifice where Gods may taste it.

3.18.d: भवा नो अग्ने सुमना उपेतौ सखेव सख्ये पितरेव साधुः । पुरुद्रुहो हि क्षितयो जनानां प्रति प्रतीचीर्दहतादरातीः ॥
3.18.e: AGNI, be kind to us when we approach thee good as a friend to friend, as sire and mother.  The races of mankind are great oppressors burn up malignity that strives against us.

3.18.d: तपो ष्वग्ने अन्तराँ अमित्रान्तपा शंसमररुषः परस्य । तपो वसो चिकितानो अचित्तान्वि ते तिष्ठन्तामजरा अयासः ॥
3.18.e: Agni, burn up the unfriendly who are near us, burn thou the foeman's curse who pays no worship.  Burn, Vasu, thou who markest well, the foolish: let thine eternal nimble beams surround thee.

3.18.d: इध्मेनाग्न इच्छमानो घृतेन जुहोमि हव्यं तरसे बलाय । यावदीशे ब्रह्मणा वन्दमान इमां धियं शतसेयाय देवीम् ॥
3.18.e: With fuel, Agni, and with oil, desirous, mine offering I present for strength and conquest,  With prayer, so far as I have power, adoring-this hymn divine to gain a hundred treasures.

3.18.d: उच्छोचिषा सहसस्पुत्र स्तुतो बृहद्वयः शशमानेषु धेहि । रेवदग्ने विश्वामित्रेषु शं योर्मर्मृज्मा ते तन्वं१ भूरि कृत्वः ॥
3.18.e: Give with thy glow, thou Son of Strength, when lauded, great vital power to those who toil to serve thee.  Give richly, Agni, to the Viśvāmitras in rest and stir. Oft have we decked thy body.

3.18.d: कृधि रत्नं सुसनितर्धनानां स घेदग्ने भवसि यत्समिद्धः । स्तोतुर्दुरोणे सुभगस्य रेवत्सृप्रा करस्ना दधिषे वपूंषि ॥
3.18.e: Give us, O liberal Lord, great store of riches, for, Agni, such art thou when duly kindled.  Thou in the happy singer's home bestowest, amply with arms extended, things of beauty.

3.19.d: अग्निं होतारं प्र वृणे मियेधे गृत्सं कविं विश्वविदममूरम् । स नो यक्षद्देवताता यजीयान्राये वाजाय वनते मघानि ॥
3.19.e: AGNI, quick, sage, infallible, all-knowing, I choose to be our Priest at this oblation.  In our Gods’ service he, best skilled, shall worship: may he obtain us boons for strength and riches.

3.19.d: प्र ते अग्ने हविष्मतीमियर्म्यच्छा सुद्युम्नां रातिनीं घृताचीम् । प्रदक्षिणिद्देवतातिमुराणः सं रातिभिर्वसुभिर्यज्ञमश्रेत् ॥
3.19.e: Agni, to thee I lift the oil-fed ladle, bright, with an offering, bearing our oblation.  From the right hand, choosing the Gods’ attendance, he with rich presents hath arranged the worship.

3.19.d: स तेजीयसा मनसा त्वोत उत शिक्ष स्वपत्यस्य शिक्षोः । अग्ने रायो नृतमस्य प्रभूतौ भूयाम ते सुष्टुतयश्च वस्वः ॥
3.19.e: Of keenest spirit is the man thou aidest give us good offspring, thou who givest freely.  In power of wealth most rich in men. O Agni, of thee, the Good, may we sing forth fair praises.

3.19.d: भूरीणि हि त्वे दधिरे अनीकाग्ने देवस्य यज्यवो जनासः । स आ वह देवतातिं यविष्ठ शर्धो यदद्य दिव्यं यजासि ॥
3.19.e: Men as they worship thee the God, O Agni, have set on thee full many a brilliant, aspect.  So bring Most Youthful One, the Gods’ assembly, the Heavenly Host which thou to-day shalt honour.

3.19.d: यत्त्वा होतारमनजन्मियेधे निषादयन्तो यजथाय देवाः । स त्वं नो अग्नेऽवितेह बोध्यधि श्रवांसि धेहि नस्तनूषु ॥
3.19.e: When Gods anoint thee Priest at their oblation, and seat thee for thy task as Sacrificer,  O Agni, be thou here our kind defender, and to ourselves vouchsafe the gift of glory.

3.20.d: अग्निमुषसमश्विना दधिक्रां व्युष्टिषु हवते वह्निरुक्थैः । सुज्योतिषो नः शृण्वन्तु देवाः सजोषसो अध्वरं वावशानाः ॥
3.20.e: WITH lauds at break of morn the priest invoketh Agni, Dawn, Dadhikrās, and both the Aśvins.  With one consent the Gods whose light is splendid, longing to taste our sacrifice, shall hear us.

3.20.d: अग्ने त्री ते वाजिना त्री षधस्था तिस्रस्ते जिह्वा ऋतजात पूर्वीः । तिस्र उ ते तन्वो देववातास्ताभिर्नः पाहि गिरो अप्रयुच्छन् ॥
3.20.e: Three are thy powers, O Agni, three thy stations, three are thy tongues, yea, many, Child of Order!  Three bodies hast thou which the Gods delight in: with these protect our hymns with care unceasing.

3.20.d: अग्ने भूरीणि तव जातवेदो देव स्वधावोऽमृतस्य नाम । याश्च माया मायिनां विश्वमिन्व त्वे पूर्वीः संदधुः पृष्टबन्धो ॥
3.20.e: O Agni, many are the names thou bearest, immortal, God, Divine, and Jātavedas.  And many charms of charmers, All-Inspirer! have they laid in thee, Lord of true attendants!

3.20.d: अग्निर्नेता भग इव क्षितीनां दैवीनां देव ऋतुपा ऋतावा । स वृत्रहा सनयो विश्ववेदाः पर्षद्विश्वाति दुरिता गृणन्तम् ॥
3.20.e: Agni, like Bhaga, leads the godly people, he who is true to Law and guards the seasons.  Ancient, all-knowing, he the Vṛtra-slayer shall bear the singer safe through every trouble.

3.20.d: दधिक्रामग्निमुषसं च देवीं बृहस्पतिं सवितारं च देवम् । अश्विना मित्रावरुणा भगं च वसून्रुद्राँ आदित्याँ इह हुवे ॥
3.20.e: I call on Savitar the God, on Morning, Bṛhaspati, and Dadhikrās, and Agni,  On Varuṇa and Mitra, on the Aśvins, Bhaga, the Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas.

3.21.d: इमं नो यज्ञममृतेषु धेहीमा हव्या जातवेदो जुषस्व । स्तोकानामग्ने मेदसो घृतस्य होतः प्राशान प्रथमो निषद्य ॥
3.21.e: SET this our sacrifice among the Immortals: be pleased with these our presents, Jātavedas.  O Priest, O Agni, sit thee down before us, and first enjoy the drops of oil and fatness.

3.21.d: घृतवन्तः पावक ते स्तोकाः श्चोतन्ति मेदसः । स्वधर्मन्देववीतये श्रेष्ठं नो धेहि वार्यम् ॥
3.21.e: For thee, O Purifier, flow the drops of fatness rich in oil.  After thy wont vouchsafe to us the choicest boon that Gods may feast.

3.21.d: तुभ्यं स्तोका घृतश्चुतोऽग्ने विप्राय सन्त्य । ऋषिः श्रेष्ठः समिध्यसे यज्ञस्य प्राविता भव ॥
3.21.e: Agni, Most Excellent! for thee the Sage are drops that drip with oil.  Thou art enkindled as the best of Seers. Help thou the sacrifice.

3.21.d: तुभ्यं श्चोतन्त्यध्रिगो शचीवः स्तोकासो अग्ने मेदसो घृतस्य । कविशस्तो बृहता भानुनागा हव्या जुषस्व मेधिर ॥
3.21.e: To thee, O Agni, mighty and resistless, to thee stream forth the drops of oil and fatness.  With great light art thou come, O praised by poets! Accept our offering, O thou Sage.

3.21.d: ओजिष्ठं ते मध्यतो मेद उद्भृतं प्र ते वयं ददामहे । श्चोतन्ति ते वसो स्तोका अधि त्वचि प्रति तान्देवशो विहि ॥
3.21.e: Fatness exceeding rich, extracted from the midst,—this as our gift we offer thee.  Excellent God, the drops run down upon thy skin. Deal them to each among the Gods.

3.22.d: अयं सो अग्निर्यस्मिन्त्सोममिन्द्रः सुतं दधे जठरे वावशानः । सहस्रिणं वाजमत्यं न सप्तिं ससवान्त्सन्त्स्तूयसे जातवेदः ॥
3.22.e: THIS is that Agni whence the longing Indra took the pressed Soma deep within his body.  Winner of spoils in thousands, like a courser, with praise art thou exalted, Jātavedas.

3.22.d: अग्ने यत्ते दिवि वर्चः पृथिव्यां यदोषधीष्वप्स्वा यजत्र । येनान्तरिक्षमुर्वाततन्थ त्वेषः स भानुरर्णवो नृचक्षाः ॥
3.22.e: That light of thine in heaven and earth, O Agni, in plants, O Holy One, and in the waters,  Wherewith thou hast spread wide the air's mid-region-bright is that splendour, wavy, man-beholding.

3.22.d: अग्ने दिवो अर्णमच्छा जिगास्यच्छा देवाँ ऊचिषे धिष्ण्या ये । या रोचने परस्तात्सूर्यस्य याश्चावस्तादुपतिष्ठन्त आपः ॥
3.22.e: O Agni, to the sea of heaven thou goest: thou hast called hither Gods beheld in spirit.  The waters, too, come hither, those up yonder in the Sun's realm of light, and those beneath it.

3.22.d: पुरीष्यासो अग्नयः प्रावणेभिः सजोषसः । जुषन्तां यज्ञमद्रुहोऽनमीवा इषो महीः ॥
3.22.e: Let fires that dwell in mist, combined with those that have their home in floods,  Guileless accept our sacrifice, great viands free from all disease.

3.22.d: इळामग्ने पुरुदंसं सनिं गोः शश्वत्तमं हवमानाय साध । स्यान्नः सूनुस्तनयो विजावाग्ने सा ते सुमतिर्भूत्वस्मे ॥
3.22.e: Agni, as holy food to thine invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels.  To us be born a son and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-ward.

3.23.d: निर्मथितः सुधित आ सधस्थे युवा कविरध्वरस्य प्रणेता । जूर्यत्स्वग्निरजरो वनेष्वत्रा दधे अमृतं जातवेदाः ॥
3.23.e: RUBBED into life, well stablished in the dwelling, Leader of sacrifice, the Sage, the youthful,  Here in the wasting fuel Jātavedas, eternal, hath assumed immortal being.

3.23.d: अमन्थिष्टां भारता रेवदग्निं देवश्रवा देववातः सुदक्षम् । अग्ने वि पश्य बृहताभि रायेषां नो नेता भवतादनु द्यून् ॥
3.23.e: Both Bharatas, Devaśravas, Devāvata, have strongly rubbed to life effectual Agni.  O Agni, look thou forth with ample riches: be, every day, bearer of food to feed us.

3.23.d: दश क्षिपः पूर्व्यं सीमजीजनन्त्सुजातं मातृषु प्रियम् । अग्निं स्तुहि दैववातं देवश्रवो यो जनानामसद्वशी ॥
3.23.e: Him nobly born of old the fingers ten produced, him whom his Mothers counted dear.  Praise Devāvata's Agni, thou Devaśravas, him who shall be the people's Lord.

3.23.d: नि त्वा दधे वर आ पृथिव्या इळायास्पदे सुदिनत्वे अह्नाम् । दृषद्वत्यां मानुष आपयायां सरस्वत्यां रेवदग्ने दिदीहि ॥
3.23.e: He set thee in the earth's most lovely station, in Iḷā's place, in days of fair bright weather.  On man, on Āpayā, Agni! on the rivers Dṛṣadvati, Sarasvatī, shine richly.

3.23.d: इळामग्ने पुरुदंसं सनिं गोः शश्वत्तमं हवमानाय साध । स्यान्नः सूनुस्तनयो विजावाग्ने सा ते सुमतिर्भूत्वस्मे ॥
3.23.e: Agni, as holy food to thine invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels.  To us be born a son and spreading offspring Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-ward

3.24.d: अग्ने सहस्व पृतना अभिमातीरपास्य । दुष्टरस्तरन्नरातीर्वर्चो धा यज्ञवाहसे ॥
3.24.e: AGNI, subdue opposing bands, and drive our enemies away.  Invincible, slay godless foes: give splendour to the worshipper.

3.24.d: अग्न इळा समिध्यसे वीतिहोत्रो अमर्त्यः । जुषस्व सू नो अध्वरम् ॥
3.24.e: Lit with libation, Agni, thou, deathless, who callest Gods to feast,  Accept our sacrifice with joy.

3.24.d: अग्ने द्युम्नेन जागृवे सहसः सूनवाहुत । एदं बर्हिः सदो मम ॥
3.24.e: With splendour, Agni, Son of Strength, thou who art worshipped, wakeful One.  Seat thee on this my sacred grass.

3.24.d: अग्ने विश्वेभिरग्निभिर्देवेभिर्महया गिरः । यज्ञेषु य उ चायवः ॥
3.24.e: With all thy fires, with all the Gods, Agni, exalt the songs we sing.  And living men in holy rites.

3.24.d: अग्ने दा दाशुषे रयिं वीरवन्तं परीणसम् । शिशीहि नः सूनुमतः ॥
3.24.e: Grant, Agni, to the worshipper wealth rich in heroes, plenteous store,  Make thou us rich with many sons.

3.25.d: अग्ने दिवः सूनुरसि प्रचेतास्तना पृथिव्या उत विश्ववेदाः । ऋधग्देवाँ इह यजा चिकित्वः ॥
3.25.e: THOU art the sapient Son of Dyaus, O Agni, yes and the Child of Earth, who knowest all things.  Bring the Gods specially, thou Sage, for worship.

3.25.d: अग्निः सनोति वीर्याणि विद्वान्त्सनोति वाजममृताय भूषन् । स नो देवाँ एह वहा पुरुक्षो ॥
3.25.e: Agni the wise bestows the might of heroes grants strengthening food, preparing it for nectar.  Thou who art rich in food bring the Gods hither.

3.25.d: अग्निर्द्यावापृथिवी विश्वजन्ये आ भाति देवी अमृते अमूरः । क्षयन्वाजैः पुरुश्चन्द्रो नमोभिः ॥
3.25.e: Agni, infallible, lights Earth and Heaven, immortal Goddesses gracious to all men,—  Lord through his strength, splendid through adorations.

3.25.d: अग्न इन्द्रश्च दाशुषो दुरोणे सुतावतो यज्ञमिहोप यातम् । अमर्धन्ता सोमपेयाय देवा ॥
3.25.e: Come to the sacrifice, Agni and Indra come to the offerer's house who hath the Soma.  Come, friendly-minded, Gods, to drink the Soma.

3.25.d: अग्ने अपां समिध्यसे दुरोणे नित्यः सूनो सहसो जातवेदः । सधस्थानि महयमान ऊती ॥
3.25.e: In the floods' home art thou enkindled, Agni, O Jātavedas, Son of Strength, eternal,  Exalting with thine help the gathering-places.

3.26.d: वैश्वानरं मनसाग्निं निचाय्या हविष्मन्तो अनुषत्यं स्वर्विदम् । सुदानुं देवं रथिरं वसूयवो गीर्भी रण्वं कुशिकासो हवामहे ॥
3.26.e: REVERING in our heart Agni Vaiśvānara, the finder of the light, whose promises are true,  The liberal, gladsome, car-borne God we Kuśikas invoke him with oblation, seeking wealth with songs.

3.26.d: तं शुभ्रमग्निमवसे हवामहे वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वानमुक्थ्यम् । बृहस्पतिं मनुषो देवतातये विप्रं श्रोतारमतिथिं रघुष्यदम् ॥
3.26.e: That Agni, bright, Vaiśvānara, we invoke for help, and Mātariśvan worthy of the song of praise;  Bṛhaspati for man's observance of the Gods, the Singer prompt to hear, the swiftly-moving guest.

3.26.d: अश्वो न क्रन्दञ्जनिभिः समिध्यते वैश्वानरः कुशिकेभिर्युगेयुगे । स नो अग्निः सुवीर्यं स्वश्व्यं दधातु रत्नममृतेषु जागृविः ॥
3.26.e: Age after age Vaiśvānara, neighing like a horse, is kindled with the women by the Kuśikas.  May Agni, he who wakes among Immortal Gods, grant us heroic strength and wealth in noble steeds.

3.26.d: प्र यन्तु वाजास्तविषीभिरग्नयः शुभे सम्मिश्लाः पृषतीरयुक्षत । बृहदुक्षो मरुतो विश्ववेदसः प्र वेपयन्ति पर्वताँ अदाभ्याः ॥
3.26.e: Let them go forth, the strong, as flames of fire with might. Gathered for victory they have yoked their spotted deer.  Pourers of floods, the Maruts, Masters of all wealth, they who can ne’er be conquered, make the mountains shake.

3.26.d: अग्निश्रियो मरुतो विश्वकृष्टय आ त्वेषमुग्रमव ईमहे वयम् । ते स्वानिनो रुद्रिया वर्षनिर्णिजः सिंहा न हेषक्रतवः सुदानवः ॥
3.26.e: The Maruts, Friends of men, are glorious as the fire: their mighty and resplendent succour we implore.  Those storming Sons of Rudra clothed in robes of rain, boon-givers of good gifts, roar as the lions roar.

3.26.d: व्रातंव्रातं गणंगणं सुशस्तिभिरग्नेर्भामं मरुतामोज ईमहे । पृषदश्वासो अनवभ्रराधसो गन्तारो यज्ञं विदथेषु धीराः ॥
3.26.e: We, band on band and troop following troop, entreat with fair lauds Agni's splendour and the Maruts’ might,  With spotted deer for steeds, with wealth that never fails, they, wise Ones, come to sacrifice at our gatherings.

3.26.d: अग्निरस्मि जन्मना जातवेदा घृतं मे चक्षुरमृतं म आसन् । अर्कस्त्रिधातू रजसो विमानोऽजस्रो घर्मो हविरस्मि नाम ॥
3.26.e: Agni am I who know, by birth, all creatures. Mine eye is butter, in my mouth is nectar.  I am light threefold, measurer of the region exhaustless heat am I, named burnt-oblation.

3.26.d: त्रिभिः पवित्रैरपुपोद्ध्य१र्कं हृदा मतिं ज्योतिरनु प्रजानन् । वर्षिष्ठं रत्नमकृत स्वधाभिरादिद्द्यावापृथिवी पर्यपश्यत् ॥
3.26.e: Bearing in mind a thought with light accordant, he purified the Sun with three refinings;  By his own nature gained the highest treasure, and looked abroad over the earth and heaven.

3.26.d: शतधारमुत्समक्षीयमाणं विपश्चितं पितरं वक्त्वानाम् । मेळिं मदन्तं पित्रोरुपस्थे तं रोदसी पिपृतं सत्यवाचम् ॥
3.26.e: The Spring that fails not with a hundred streamlets, Father inspired of prayers that men should utter,  The Sparkler, joyous in his Parents' bosorn, -him, the Truth-speaker, sate ye, Earth and Heaven.

3.27.d: प्र वो वाजा अभिद्यवो हविष्मन्तो घृताच्या । देवाञ्जिगाति सुम्नयुः ॥
3.27.e: IN ladle dropping oil your food goes in oblation up to heaven,  Goes to the Gods in search of bliss.

3.27.d: ईळे अग्निं विपश्चितं गिरा यज्ञस्य साधनम् । श्रुष्टीवानं धितावानम् ॥
3.27.e: Agni I laud, the Sage inspired, crowner of sacrifice through song,  Who listens and gives bounteous gifts.

3.27.d: अग्ने शकेम ते वयं यमं देवस्य वाजिनः । अति द्वेषांसि तरेम ॥
3.27.e: O Agni, if we might obtain control of thee the potent God,  Then should we overcome our foes.
Kindled at sacrifices he is Agni, hallower, meet for praise,  With flame for hair: to him we seek.
Immortal Agni, shining far, enrobed with oil, well worshipped, bears  The gifts of sacrifice away.

3.27.d: तं सबाधो यतस्रुच इत्था धिया यज्ञवन्तः । आ चक्रुरग्निमूतये ॥
3.27.e: The priests with ladles lifted up, worshipping here with holy thought,  Have brought this Agni for our aid.

3.27.d: होता देवो अमर्त्यः पुरस्तादेति मायया । विदथानि प्रचोदयन् ॥
3.27.e: Immortal, Sacrificer, God, with wondrous power he leads the way,  Urging the great assembly on.

3.27.d: वाजी वाजेषु धीयतेऽध्वरेषु प्र णीयते । विप्रो यज्ञस्य साधनः ॥
3.27.e: Strong, he is set on deeds ofstrength. In sacrifices led in front,  As Singer he completes the rite.

3.27.d: धिया चक्रे वरेण्यो भूतानां गर्भमा दधे । दक्षस्य पितरं तना ॥
3.27.e: Excellent, he was made by thought. The Germ of beings have I gained,  Yea, and die Sire of active strength.

3.27.d: नि त्वा दधे वरेण्यं दक्षस्येळा सहस्कृत । अग्ने सुदीतिमुशिजम् ॥
3.27.e: Thee have I stablished, Excellent, O strengthened by the sage's prayer,  Thee, Agni, longing, nobly bright.

3.27.d: अग्निं यन्तुरमप्तुरमृतस्य योगे वनुषः । विप्रा वाजैः समिन्धते ॥
3.27.e: Agni, the swift and active One, singers, at time of sacrifice,  Eagerly kindle with their food.

3.27.d: ऊर्जो नपातमध्वरे दीदिवांसमुप द्यवि । अग्निमीळे कविक्रतुम् ॥
3.27.e: Agni the Son of Strength who shines up to the heaven in solemn rites,  The wise of heart, I glorify.
Meet to be lauded and adored, showing in beauty through the dark,  Agni, the Strong, is kindled well.

3.27.d: वृषो अग्निः समिध्यतेऽश्वो न देववाहनः । तं हविष्मन्त ईळते ॥
3.27.e: Agni is kindled as a bull, like a horsebearer of the Gods:  Men with oblations worship him.

3.27.d: वृषणं त्वा वयं वृषन्वृषणः समिधीमहि । अग्ने दीद्यतं बृहत् ॥
3.27.e: Thee will we kindle as a bull, we who are Bulls ourselves, O Bull.  Thee, Agni, shining mightily.

3.28.d: अग्ने जुषस्व नो हविः पुरोळाशं जातवेदः । प्रातःसावे धियावसो ॥
3.28.e: AGNI who knowest all, accept our offering and the cake of meal,  At dawn's libation, rich in prayer!

3.28.d: पुरोळा अग्ने पचतस्तुभ्यं वा घा परिष्कृतः । तं जुषस्व यविष्ठ्य ॥
3.28.e: Agni, the sacrificial cake hath been prepared and dressed for thee:  Accept it, O Most Youthful God.

3.28.d: अग्ने वीहि पुरोळाशमाहुतं तिरोअह्न्यम् । सहसः सूनुरस्यध्वरे हितः ॥
3.28.e: Agni, enjoy the cake of meal and our oblation three days old:  Thou, Son of Strength, art stablished at our sacrifice.

3.28.d: माध्यंदिने सवने जातवेदः पुरोळाशमिह कवे जुषस्व । अग्ने यह्वस्य तव भागधेयं न प्र मिनन्ति विदथेषु धीराः ॥
3.28.e: Here at the midday sacrifice enjoy thou the sacrificial cake, wise, Jātavedas!  Agni, the sages in assemblies never minish the portion due to thee the Mighty.

3.28.d: अग्ने तृतीये सवने हि कानिषः पुरोळाशं सहसः सूनवाहुतम् । अथा देवेष्वध्वरं विपन्यया धा रत्नवन्तममृतेषु जागृविम् ॥
3.28.e: O Agni, at the third libation takewith joy the offered cake of sacrifice, thou, Son of Strength.  Through skill in song bear to the Gods our sacrifice, watchful and fraught with riches, to Immortal God.

3.28.d: अग्ने वृधान आहुतिं पुरोळाशं जातवेदः । जुषस्व तिरोअह्न्यम् ॥
3.28.e: O waxing Agni, knower, thou, of all, accept our gifts, the cake,  And that prepared ere yesterday.

3.29.d: अस्तीदमधिमन्थनमस्ति प्रजननं कृतम् । एतां विश्पत्नीमा भराग्निं मन्थाम पूर्वथा ॥
3.29.e: HERE is the gear for friction, here tinder made ready for the spark.  Bring thou the Matron: we will rub Agni in ancient fashion forth.

3.29.d: अरण्योर्निहितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुधितो गर्भिणीषु । दिवेदिव ईड्यो जागृवद्भिर्हविष्मद्भिर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः ॥
3.29.e: 1n the two fire-sticks Jātavedas lieth, even as the well-set germ in pregnant women,  Agni who day by day must be exalted by men who watch and worship with oblations.

3.29.d: उत्तानायामव भरा चिकित्वान्त्सद्यः प्रवीता वृषणं जजान । अरुषस्तूपो रुशदस्य पाज इळायास्पुत्रो वयुनेऽजनिष्ट ॥
3.29.e: Lay this with care on that which lies extended: straight hath she borne the Steer when made prolific.  With his red pillar—radiant is his splendour—in our skilled task is born the Son of Iḷā.

3.29.d: इळायास्त्वा पदे वयं नाभा पृथिव्या अधि । जातवेदो नि धीमह्यग्ने हव्याय वोळ्हवे ॥
3.29.e: In Iḷā's place we set thee down, upon the central point of earth,  That, Agni Jātavedas, thou mayst bear our offerings to the Gods.

3.29.d: मन्थता नरः कविमद्वयन्तं प्रचेतसममृतं सुप्रतीकम् । यज्ञस्य केतुं प्रथमं पुरस्तादग्निं नरो जनयता सुशेवम् ॥
3.29.e: Rub into life, ye men, the Sage, the guileless, Immortal, very wise and fair to look on.  O men, bring forth the most propitious Agni, first ensign of the sacrifice to eastward.

3.29.d: यदी मन्थन्ति बाहुभिर्वि रोचतेऽश्वो न वाज्यरुषो वनेष्वा । चित्रो न यामन्नश्विनोरनिवृतः परि वृणक्त्यश्मनस्तृणा दहन् ॥
3.29.e: When with their arms they rub him straight he shineth forth like a strong courser, red in colour, in the wood.  Bright, checkless, as it were upon the Aśvins' path, he passeth by the stones and burneth up the grass.

3.29.d: जातो अग्नी रोचते चेकितानो वाजी विप्रः कविशस्तः सुदानुः । यं देवास ईड्यं विश्वविदं हव्यवाहमदधुरध्वरेषु ॥
3.29.e: Agni shines forth when born, observant, mighty, the bountiful, the Singer praised by sages;  Whom, as adorable and knowing all things, Gods set at solemn rites as offering-bearer.

3.29.d: सीद होतः स्व उ लोके चिकित्वान्त्सादया यज्ञं सुकृतस्य योनौ । देवावीर्देवान्हविषा यजास्यग्ने बृहद्यजमाने वयो धाः ॥
3.29.e: Set thee, O Priest, in, thine own place, observant: lay down the sacrifice in the home of worship.  Thou, dear to Gods, shalt serve them with oblation: Agni, give long life to the sacrificer.

3.29.d: कृणोत धूमं वृषणं सखायोऽस्रेधन्त इतन वाजमच्छ । अयमग्निः पृतनाषाट् सुवीरो येन देवासो असहन्त दस्यून् ॥
3.29.e: Raise ye a mighty smoke, my fellow-workers! Ye shall attain to wealth without obstruction.  This Agni is the battle-winning Hero by whom the Gods have overcome the Dasyus.

3.29.d: अयं ते योनिर्ऋत्वियो यतो जातो अरोचथाः । तं जानन्नग्न आ सीदाथा नो वर्धया गिरः ॥
3.29.e: This is thine ordered place of birth whence sprung to life thou shonest forth.  Knowing this, Agni, sit thee down, and prosper thou the songs we sing.

3.29.d: तनूनपादुच्यते गर्भ आसुरो नराशंसो भवति यद्विजायते । मातरिश्वा यदमिमीत मातरि वातस्य सर्गो अभवत्सरीमणि ॥
3.29.e: As Germ Celestial he is called Tanūnapāt, and Narāśaṁsa born diffused in varied shape.  Formed in his Mother he is Mātariśvan; he hath, in his course, become the rapid flight of wind.

3.29.d: सुनिर्मथा निर्मथितः सुनिधा निहितः कविः । अग्ने स्वध्वरा कृणु देवान्देवयते यज ॥
3.29.e: With strong attrition rubbed to life, laid down with careful hand, a Sage,  Agni, make sacrifices good, and for the pious bring the Gods.

3.29.d: अजीजनन्नमृतं मर्त्यासोऽस्रेमाणं तरणिं वीळुजम्भम् । दश स्वसारो अग्रुवः समीचीः पुमांसं जातमभि सं रभन्ते ॥
3.29.e: Mortals have brought to life the God Immortal, the Conqueror with mighty jaws, unfailing.  The sisters ten, unwedded and united, together grasp the Babe, the new-born Infant.

3.29.d: प्र सप्तहोता सनकादरोचत मातुरुपस्थे यदशोचदूधनि । न नि मिषति सुरणो दिवेदिवे यदसुरस्य जठरादजायत ॥
3.29.e: Served by the seven priests, he shone forth from ancient time, when in his Mother's bosom, in her lap, he glowed.  Giving delight each day he closeth not his eye, since from the Asura's body hewas brought to life.

3.29.d: अमित्रायुधो मरुतामिव प्रयाः प्रथमजा ब्रह्मणो विश्वमिद्विदुः । द्युम्नवद्ब्रह्म कुशिकास एरिर एकएको दमे अग्निं समीधिरे ॥
3.29.e: Even as the Maruts, onslaughts who attack the foe, those born the first of all knew the full power of prayer.  The Kuśikas have made the glorious hymn ascend, and, each one singly in his home, have kindled fire.

3.29.d: यदद्य त्वा प्रयति यज्ञे अस्मिन्होतश्चिकित्वोऽवृणीमहीह । ध्रुवमया ध्रुवमुताशमिष्ठाः प्रजानन्विद्वाँ उप याहि सोमम् ॥
3.29.e: As we, O Priest observant, have elected thee this day, what time the solemn sacrifice began,  So surely hast thou worshipped, surely hast thou toiled: come thou unto the Soma, wise and knowing all.

3.30.d: इच्छन्ति त्वा सोम्यासः सखायः सुन्वन्ति सोमं दधति प्रयांसि । तितिक्षन्ते अभिशस्तिं जनानामिन्द्र त्वदा कश्चन हि प्रकेतः ॥
3.30.e: THE friends who offer Soma long to find thee: they pour forth Soma and present their viands.  They bear unmoved the cursing of the people, for all our wisdom comes from thee, O Indra.

3.30.d: न ते दूरे परमा चिद्रजांस्या तु प्र याहि हरिवो हरिभ्याम् । स्थिराय वृष्णे सवना कृतेमा युक्ता ग्रावाणः समिधाने अग्नौ ॥
3.30.e: Not far for thee are mid-air's loftiest regions: start hither, Lord of Bays, with thy Bay Horses.  Made for the Firm and Strong are these libations. The pressing-stones are set and fire is kindled.

3.30.d: इन्द्रः सुशिप्रो मघवा तरुत्रो महाव्रातस्तुविकूर्मिर्ऋघावान् । यदुग्रो धा बाधितो मर्त्येषु क्व१ त्या ते वृषभ वीर्याणि ॥
3.30.e: Fair cheeks hath Indra, Maghavan, the Victor, Lord of a great host, Stormer, strong in action.  What once thou didst in might when mortals vexed thee,—where now, O Bull, are those thy hero exploits?

3.30.d: त्वं हि ष्मा च्यावयन्नच्युतान्येको वृत्रा चरसि जिघ्नमानः । तव द्यावापृथिवी पर्वतासोऽनु व्रताय निमितेव तस्थुः ॥
3.30.e: For, overthrowing what hath ne’er been shaken, thou goest forth alone destroying Vṛtras.  For him who followeth thy Law the mountains and heaven and earth stand as if firmly stablished.

3.30.d: उताभये पुरुहूत श्रवोभिरेको दृळ्हमवदो वृत्रहा सन् । इमे चिदिन्द्र रोदसी अपारे यत्संगृभ्णा मघवन्काशिरित्ते ॥
3.30.e: Yea, Much-invoked! in safety through thy glories alone thou speakest truth as Vṛtra's slayer.  E’en these two boundless worlds to thee, O Indra, what time thou graspest them, are but a handful.

3.30.d: प्र सू त इन्द्र प्रवता हरिभ्यां प्र ते वज्रः प्रमृणन्नेतु शत्रून् । जहि प्रतीचो अनूचः पराचो विश्वं सत्यं कृणुहि विष्टमस्तु ॥
3.30.e: Forthwith thy Bay steeds down the steep, O Indra, forth, crushing foemen, go thy bolt of thunder!  Slay those who meet thee, those who flee, who follow: make all thy promise true; be all completed.

3.30.d: यस्मै धायुरदधा मर्त्यायाभक्तं चिद्भजते गेह्यं१ सः । भद्रा त इन्द्र सुमतिर्घृताची सहस्रदाना पुरुहूत रातिः ॥
3.30.e: The man to whom thou givest as Provider enjoys domestic plenty undivided.  Blest, Indra, is thy favour dropping fatness: thy worship, Much-invoked! brings gifts in thousands.

3.30.d: सहदानुं पुरुहूत क्षियन्तमहस्तमिन्द्र सं पिणक्कुणारुम् । अभि वृत्रं वर्धमानं पियारुमपादमिन्द्र तवसा जघन्थ ॥
3.30.e: Thou, Indra, Much-invoked! didst crush to pieces Kunaru handless fiend who dwelt with Danu.  Thou with might, Indra, smotest dead the scorner, the footless Vṛtra as he waxed in vigour.

3.30.d: नि सामनामिषिरामिन्द्र भूमिं महीमपारां सदने ससत्थ । अस्तभ्नाद्द्यां वृषभो अन्तरिक्षमर्षन्त्वापस्त्वयेह प्रसूताः ॥
3.30.e: Thou hast established in her seat, O Indra, the level earth, vast, vigorous, unbounded.  The Bull hath propped the heaven and air's mid-region. By thee sent onward let the floods flow hither.

3.30.d: अलातृणो वल इन्द्र व्रजो गोः पुरा हन्तोर्भयमानो व्यार । सुगान्पथो अकृणोन्निरजे गाः प्रावन्वाणीः पुरुहूतं धमन्तीः ॥
3.30.e: He who withheld the kine, in silence I yielded in fear before thy blow, O Indra.  He made paths easy to drive forth the cattle. Loud-breathing praises helped the Much-invoked One.

3.30.d: एको द्वे वसुमती समीची इन्द्र आ पप्रौ पृथिवीमुत द्याम् । उतान्तरिक्षादभि नः समीक इषो रथीः सयुजः शूर वाजान् ॥
3.30.e: Indra alone filled full the earth and heaven, the Pair who meet together, rich in treasures.  Yea, bring thou near us from the air's mid-region strength, on thy car, and wholesome food, O Hero.

3.30.d: दिशः सूर्यो न मिनाति प्रदिष्टा दिवेदिवे हर्यश्वप्रसूताः । सं यदानळध्वन आदिदश्वैर्विमोचनं कृणुते तत्त्वस्य ॥
3.30.e: Sūrya transgresses not the ordered limits set daily by the Lord of Tawny Coursers.  When to the goal he comes, his journey ended, his Steeds he looses: this is Indra's doing.

3.30.d: दिदृक्षन्त उषसो यामन्नक्तोर्विवस्वत्या महि चित्रमनीकम् । विश्वे जानन्ति महिना यदागादिन्द्रस्य कर्म सुकृता पुरूणि ॥
3.30.e: Men gladly in the course of night would look on the broad bright front of the refulgent Morning;  And all acknowledge, when she comes in glory, the manifold and goodly works of Indra.

3.30.d: महि ज्योतिर्निहितं वक्षणास्वामा पक्वं चरति बिभ्रती गौः । विश्वं स्वाद्म सम्भृतमुस्रियायां यत्सीमिन्द्रो अदधाद्भोजनाय ॥
3.30.e: A mighty splendour rests upon her bosom: bearing ripe milk the Cow, unripe, advances.  All sweetness is collected in the Heifer, sweetness which Indra made for our enjoyment.

3.30.d: इन्द्र दृह्य यामकोशा अभूवन्यज्ञाय शिक्ष गृणते सखिभ्यः । दुर्मायवो दुरेवा मर्त्यासो निषङ्गिणो रिपवो हन्त्वासः ॥
3.30.e: Barring the way they come. Be firm, O Indra; aid friends to sacrifice and him who singeth.  These must be slain by thee, malignant mortals, armed with ill arts, our quiverbearing foemen.

3.30.d: सं घोषः शृण्वेऽवमैरमित्रैर्जही न्येष्वशनिं तपिष्ठाम् । वृश्चेमधस्ताद्वि रुजा सहस्व जहि रक्षो मघवन्रन्धयस्व ॥
3.30.e: A cry is beard from enemies most near us: against them send thy fiercest-flaming weapon.  Rend them from under, crush them and subdue them. Slay, Maghavan, and make the fiends our booty.

3.30.d: उद्वृह रक्षः सहमूलमिन्द्र वृश्चा मध्यं प्रत्यग्रं शृणीहि । आ कीवतः सललूकं चकर्थ ब्रह्मद्विषे तपुषिं हेतिमस्य ॥
3.30.e: Root up the race of Rākṣasas, O Indra rend it in front and crush it in the middle.  How long hast thou bebaved as one who wavers? Cast thy hot dart at him who hates devotion:

3.30.d: स्वस्तये वाजिभिश्च प्रणेतः सं यन्महीरिष आसत्सि पूर्वीः । रायो वन्तारो बृहतः स्यामास्मे अस्तु भग इन्द्र प्रजावान् ॥
3.30.e: When borne by strong Steeds for our weal, O Leader, thou seatest thee at many noble viands.  May we be winners of abundant riches. May Indra be our wealth with store of children.

3.30.d: आ नो भर भगमिन्द्र द्युमन्तं नि ते देष्णस्य धीमहि प्ररेके । ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे तमा पृण वसुपते वसूनाम् ॥
3.30.e: Bestow on us resplendent wealth. O Indra let us enjoy thine overflow of bounty.  Wide as a sea our longing hath expanded, fulfil it, O thou Treasure-Lord of treasures.

3.30.d: इमं कामं मन्दया गोभिरश्वैश्चन्द्रवता राधसा पप्रथश्च । स्वर्यवो मतिभिस्तुभ्यं विप्रा इन्द्राय वाहः कुशिकासो अक्रन् ॥
3.30.e: With kine and horses satisfy this longing with very splendid bounty skill extend it.  Seeking the light, with hymns to thee, O Indra, Kuśikas have brought their gift, the singers.

3.30.d: आ नो गोत्रा दर्दृहि गोपते गाः समस्मभ्यं सनयो यन्तु वाजाः । दिवक्षा असि वृषभ सत्यशुष्मोऽस्मभ्यं सु मघवन्बोधि गोदाः ॥
3.30.e: Lord of the kine, burst the kine's stable open: cows shall be ours, and strength that wins the booty.  Hero, whose might is true, thy home is heaven: to us, O Maghavan, grant gifts of cattle.

3.30.d: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिन्द्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ । शृण्वन्तमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नन्तं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानाम् ॥
3.30.e: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.31.d: शासद्वह्निर्दुहितुर्नप्त्यं गाद्विद्वाँ ऋतस्य दीधितिं सपर्यन् । पिता यत्र दुहितुः सेकमृञ्जन्त्सं शग्म्येन मनसा दधन्वे ॥
3.31.e: WISE, teaching, following the thought of Order, the sonless gained a grandson from his daughter.  Fain, as a sire, to see his child prolific, he sped to meet her with an eager spirit.

3.31.d: न जामये तान्वो रिक्थमारैक्चकार गर्भं सनितुर्निधानम् । यदी मातरो जनयन्त वह्निमन्यः कर्ता सुकृतोरन्य ऋन्धन् ॥
3.31.e: The Son left not his portion to the brother, he made a home to hold him who should gain, it.  What time his Parents gave the Priest his being, of the good pair one acted, one promoted.

3.31.d: अग्निर्जज्ञे जुह्वा३ रेजमानो महस्पुत्राँ अरुषस्य प्रयक्षे । महान्गर्भो मह्या जातमेषां मही प्रवृद्धर्यश्वस्य यज्ञैः ॥
3.31.e: Agni was born trembling with tongue that flickered, so that the Red's great children should be honoured.  Great is their germ, that born of them is mighty, great the Bays' Lord's approach through sacrifices.

3.31.d: अभि जैत्रीरसचन्त स्पृधानं महि ज्योतिस्तमसो निरजानन् । तं जानतीः प्रत्युदायन्नुषासः पतिर्गवामभवदेक इन्द्रः ॥
3.31.e: Conquering bands upon the Warrior waited: they recognized great light from out the darkness.  The conscious Dawns went forth to meet his coming, and the sole Master of the kine was Indra.

3.31.d: वीळौ सतीरभि धीरा अतृन्दन्प्राचाहिन्वन्मनसा सप्त विप्राः । विश्वामविन्दन्पथ्यामृतस्य प्रजानन्नित्ता नमसा विवेश ॥
3.31.e: The sages freed them from their firmbuilt prison: the seven priests drove them forward with their spirit.  All holy Order's pathway they discovered he, full of knowledge, shared these deeds through worship.

3.31.d: विदद्यदी सरमा रुग्णमद्रेर्महि पाथः पूर्व्यं सध्र्यक्कः । अग्रं नयत्सुपद्यक्षराणामच्छा रवं प्रथमा जानती गात् ॥
3.31.e: When Saramā had found the mountain's fissure, that vast and ancient place she plundered thoroughly.  In the floods' van she led them forth, light-footed: she who well knew came first unto their lowing.

3.31.d: अगच्छदु विप्रतमः सखीयन्नसूदयत्सुकृते गर्भमद्रिः । ससान मर्यो युवभिर्मखस्यन्नथाभवदङ्गिराः सद्यो अर्चन् ॥
3.31.e: Longing for friendship came the noblest singer: the hill poured forth its treasure for the pious.  The Hero with young followers fought and conquered, and straightway Aṅgiras was singing praises,

3.31.d: सतःसतः प्रतिमानं पुरोभूर्विश्वा वेद जनिमा हन्ति शुष्णम् । प्र णो दिवः पदवीर्गव्युरर्चन्त्सखा सखीँरमुञ्चन्निरवद्यात् ॥
3.31.e: Peer of each noble thing, yea, all excelling, all creatures doth he know, he slayeth Śuṣṇa.  Our leader, fain for war, singing from heaven, as Friend he saved his lovers from dishonour.

3.31.d: नि गव्यता मनसा सेदुरर्कैः कृण्वानासो अमृतत्वाय गातुम् । इदं चिन्नु सदनं भूर्येषां येन मासाँ असिषासन्नृतेन ॥
3.31.e: They sate them down with spirit fain for booty, making with hymns a way to life eternal.  And this is still their place of frequent session, whereby they sought to gain the months through Order.

3.31.d: सम्पश्यमाना अमदन्नभि स्वं पयः प्रत्नस्य रेतसो दुघानाः । वि रोदसी अतपद्घोष एषां जाते निष्ठामदधुर्गोषु वीरान् ॥
3.31.e: Drawing the milk of ancient seed prolific, they joyed as they beheld their own possession.  Their shout of triumph heated earth and heaven. When the kine showed, they bade the heroes rouse them.

3.31.d: स जातेभिर्वृत्रहा सेदु हव्यैरुदुस्रिया असृजदिन्द्रो अर्कैः । उरूच्यस्मै घृतवद्भरन्ती मधु स्वाद्म दुदुहे जेन्या गौः ॥
3.31.e: Indra drove forth the kine, that Vṛtra-slayer, while hymns of praise rose up and gifts were offered.  For him the Cow, noble and far-extending, poured pleasant juices, bringing oil and sweetness.

3.31.d: पित्रे चिच्चक्रुः सदनं समस्मै महि त्विषीमत्सुकृतो वि हि ख्यन् । विष्कभ्नन्तः स्कम्भनेना जनित्री आसीना ऊर्ध्वं रभसं वि मिन्वन् ॥
3.31.e: They made a mansion for their Father, deftly provided him a great and glorious dwelling;  With firm support parted and stayed the Parents, and, sitting, fixed him there erected, mighty.

3.31.d: मही यदि धिषणा शिश्नथे धात्सद्योवृधं विभ्वं१ रोदस्योः । गिरो यस्मिन्ननवद्याः समीचीर्विश्वा इन्द्राय तविषीरनुत्ताः ॥
3.31.e: What time the ample chalice had impelled him, swift waxing, vast, to pierce the earth and heaven,—  Him in whom blameless songs are all united: all powers invincible belong to Indra.

3.31.d: मह्या ते सख्यं वश्मि शक्तीरा वृत्रघ्ने नियुतो यन्ति पूर्वीः । महि स्तोत्रमव आगन्म सूरेरस्माकं सु मघवन्बोधि गोपाः ॥
3.31.e: I crave thy powers, I crave thy mighty friendship: full many a team goes to the Vṛtra-slayer.  Great is the laud, we seek the Princes' favour. Be thou, O Maghavan, our guard and keeper.

3.31.d: महि क्षेत्रं पुरु श्चन्द्रं विविद्वानादित्सखिभ्यश्चरथं समैरत् । इन्द्रो नृभिरजनद्दीद्यानः साकं सूर्यमुषसं गातुमग्निम् ॥
3.31.e: He, having found great, splendid, rich dominion, sent life and motion to his friends and lovers.  Indra who shone together with the Heroes begot the song, the fire, and Sun and Morning.

3.31.d: अपश्चिदेष विभ्वो३ दमूनाः प्र सध्रीचीरसृजद्विश्वश्चन्द्राः । मध्वः पुनानाः कविभिः पवित्रैर्द्युभिर्हिन्वन्त्यक्तुभिर्धनुत्रीः ॥
3.31.e: Vast, the House-Friend, he set the waters flowing, all-lucid, widely spread, that move together.  By the wise cleansings of the meath made holy, through days, and nights they speed the swift streams onward.

3.31.d: अनु कृष्णे वसुधिती जिहाते उभे सूर्यस्य मंहना यजत्रे । परि यत्ते महिमानं वृजध्यै सखाय इन्द्र काम्या ऋजिप्याः ॥
3.31.e: To thee proceed the dark, the treasure-holders, both of them sanctified by Sūrya's bounty.  The while thy ovely storming Friends, O Indra, fail to attain the measure of thy greatness.

3.31.d: पतिर्भव वृत्रहन्त्सूनृतानां गिरां विश्वायुर्वृषभो वयोधाः । आ नो गहि सख्येभिः शिवेभिर्महान्महीभिरूतिभिः सरण्यन् ॥
3.31.e: Be Lord of joyous songs, O Vṛtra-slayer, Bull dear to all, who gives the power of living.  Come unto us with thine auspicious friendship, hastening, Mighty One, with mighty succours.

3.31.d: तमङ्गिरस्वन्नमसा सपर्यन्नव्यं कृणोमि सन्यसे पुराजाम् । द्रुहो वि याहि बहुला अदेवीः स्वश्च नो मघवन्त्सातये धाः ॥
3.31.e: Like Aṅgiras I honour him with worship, and renovate old song for him the Ancient.  Chase thou the many godless evil creatures, and give us, Maghavan, heaven's light to help m.

3.31.d: मिहः पावकाः प्रतता अभूवन्त्स्वस्ति नः पिपृहि पारमासाम् । इन्द्र त्वं रथिरः पाहि नो रिषो मक्षूमक्षू कृणुहि गोजितो नः ॥
3.31.e: Far forth are spread the purifying waters convey thou us across them unto safety.  Save us, our Charioteer, from harm, O Indra, soon, very soon, make us win spoil of cattle.

3.31.d: अदेदिष्ट वृत्रहा गोपतिर्गा अन्तः कृष्णाँ अरुषैर्धामभिर्गात् । प्र सूनृता दिशमान ऋतेन दुरश्च विश्वा अवृणोदप स्वाः ॥
3.31.e: His kine their Lord hath shown, e’en Vṛtra's slayer, through the black hosts he passed with red attendants.  Teaching us pleasant things by holy Order, to, us hath he thrown open all his portals.

3.31.d: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिन्द्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ । शृण्वन्तमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नन्तं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानाम् ॥
3.31.e: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered.  The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.32.d: इन्द्र सोमं सोमपते पिबेमं माध्यंदिनं सवनं चारु यत्ते । प्रप्रुथ्या शिप्रे मघवन्नृजीषिन्विमुच्या हरी इह मादयस्व ॥
3.32.e: DRINK thou this Soma, Indra, Lord of Soma; drink thou the draught of noonday which thou Iovest.  Puffing thy cheeks, impetuous, liberal Giver, here loose thy two Bay Horses and rejoice thee.

3.32.d: गवाशिरं मन्थिनमिन्द्र शुक्रं पिबा सोमं ररिमा ते मदाय । ब्रह्मकृता मारुतेना गणेन सजोषा रुद्रैस्तृपदा वृषस्व ॥
3.32.e: Quaff it pure, meal-blent, mixt with milk, O Indra; we have poured forth the Soma for thy rapture.  Knit with the prayer-fulfilling band of Maruts, yea, with the Rudras, drink till thou art sated;

3.32.d: ये ते शुष्मं ये तविषीमवर्धन्नर्चन्त इन्द्र मरुतस्त ओजः । माध्यंदिने सवने वज्रहस्त पिबा रुद्रेभिः सगणः सुशिप्र ॥
3.32.e: Those who gave increase to thy strength and vigour; the Maruts singing forth thy might, O Indra.  Drink thou, O fair of cheek, whose hand wields thunder, with Rudras banded, at our noon libation.

3.32.d: त इन्न्वस्य मधुमद्विविप्र इन्द्रस्य शर्धो मरुतो य आसन् । येभिर्वृत्रस्येषितो विवेदामर्मणो मन्यमानस्य मर्म ॥
3.32.e: They, even the Maruts who were there, excited with song the meath-created strength of Indra.  By them impelled to act he reached the vitals Of Vṛtra, though he deemed that none might wound him.

3.32.d: मनुष्वदिन्द्र सवनं जुषाणः पिबा सोमं शश्वते वीर्याय । स आ ववृत्स्व हर्यश्व यज्ञैः सरण्युभिरपो अर्णा सिसर्षि ॥
3.32.e: Pleased, like a man, with our libation, Indra, drink, for enduring hero might, the Soma.  Lord of Bays, moved by sacrifice come hither: thou with the Swift Ones stirrest floods and waters.

3.32.d: त्वमपो यद्ध वृत्रं जघन्वाँ अत्याँ इव प्रासृजः सर्तवाजौ । शयानमिन्द्र चरता वधेन वव्रिवांसं परि देवीरदेवम् ॥
3.32.e: When thou didst loose the streams to run like racers in the swift contest, having smitten Vṛtra  With flying weapon where he lay, O Indra, and, godless, kept the Goddesses encompassed.

3.32.d: यजाम इन्नमसा वृद्धमिन्द्रं बृहन्तमृष्वमजरं युवानम् । यस्य प्रिये ममतुर्यज्ञियस्य न रोदसी महिमानं ममाते ॥
3.32.e: With reverence let us worship mighty Indra, great and sublime, eternal, everyouthful,  Whose greatness the dear world-halves have not measured, no, nor conceived the might of him the Holy.

3.32.d: इन्द्रस्य कर्म सुकृता पुरूणि व्रतानि देवा न मिनन्ति विश्वे । दाधार यः पृथिवीं द्यामुतेमां जजान सूर्यमुषसं सुदंसाः ॥
3.32.e: Many are Indra's nobly wrought achievements, and none of all the Gods transgress his statutes.  He beareth up this earth and heaven, and, doer of marvels, he begot the Sun and Morning.

3.32.d: अद्रोघ सत्यं तव तन्महित्वं सद्यो यज्जातो अपिबो ह सोमम् । न द्याव इन्द्र तवसस्त ओजो नाहा न मासाः शरदो वरन्त ॥
3.32.e: Herein, O Guileless One, is thy true greatness, that soon as born thou drankest up the Soma.  Days may not check the power of thee the Mighty, nor the nights, Indra, nor the months, nor autumns.

3.32.d: त्वं सद्यो अपिबो जात इन्द्र मदाय सोमं परमे व्योमन् । यद्ध द्यावापृथिवी आविवेशीरथाभवः पूर्व्यः कारुधायाः ॥
3.32.e: As soon as thou wast born in highest heaven thou drankest Soma to delight thee, Indra;  And when thou hadst pervaded earth and heaven thou wast the first supporter of the singer.

3.32.d: अहन्नहिं परिशयानमर्ण ओजायमानं तुविजात तव्यान् । न ते महित्वमनु भूदध द्यौर्यदन्यया स्फिग्या३ क्षामवस्थाः ॥
3.32.e: Thou, puissant God, more mighty, slewest. Ahi showing his strength when couched around the waters.  The heaven itself attained not to thy greatness when with one hip of thine the earth was shadowed.

3.32.d: यज्ञो हि त इन्द्र वर्धनो भूदुत प्रियः सुतसोमो मियेधः । यज्ञेन यज्ञमव यज्ञियः सन्यज्ञस्ते वज्रमहिहत्य आवत् ॥
3.32.e: Sacrifice, Indra, made thee wax so mighty, the dear oblation with the flowing Soma.  O Worshipful, with worship help our worship, for worship helped thy bolt when slaying Ahi.

3.32.d: यज्ञेनेन्द्रमवसा चक्रे अर्वागैनं सुम्नाय नव्यसे ववृत्याम् । यः स्तोमेभिर्वावृधे पूर्व्येभिर्यो मध्यमेभिरुत नूतनेभिः ॥
3.32.e: With sacrifice and wish have I brought Indra; still for new blessings may I turn him hither,  Him magnified by ancient songs and praises, by lauds of later time and days yet recent.

3.32.d: विवेष यन्मा धिषणा जजान स्तवै पुरा पार्यादिन्द्रमह्नः । अंहसो यत्र पीपरद्यथा नो नावेव यान्तमुभये हवन्ते ॥
3.32.e: I have brought forth a song when longing seized me: ere the decisive day will I laud Indra;  Then may he safely bear us over trouble, as in a ship, when both sides invocate him.

3.32.d: आपूर्णो अस्य कलशः स्वाहा सेक्तेव कोशं सिसिचे पिबध्यै । समु प्रिया आववृत्रन्मदाय प्रदक्षिणिदभि सोमास इन्द्रम् ॥
3.32.e: Full is his chalice: Glory! Like a pourer I have filled up the vessel for his drinking.  Presented on the right, dear Soma juices have brought us Indra, to rejoice him, hither.

3.32.d: न त्वा गभीरः पुरुहूत सिन्धुर्नाद्रयः परि षन्तो वरन्त । इत्था सखिभ्य इषितो यदिन्द्रा दृळ्हं चिदरुजो गव्यमूर्वम् ॥
3.32.e: Not the deep-flowing flood, O Much-invoked One! not hills that compass thee about restrain thee,  Since here incited, for thy friends, O Indra, thou breakest e’en the firm built stall of cattle.

3.32.d: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिन्द्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ । शृण्वन्तमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नन्तं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानाम् ॥
3.32.e: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.33.d: प्र पर्वतानामुशती उपस्थादश्वे इव विषिते हासमाने । गावेव शुभ्रे मातरा रिहाणे विपाट् छुतुद्री पयसा जवेते ॥
3.33.e: FORTH from the bosom of the mountains, eager as two swift mares with loosened rein contending,  Like two bright mother cows who lick their youngling, Vipāś and Sutudri speed down their waters.

3.33.d: इन्द्रेषिते प्रसवं भिक्षमाणे अच्छा समुद्रं रथ्येव याथः । समाराणे ऊर्मिभिः पिन्वमाने अन्या वामन्यामप्येति शुभ्रे ॥
3.33.e: Impelled by Indra whom ye pray to urge you, ye move as ’twere on chariots to the ocean.  Flowing together, swelling with your billows, O lucid Streams, each of you seeks the other.

3.33.d: अच्छा सिन्धुं मातृतमामयासं विपाशमुर्वीं सुभगामगन्म । वत्समिव मातरा संरिहाणे समानं योनिमनु संचरन्ती ॥
3.33.e: I have attained the most maternal River, we have approached Vipāś, the broad, the blessed.  Licking as ’twere their calf the pair of Mothers flow onward to their common home together.

3.33.d: एना वयं पयसा पिन्वमाना अनु योनिं देवकृतं चरन्तीः । न वर्तवे प्रसवः सर्गतक्तः किंयुर्विप्रो नद्यो जोहवीति ॥
3.33.e: We two who rise and swell with billowy waters move forward to the home which Gods have made us.  Our flood may not be stayed when urged to motion. What would the singer, calling to the Rivers?

3.33.d: रमध्वं मे वचसे सोम्याय ऋतावरीरुप मुहूर्तमेवैः । प्र सिन्धुमच्छा बृहती मनीषावस्युरह्वे कुशिकस्य सूनुः ॥
3.33.e: Linger a little at my friendly bidding rest, Holy Ones, a moment in your journey.  With hymn sublime soliciting your favour Kuśika's son hath called unto the River.

3.33.d: इन्द्रो अस्माँ अरदद्वज्रबाहुरपाहन्वृत्रं परिधिं नदीनाम् । देवोऽनयत्सविता सुपाणिस्तस्य वयं प्रसवे याम उर्वीः ॥
3.33.e: Indra who wields the thunder dug our channels: he smote down Vṛtra, him who stayed our currents.  Savitar, God, the lovely-handed, led us, and at his sending forth we flow expanded.

3.33.d: प्रवाच्यं शश्वधा वीर्यं१ तदिन्द्रस्य कर्म यदहिं विवृश्चत् । वि वज्रेण परिषदो जघानायन्नापोऽयनमिच्छमानाः ॥
3.33.e: That hero deed of Indra must be lauded for ever that he rent Ahi in pieces.  He smote away the obstructors with his thunder, and eager for their course forth flowed the waters.

3.33.d: एतद्वचो जरितर्मापि मृष्ठा आ यत्ते घोषानुत्तरा युगानि । उक्थेषु कारो प्रति नो जुषस्व मा नो नि कः पुरुषत्रा नमस्ते ॥
3.33.e: Never forget this word of thine, O singer, which future generations shall reecho.  In hymns, O bard, show us thy loving kindness. Humble us not mid men. To thee be honour!

3.33.d: ओ षु स्वसारः कारवे शृणोत ययौ वो दूरादनसा रथेन । नि षू नमध्वं भवता सुपारा अधोअक्षाः सिन्धवः स्रोत्याभिः ॥
3.33.e: List quickly, Sisters, to the bard who cometh to you from far away with car and wagon.  Bow lowly down; be easy to be traversed stay, Rivers, with your floods below our axles.

3.33.d: आ ते कारो शृणवामा वचांसि ययाथ दूरादनसा रथेन । नि ते नंसै पीप्यानेव योषा मर्यायेव कन्या शश्वचै ते ॥
3.33.e: Yea, we will listen to thy words, O singer. With wain and car from far away thou comest.  Low, like a nursing mother, will I bend me, and yield me as a maiden to her lover.

3.33.d: यदङ्ग त्वा भरताः संतरेयुर्गव्यन्ग्राम इषित इन्द्रजूतः । अर्षादह प्रसवः सर्गतक्त आ वो वृणे सुमतिं यज्ञियानाम् ॥
3.33.e: Soon as the Bharatas have fared across thee, the warrior band, urged on and sped by Indra,  Then let your streams flow on in rapid motion. I crave your favour who deserve our worship.

3.33.d: अतारिषुर्भरता गव्यवः समभक्त विप्रः सुमतिं नदीनाम् । प्र पिन्वध्वमिषयन्तीः सुराधा आ वक्षणाः पृणध्वं यात शीभम् ॥
3.33.e: The warrior host, the Bharatas, fared over the singer won the favour of the Rivers.  Swell with your billows, hasting, pouring riches. Fill full your channels, and roll swiftly onward.

3.33.d: उद्व ऊर्मिः शम्या हन्त्वापो योक्त्राणि मुञ्चत । मादुष्कृतौ व्येनसाघ्न्यौ शूनमारताम् ॥
3.33.e: So let your wave bear up the pins, and ye, O Waters, spare the thongs;  And never may the pair of Bulls, harmless and sinless, waste away.

3.34.d: इन्द्रः पूर्भिदातिरद्दासमर्कैर्विदद्वसुर्दयमानो वि शत्रून् । ब्रह्मजूतस्तन्वा वावृधानो भूरिदात्र आपृणद्रोदसी उभे ॥
3.34.e: FORT-RENDER, Lord of Wealth, dispelling foemen, Indra with lightnings hath o’ercome the Dāsa.  Impelled by prayer and waxen great in body, he hath filled earth and heaven, the Bounteous Giver.

3.34.d: मखस्य ते तविषस्य प्र जूतिमियर्मि वाचममृताय भूषन् । इन्द्र क्षितीनामसि मानुषीणां विशां दैवीनामुत पूर्वयावा ॥
3.34.e: I stimulate thy zeal, the Strong, the Hero decking my song of praise forth; Immortal.  O Indra, thou art equally the Leader of heavenly hosts and human generations.

3.34.d: इन्द्रो वृत्रमवृणोच्छर्धनीतिः प्र मायिनाममिनाद्वर्पणीतिः । अहन्व्यंसमुशधग्वनेष्वाविर्धेना अकृणोद्राम्याणाम् ॥
3.34.e: Leading, his band Indra encompassed Vṛtra; weak grew the wily leader of enchanters.  He who burns fierce in forests slaughtered Vyaṁsa, and made the Milch-kine of the nights apparent.

3.34.d: इन्द्रः स्वर्षा जनयन्नहानि जिगायोशिग्भिः पृतना अभिष्टिः । प्रारोचयन्मनवे केतुमह्नामविन्दज्ज्योतिर्बृहते रणाय ॥
3.34.e: Indra, light-winner, days' Creator, conquered, victorious, hostile bands with those who loved him.  For man the days' bright ensign he illumined, and found the light for his joy and gladness.

3.34.d: इन्द्रस्तुजो बर्हणा आ विवेश नृवद्दधानो नर्या पुरूणि । अचेतयद्धिय इमा जरित्रे प्रेमं वर्णमतिरच्छुक्रमासाम् ॥
3.34.e: Forward to fiercely falling blows pressed Indra, herolike doing many hero exploits.  These holy songs he taught the bard who gaised him, and widely spread these Dawns' resplendent colour.

3.34.d: महो महानि पनयन्त्यस्येन्द्रस्य कर्म सुकृता पुरूणि । वृजनेन वृजिनान्त्सं पिपेष मायाभिर्दस्यूँरभिभूत्योजाः ॥
3.34.e: They laud the mighty acts of him the Mighty, the many glorious deeds performed by Indra.  He in his strength, with all-surpassing prowess, through wondrous arts crushed the malignant Dasyus.

3.34.d: युधेन्द्रो मह्ना वरिवश्चकार देवेभ्यः सत्पतिश्चर्षणिप्राः । विवस्वतः सदने अस्य तानि विप्रा उक्थेभिः कवयो गृणन्ति ॥
3.34.e: Lord of the brave, Indra who rules the people gave freedom to the Gods by might and battle.  Wise singers glorify with chanted praises these his achievements in Vivasvān's dwelling.

3.34.d: सत्रासाहं वरेण्यं सहोदां ससवांसं स्वरपश्च देवीः । ससान यः पृथिवीं द्यामुतेमामिन्द्रं मदन्त्यनु धीरणासः ॥
3.34.e: Excellent, Conqueror, the victory-giver, the winner of the light and Godlike Waters,  He who hath won this broad earth and this heaven, -in Indra they rejoice who love devotions.

3.34.d: ससानात्याँ उत सूर्यं ससानेन्द्रः ससान पुरुभोजसं गाम् । हिरण्ययमुत भोगं ससान हत्वी दस्यून्प्रार्यं वर्णमावत् ॥
3.34.e: He gained possession of the Sun and Horses, Indra obtained the Cow who feedeth many.  Treasure of gold he won; he smote the Dasyus, and gave protection to the Āryan colour.

3.34.d: इन्द्र ओषधीरसनोदहानि वनस्पतीँरसनोदन्तरिक्षम् । बिभेद वलं नुनुदे विवाचोऽथाभवद्दमिताभिक्रतूनाम् ॥
3.34.e: He took the plants and days for his possession; he gained the forest trees and air's mid-region.  Vala he cleft, and chased away opponents: thus was he tamer of the overweening.

3.34.d: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिन्द्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ । शृण्वन्तमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नन्तं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानाम् ॥
3.34.e: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers treasures.

3.35.d: तिष्ठा हरी रथ आ युज्यमाना याहि वायुर्न नियुतो नो अच्छ । पिबास्यन्धो अभिसृष्टो अस्मे इन्द्र स्वाहा ररिमा ते मदाय ॥
3.35.e: MOUNT the Bay Horses to thy chariot harnessed, and come to us like Vāyu with his coursers.  Thou, hastening to us, shalt drink the Soma. Hail, Indra. We have poured it for thy rapture.

3.35.d: उपाजिरा पुरुहूताय सप्ती हरी रथस्य धूर्ष्वा युनज्मि । द्रवद्यथा सम्भृतं विश्वतश्चिदुपेमं यज्ञमा वहात इन्द्रम् ॥
