3.35.e: For him, the God who is invoked by many, the two swift Bay Steeds to the pole I harness,  That they in fleet course may bring Indra hither, e’en to this sacrifice arranged completely.

3.35.d: उपो नयस्व वृषणा तपुष्पोतेमव त्वं वृषभ स्वधावः । ग्रसेतामश्वा वि मुचेह शोणा दिवेदिवे सदृशीरद्धि धानाः ॥
3.35.e: Bring the strong Steeds who drink the warm libation, and, Bull of Godlike nature, be thou gracious.  Let thy Steeds eat; set free thy Tawny Horses, and roasted grain like this consume thou daily.

3.35.d: ब्रह्मणा ते ब्रह्मयुजा युनज्मि हरी सखाया सधमाद आशू । स्थिरं रथं सुखमिन्द्राधितिष्ठन्प्रजानन्विद्वाँ उप याहि सोमम् ॥
3.35.e: Those who are yoked by prayer I harness, fleet friendly Bays who take their joy together.  Mounting thy firm and easy car, O Indra, wise and all-knowing come thou to the Soma.

3.35.d: मा ते हरी वृषणा वीतपृष्ठा नि रीरमन्यजमानासो अन्ये । अत्यायाहि शश्वतो वयं तेऽरं सुतेभिः कृणवाम सोमैः ॥
3.35.e: No other worshippers must stay beside them thy Bays, thy vigorous and smooth-backed Coursers.  Pass by them all and hasten onward hither: with Soma pressed we will prepare to feast thee.

3.35.d: तवायं सोमस्त्वमेह्यर्वाङ्छश्वत्तमं सुमना अस्य पाहि । अस्मिन्यज्ञे बर्हिष्या निषद्या दधिष्वेमं जठर इन्दुमिन्द्र ॥
3.35.e: Thine is this Soma: hasten to approach it. Drink thou thereof, benevolent, and cease not.  Sit on the sacred grass at this our worship, and take these drops into thy belly, Indra.

3.35.d: स्तीर्णं ते बर्हिः सुत इन्द्र सोमः कृता धाना अत्तवे ते हरिभ्याम् । तदोकसे पुरुशाकाय वृष्णे मरुत्वते तुभ्यं राता हवींषि ॥
3.35.e: The grass is strewn for thee, pressed is the Soma; the grain is ready for thy Bays to feed on.  To thee who lovest them, the very mighty, strong, girt by Maruts, are these gifts presented.

3.35.d: इमं नरः पर्वतास्तुभ्यमापः समिन्द्र गोभिर्मधुमन्तमक्रन् । तस्यागत्या सुमना ऋष्व पाहि प्रजानन्विद्वान्पथ्या३ अनु स्वाः ॥
3.35.e: This the sweet draught, with cows, the men, the mountains, the waters, Indra, have for thee made ready.  Come, drink thereof, Sublime One, friendly-minded, foreseeing, knowing well the ways thou goest.

3.35.d: याँ आभजो मरुत इन्द्र सोमे ये त्वामवर्धन्नभवन्गणस्ते । तेभिरेतं सजोषा वावशानो३ऽग्नेः पिब जिह्वया सोममिन्द्र ॥
3.35.e: The Maruts, they with whom thou sharedst Soma, Indra, who made thee strong and were thine army,—  With these accordant, eagerly desirous drink thou this Soma with the tongue of Agni.

3.35.d: इन्द्र पिब स्वधया चित्सुतस्याग्नेर्वा पाहि जिह्वया यजत्र । अध्वर्योर्वा प्रयतं शक्र हस्ताद्धोतुर्वा यज्ञं हविषो जुषस्व ॥
3.35.e: Drink, Indra, of the juice by thine own nature, or by the tongue of Agni, O thou Holy.  Accept the sacrificial gift, O Śakra, from the Adhvaryu's hand or from the Hotar's.

3.35.d: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिन्द्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ । शृण्वन्तमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नन्तं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानाम् ॥
3.35.e: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong, who listens, who.gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.36.d: इमामू षु प्रभृतिं सातये धाः शश्वच्छश्वदूतिभिर्यादमानः । सुतेसुते वावृधे वर्धनेभिर्यः कर्मभिर्महद्भिः सुश्रुतो भूत् ॥
3.36.e: WITH constant succours, fain thyself to share it, make this oblation which we bring effective.  Grown great through strengthening gifts at each libation, he hath become renowned by mighty exploits.

3.36.d: इन्द्राय सोमाः प्रदिवो विदाना ऋभुर्येभिर्वृषपर्वा विहायाः । प्रयम्यमानान्प्रति षू गृभायेन्द्र पिब वृषधूतस्य वृष्णः ॥
3.36.e: For Indra were the Somas erst- discovered, whereby he grew strong-jointed, vast, and skilful.  Indra , take quickly these presented juices: drink of the strong, that which the strong have shaken.

3.36.d: पिबा वर्धस्व तव घा सुतास इन्द्र सोमासः प्रथमा उतेमे । यथापिबः पूर्व्याँ इन्द्र सोमाँ एवा पाहि पन्यो अद्या नवीयान् ॥
3.36.e: Drink and wax great. Thine are the juices, Indra, both Somas of old time and these we bring thee.  Even as thou drankest, Indra, earlier Somas, so drink to-day, a new guest, meet for praises.

3.36.d: महाँ अमत्रो वृजने विरप्श्यु१ग्रं शवः पत्यते धृष्ण्वोजः । नाह विव्याच पृथिवी चनैनं यत्सोमासो हर्यश्वममन्दन् ॥
3.36.e: Great and impetuous, mighty-voiced in battle, surpassing power is his, and strength resistless.  Him the broad earth hath never comprehended when Somas cheered the Lord of Tawny Coursers.

3.36.d: महाँ उग्रो वावृधे वीर्याय समाचक्रे वृषभः काव्येन । इन्द्रो भगो वाजदा अस्य गावः प्र जायन्ते दक्षिणा अस्य पूर्वीः ॥
3.36.e: Mighty and strong he waxed for hero exploit: the Bull was furnished a Sage's wisdom.  Indra is our kind Lord; his steers have vigour; his cows are many with abundant offspring.

3.36.d: प्र यत्सिन्धवः प्रसवं यथायन्नापः समुद्रं रथ्येव जग्मुः । अतश्चिदिन्द्रः सदसो वरीयान्यदीं सोमः पृणति दुग्धो अंशुः ॥
3.36.e: As floods according to their stream flow onward, so to the sea, as borne on cars, the waters.  Vaster is Indra even than his dwelling, what time the stalk milked out, the Soma, fills him.

3.36.d: समुद्रेण सिन्धवो यादमाना इन्द्राय सोमं सुषुतं भरन्तः । अंशुं दुहन्ति हस्तिनो भरित्रैर्मध्वः पुनन्ति धारया पवित्रैः ॥
3.36.e: Eager to mingle with the sea, the rivers carry the well-pressed Soma juice to Indra.  They drain the stalk out with their arms, quick-banded, and cleanse it with a stream of mead and filters.

3.36.d: ह्रदा इव कुक्षयः सोमधानाः समी विव्याच सवना पुरूणि । अन्ना यदिन्द्रः प्रथमा व्याश वृत्रं जघन्वाँ अवृणीत सोमम् ॥
3.36.e: Like lakes appear his flanks filled full with Soma: yea, he contains libations in abundance.  When Indra had consumed the first sweet viands, he, after slaying Vṛtra, claimed the Soma.

3.36.d: आ तू भर माकिरेतत्परि ष्ठाद्विद्मा हि त्वा वसुपतिं वसूनाम् । इन्द्र यत्ते माहिनं दत्रमस्त्यस्मभ्यं तद्धर्यश्व प्र यन्धि ॥
3.36.e: Then bring thou hither, and let none prevent it: we know thee well, the Lord of wealth and treasure.  That splendid gift which is thine own, O Indra, vouchsafe to us, Lord of the Tawny Coursers.

3.36.d: अस्मे प्र यन्धि मघवन्नृजीषिन्निन्द्र रायो विश्ववारस्य भूरेः । अस्मे शतं शरदो जीवसे धा अस्मे वीराञ्छश्वत इन्द्र शिप्रिन् ॥
3.36.e: O Indra, Maghavan, impetuous mover, grant us abundant wealth that brings all blessings.  Give us a hundred autumns for our lifetime: give us, O fair-checked Indra, store of heroes.

3.36.d: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिन्द्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ । शृण्वन्तमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नन्तं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानाम् ॥
3.36.e: Call we on Indra, Maghavan, auspicious, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.37.d: वार्त्रहत्याय शवसे पृतनाषाह्याय च । इन्द्र त्वा वर्तयामसि ॥
3.37.e: O INDRA, for the strength that slays Vṛtra and conquers in the fight,  We turn thee hitherward to us.

3.37.d: अर्वाचीनं सु ते मन उत चक्षुः शतक्रतो । इन्द्र कृण्वन्तु वाघतः ॥
3.37.e: O Indra, Lord of Hundred Powers, may those who praise thee hitherward.  Direct thy spirit and thine eye.
O Indra, Lord of Hundred Powers, with all our songs we invocate  Thy names for triumph over foes.

3.37.d: पुरुष्टुतस्य धामभिः शतेन महयामसि । इन्द्रस्य चर्षणीधृतः ॥
3.37.e: We strive for glory through the powers immense of him whom many praise,  Of Indra who supports mankind.

3.37.d: इन्द्रं वृत्राय हन्तवे पुरुहूतमुप ब्रुवे । भरेषु वाजसातये ॥
3.37.e: For Vṛtra's slaughter I address Indra whom many invocate,  To win us booty in the wars.

3.37.d: वाजेषु सासहिर्भव त्वामीमहे शतक्रतो । इन्द्र वृत्राय हन्तवे ॥
3.37.e: In battles be victorious. We seek thee, Lord of Hundred Powers,  Indra, that Vṛtra may be slain.

3.37.d: द्युम्नेषु पृतनाज्ये पृत्सुतूर्षु श्रवःसु च । इन्द्र साक्ष्वाभिमातिषु ॥
3.37.e: In splendid combats of the hosts, in glories where the fight is won.  Indra, be victor over foes.

3.37.d: शुष्मिन्तमं न ऊतये द्युम्निनं पाहि जागृविम् । इन्द्र सोमं शतक्रतो ॥
3.37.e: Drink thou the Soma for our help, bright, vigilant, exceeding strong,  O Indra, Lord of Hundred Powers.

3.37.d: इन्द्रियाणि शतक्रतो या ते जनेषु पञ्चसु । इन्द्र तानि त आ वृणे ॥
3.37.e: O Śatakratu, powers which thou mid the Five Races hast displayed-  These, Indra, do I claim of thee.

3.37.d: अगन्निन्द्र श्रवो बृहद्द्युम्नं दधिष्व दुष्टरम् । उत्ते शुष्मं तिरामसि ॥
3.37.e: Indra, great glory hast thou gained. Win splendid fame which none may mar  We make thy might perpetual.

3.37.d: अर्वावतो न आ गह्यथो शक्र परावतः । उ लोको यस्ते अद्रिव इन्द्रेह तत आ गहि ॥
3.37.e: Come to us either from anear, Or, Śakra, come from far away.  Indra, wherever be thy home, come to us thence, O Thunder-armed.

3.38.d: अभि तष्टेव दीधया मनीषामत्यो न वाजी सुधुरो जिहानः । अभि प्रियाणि मर्मृशत्पराणि कवीँरिच्छामि संदृशे सुमेधाः ॥
3.38.e: HASTING like some strong courser good at drawing, a thought have I imagined like a workman.  Pondering what is dearest and most noble, I long to see the sages full of wisdom.

3.38.d: इनोत पृच्छ जनिमा कवीनां मनोधृतः सुकृतस्तक्षत द्याम् । इमा उ ते प्रण्यो३ वर्धमाना मनोवाता अध नु धर्मणि ग्मन् ॥
3.38.e: Ask of the sages' mighty generations firm-minded and devout they framed the heaven.  These are thy heart-sought strengthening directions, and they have come to be sky's upholders.

3.38.d: नि षीमिदत्र गुह्या दधाना उत क्षत्राय रोदसी समञ्जन् । सं मात्राभिर्ममिरे येमुरुर्वी अन्तर्मही समृते धायसे धुः ॥
3.38.e: Assuming in this world mysterious natures, they decked the heaven and earth for high dominion,  Measured with measures, fixed their broad expanses, set the great worlds apart held firm for safety.

3.38.d: आतिष्ठन्तं परि विश्वे अभूषञ्छ्रियो वसानश्चरति स्वरोचिः । महत्तद्वृष्णो असुरस्य नामा विश्वरूपो अमृतानि तस्थौ ॥
3.38.e: Even as he mounted up they all adorned him: self-luminous he travels clothed in splendour.  That is the Bull's, the Asura's mighty figure: he, omniform, hath reached the eternal waters.

3.38.d: असूत पूर्वो वृषभो ज्यायानिमा अस्य शुरुधः सन्ति पूर्वीः । दिवो नपाता विदथस्य धीभिः क्षत्रं राजाना प्रदिवो दधाथे ॥
3.38.e: First the more ancient Bull engendered offspring; these are his many draughts that lent him vigour.  From days of old ye Kings, two Sons of Heaven, by hymns of sacrifice have won dominion.

3.38.d: त्रीणि राजाना विदथे पुरूणि परि विश्वानि भूषथः सदांसि । अपश्यमत्र मनसा जगन्वान्व्रते गन्धर्वाँ अपि वायुकेशान् ॥
3.38.e: Three seats ye Sovrans, in the Holy synod, many, yea, all, ye honour with your presence.  There saw I, going thither in the spirit, Gandharvas in their course with wind-blown tresses.

3.38.d: तदिन्न्वस्य वृषभस्य धेनोरा नामभिर्ममिरे सक्म्यं गोः । अन्यदन्यदसुर्यं१ वसाना नि मायिनो ममिरे रूपमस्मिन् ॥
3.38.e: That same companionship of her, the Milch-cow, here with the strong Bull's divers forms they stablished.  Enduing still some new celestial figure, the skilful workers shaped a form around him.

3.38.d: तदिन्न्वस्य सवितुर्नकिर्मे हिरण्ययीममतिं यामशिश्रेत् । आ सुष्टुती रोदसी विश्वमिन्वे अपीव योषा जनिमानि वव्रे ॥
3.38.e: Let no one here debar me from enjoying the golden light which Savitar diffuses.  He covers both all-fostering worlds with praises even as a woman cherishes her children.

3.38.d: युवं प्रत्नस्य साधथो महो यद्दैवी स्वस्तिः परि णः स्यातम् । गोपाजिह्वस्य तस्थुषो विरूपा विश्वे पश्यन्ति मायिनः कृतानि ॥
3.38.e: Fulfil, ye twain, his work, the Great, the Ancient: as heavenly blessing keep your guard around us.  All the wise Gods behold his varied actions who stands erect, whose voice is like a herdsman's.

3.38.d: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिन्द्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ । शृण्वन्तमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नन्तं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानाम् ॥
3.38.e: Call we on Indra, Maghavan, auspicious, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.39.d: इन्द्रं मतिर्हृद आ वच्यमानाच्छा पतिं स्तोमतष्टा जिगाति । या जागृविर्विदथे शस्यमानेन्द्र यत्ते जायते विद्धि तस्य ॥
3.39.e: To Indra from the heart the hymn proceedeth, to him the Lord, recited, built with praises;  The wakening song sung forth in holy synod: that which is born for thee, O Indra, notice.

3.39.d: दिवश्चिदा पूर्व्या जायमाना वि जागृविर्विदथे शस्यमाना । भद्रा वस्त्राण्यर्जुना वसाना सेयमस्मे सनजा पित्र्या धीः ॥
3.39.e: Born from the heaven e’en in the days aforetime, wakening, sting aloud in holy synod,  Auspicious, clad in white and shining raiment, this is the ancient hymn of our forefathers.

3.39.d: यमा चिदत्र यमसूरसूत जिह्वाया अग्रं पतदा ह्यस्थात् । वपूंषि जाता मिथुना सचेते तमोहना तपुषो बुध्न एता ॥
3.39.e: The Mother of the Twins hath borne Twin Children: my tongue's tip raised itself and rested silent.  Killing the darkness at the light's foundation, the Couple newly born attain their beauty.

3.39.d: नकिरेषां निन्दिता मर्त्येषु ये अस्माकं पितरो गोषु योधाः । इन्द्र एषां दृंहिता माहिनावानुद्गोत्राणि ससृजे दंसनावान् ॥
3.39.e: Not one is found among them, none of mortals, to blame our sires who fought to win the cattle.  Their strengthener was Indra the Majestic he spread their stalls of kine the Wonder-Worker.

3.39.d: सखा ह यत्र सखिभिर्नवग्वैरभिज्ञ्वा सत्वभिर्गा अनुग्मन् । सत्यं तदिन्द्रो दशभिर्दशग्वैः सूर्यं विवेद तमसि क्षियन्तम् ॥
3.39.e: Where as a Friend with friendly men, Navagvas, with heroes, on his knees he sought the cattle.  There, verily with ten Daśagvas Indra found the Sun lying hidden in the darkness.

3.39.d: इन्द्रो मधु सम्भृतमुस्रियायां पद्वद्विवेद शफवन्नमे गोः । गुहा हितं गुह्यं गूळ्हमप्सु हस्ते दधे दक्षिणे दक्षिणावान् ॥
3.39.e: Indra found meath collected in the milch-cow, by foot and hoof, in the cow's place of pasture.  That which lay secret, hidden in the waters, he held in his right hand, the rich rewarder.

3.39.d: ज्योतिर्वृणीत तमसो विजानन्नारे स्याम दुरितादभीके । इमा गिरः सोमपाः सोमवृद्ध जुषस्वेन्द्र पुरुतमस्य कारोः ॥
3.39.e: He took the light, discerning it from darkness: may we be far removed from all misfortune.  These songs, O Soma-drinker, cheered by Soma, Indra, accept from thy most zealous poet.

3.39.d: ज्योतिर्यज्ञाय रोदसी अनु ष्यादारे स्याम दुरितस्य भूरेः । भूरि चिद्धि तुजतो मर्त्यस्य सुपारासो वसवो बर्हणावत् ॥
3.39.e: Let there be light through both the worlds for worship: may we be far from most overwhelming evil.  Great woe comes even from the hostile mortal, piled up; but good at rescue are the Vasus.

3.39.d: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिन्द्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ । शृण्वन्तमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नन्तं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानाम् ॥
3.39.e: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered,  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.40.d: इन्द्र त्वा वृषभं वयं सुते सोमे हवामहे । स पाहि मध्वो अन्धसः ॥
3.40.e: THEE, Indra, we invoke, the Bull, what time the Soma is expressed.  So drink thou of the savoury juice.

3.40.d: इन्द्र क्रतुविदं सुतं सोमं हर्य पुरुष्टुत । पिबा वृषस्व तातृपिम् ॥
3.40.e: Indra, whom many laud, accept the strength-conferring Soma juice:  Quaff, pour down drink that satisfies.

3.40.d: इन्द्र प्र णो धितावानं यज्ञं विश्वेभिर्देवेभिः । तिर स्तवान विश्पते ॥
3.40.e: Indra, with all the Gods promote our wealth-bestowing sacrifice,  Thou highly-lauded Lord of men.

3.40.d: इन्द्र सोमाः सुता इमे तव प्र यन्ति सत्पते । क्षयं चन्द्रास इन्दवः ॥
3.40.e: Lord of the brave, to thee proceed these drops of Soma juice expressed,  The bright drops to thy dwelling-place.

3.40.d: दधिष्वा जठरे सुतं सोममिन्द्र वरेण्यम् । तव द्युक्षास इन्दवः ॥
3.40.e: Within thy belly, Indra, take juice, Soma the most excellent: Thine are the drops celestial.

3.40.d: गिर्वणः पाहि नः सुतं मधोर्धाराभिरज्यसे । इन्द्र त्वादातमिद्यशः ॥
3.40.e: Drink our libation, Lord of hymns: with streams of meath thou art bedewed  Our glory, Indra, is thy gift.

3.40.d: अभि द्युम्नानि वनिन इन्द्रं सचन्ते अक्षिता । पीत्वी सोमस्य वावृधे ॥
3.40.e: To Indra go the treasures of the worshipper, which never fail:  He drinks the Soma and is strong

3.40.d: अर्वावतो न आ गहि परावतश्च वृत्रहन् । इमा जुषस्व नो गिरः ॥
3.40.e: From far away, from near at hand, O Vṛtra-slayer, come to us:  Accept the songs we sing to thee.

3.40.d: यदन्तरा परावतमर्वावतं च हूयसे । इन्द्रेह तत आ गहि ॥
3.40.e: When from the space between the near and far thou art invoked by us,  Thence, Indra. come thou hitherward.

3.41.d: आ तू न इन्द्र मद्र्यग्घुवानः सोमपीतये । हरिभ्यां याह्यद्रिवः ॥
3.41.e: INVOKED to drink the Soma juice, come with thy Bay Steeds, Thunder-armed  Come, Indra, hitherward to me.

3.41.d: सत्तो होता न ऋत्वियस्तिस्तिरे बर्हिरानुषक् । अयुज्रन्प्रातरद्रयः ॥
3.41.e: Our priest is seated, true to time; the grass is regularly strewn;  The pressing-stones were set at morn.

3.41.d: इमा ब्रह्म ब्रह्मवाहः क्रियन्त आ बर्हिः सीद । वीहि शूर पुरोळाशम् ॥
3.41.e: These prayers, O thou who hearest prayer are offered: seat thee on the grass.  Hero, enjoy the offered cake.

3.41.d: रारन्धि सवनेषु ण एषु स्तोमेषु वृत्रहन् । उक्थेष्विन्द्र गिर्वणः ॥
3.41.e: O Vṛtra-slayer, be thou pleased with these libations, with these hymns,  Song-loving Indra, with our lauds.

3.41.d: मतयः सोमपामुरुं रिहन्ति शवसस्पतिम् । इन्द्रं वत्सं न मातरः ॥
3.41.e: Our hymns caress the Lord of Strength, vast, drinker of the Soma's juice,  Indra, as mother-cows their calf.

3.41.d: स मन्दस्वा ह्यन्धसो राधसे तन्वा महे । न स्तोतारं निदे करः ॥
3.41.e: Delight thee with the juice we pour for thine own great munificence:  Yield not thy singer to reproach.

3.41.d: वयमिन्द्र त्वायवो हविष्मन्तो जरामहे । उत त्वमस्मयुर्वसो ॥
3.41.e: We, Indra, dearly loving thee, bearing oblation, sing thee hymns  Thou, Vasu, dearly lovest us.

3.41.d: मारे अस्मद्वि मुमुचो हरिप्रियार्वाङ्याहि । इन्द्र स्वधावो मत्स्वेह ॥
3.41.e: O thou to whom thy Bays are dear, loose not thy Horses far from us:  Here glad thee, Indra, Lord divine.

3.41.d: अर्वाञ्चं त्वा सुखे रथे वहतामिन्द्र केशिना । घृतस्नू बर्हिरासदे ॥
3.41.e: May long-maned Coursers, dropping oil, bring thee on swift car hitherward,  Indra, to seat thee on the grass.

3.42.d: उप नः सुतमा गहि सोममिन्द्र गवाशिरम् । हरिभ्यां यस्ते अस्मयुः ॥
3.42.e: COME to the juice that we have pressed, to Soma, Indra, bleat with milk:  Come, favouring us, thy Bay-drawn car!

3.42.d: तमिन्द्र मदमा गहि बर्हिःष्ठां ग्रावभिः सुतम् । कुविन्न्वस्य तृप्णवः ॥
3.42.e: Come, Indra, to this gladdening drink, placed on the grass, pressed out with stones:  Wilt thou not drink thy fill thereof?

3.42.d: इन्द्रमित्था गिरो ममाच्छागुरिषिता इतः । आवृते सोमपीतये ॥
3.42.e: To Indra have my songs of praise gone forth, thus rapidly sent hence,  To turn him to the Soma-draught.

3.42.d: इन्द्रं सोमस्य पीतये स्तोमैरिह हवामहे । उक्थेभिः कुविदागमत् ॥
3.42.e: Hither with songs of praise we call Indra to drink the Soma juice:  Will he not come to us by lauds?

3.42.d: इन्द्र सोमाः सुता इमे तान्दधिष्व शतक्रतो । जठरे वाजिनीवसो ॥
3.42.e: Indra, these Somas are expressed. Take them within thy belly, Lord  Of Hundred Powers, thou Prince of Wealth.

3.42.d: विद्मा हि त्वा धनंजयं वाजेषु दधृषं कवे । अधा ते सुम्नमीमहे ॥
3.42.e: We know thee winner of the spoil, and resolute in battles, Sage!  Therefore thy blessing we implore.

3.42.d: इममिन्द्र गवाशिरं यवाशिरं च नः पिब । आगत्या वृषभिः सुतम् ॥
3.42.e: Borne hither by thy Stallions, drink, Indra, this juice which we have pressed,  Mingled with barley and with milk.

3.42.d: तुभ्येदिन्द्र स्व ओक्ये३ सोमं चोदामि पीतये । एष रारन्तु ते हृदि ॥
3.42.e: Indra, for thee, in thine own place, I urge the Soma for thy draught:  Deep in thy heart let it remain,

3.42.d: त्वां सुतस्य पीतये प्रत्नमिन्द्र हवामहे । कुशिकासो अवस्यवः ॥
3.42.e: We call on thee, the Ancient One, Indra, to drink the Soma juice,  We Kuśikas who seek thine aid.

3.43.d: आ याह्यर्वाङुप वन्धुरेष्ठास्तवेदनु प्रदिवः सोमपेयम् । प्रिया सखाया वि मुचोप बर्हिस्त्वामिमे हव्यवाहो हवन्ते ॥
3.43.e: MOUNTED upon thy chariot-seat approach us: thine is the Soma-draught from days aforetime.  Loose for the sacred grass thy dear companions. These men who bring oblation call thee hither.

3.43.d: आ याहि पूर्वीरति चर्षणीराँ अर्य आशिष उप नो हरिभ्याम् । इमा हि त्वा मतयः स्तोमतष्टा इन्द्र हवन्ते सख्यं जुषाणाः ॥
3.43.e: Come our true Friend, passing by many people; come with thy two Bay Steeds to our devotions;  For these our hymns are calling thee, O Indra, hymns formed for praise, soliciting thy friendship.

3.43.d: आ नो यज्ञं नमोवृधं सजोषा इन्द्र देव हरिभिर्याहि तूयम् । अहं हि त्वा मतिभिर्जोहवीमि घृतप्रयाः सधमादे मधूनाम् ॥
3.43.e: Pleased, with thy Bay Steeds, Indra, God, come quickly to this our sacrifice that heightens worship;  For with my thoughts, presenting oil to feed thee, I call thee to the feast of sweet libations.

3.43.d: आ च त्वामेता वृषणा वहातो हरी सखाया सुधुरा स्वङ्गा । धानावदिन्द्रः सवनं जुषाणः सखा सख्युः शृणवद्वन्दनानि ॥
3.43.e: Yea, let thy two Bay Stallions bear thee hither, well limbed and good to draw, thy dear companions.  Pleased with the corn-blent offering which we bring thee, may Indra, Friend, hear his friend's adoration.

3.43.d: कुविन्मा गोपां करसे जनस्य कुविद्राजानं मघवन्नृजीषिन् । कुविन्म ऋषिं पपिवांसं सुतस्य कुविन्मे वस्वो अमृतस्य शिक्षाः ॥
3.43.e: Wilt thou not make me guardian of the people, make me, impetuous Maghavan, their ruler?  Make me a Ṛṣi having drunk of Soma? Wilt thou not give me wealth that lasts for ever?

3.43.d: आ त्वा बृहन्तो हरयो युजाना अर्वागिन्द्र सधमादो वहन्तु । प्र ये द्विता दिव ऋञ्जन्त्याताः सुसम्मृष्टासो वृषभस्य मूराः ॥
3.43.e: Yoked to thy chariot, led thy tall Bays, Indra, companions of thy banquet, bear thee hither,  Who from of old press to heaven's farthest limits, the Bull's impetuous and well-groomed Horses.

3.43.d: इन्द्र पिब वृषधूतस्य वृष्ण आ यं ते श्येन उशते जभार । यस्य मदे च्यावयसि प्र कृष्टीर्यस्य मदे अप गोत्रा ववर्थ ॥
3.43.e: Drink of the strong pressed out by strong ones, Indra, that which the Falcon brought thee when thou longedst;  In whose wild joy thou stirrest up the people, in whose wild joy thou didst unbar the cow-stalls.

3.43.d: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिन्द्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ । शृण्वन्तमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नन्तं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानाम् ॥
3.43.e: Call we on Indra, Makhavan, auspicious, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered;  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.44.d: अयं ते अस्तु हर्यतः सोम आ हरिभिः सुतः । जुषाण इन्द्र हरिभिर्न आ गह्या तिष्ठ हरितं रथम् ॥
3.44.e: May this delightsome Soma be expressed for thee by tawny stones.  Joying thereat, O Indra, with thy Bay Steeds come:. ascend thy golden-coloured car.

3.44.d: हर्यन्नुषसमर्चयः सूर्यं हर्यन्नरोचयः । विद्वाँश्चिकित्वान्हर्यश्व वर्धस इन्द्र विश्वा अभि श्रियः ॥
3.44.e: In love thou madest Uṣas glow, in love thou madest Sūrya shine.  Thou, Indra, knowing, thinking, Lord of Tawny Steeds, above all glories waxest great.

3.44.d: द्यामिन्द्रो हरिधायसं पृथिवीं हरिवर्पसम् । अधारयद्धरितोर्भूरि भोजनं ययोरन्तर्हरिश्चरत् ॥
3.44.e: The heaven with streams of golden hue, earth with her tints of green and gold-  The golden Pair yield Indra plenteous nourishment: between them moves the golden One.

3.44.d: जज्ञानो हरितो वृषा विश्वमा भाति रोचनम् । हर्यश्वो हरितं धत्त आयुधमा वज्रं बाह्वोर्हरिम् ॥
3.44.e: When born to life the golden Bull illumines all the realm of light.  He takes his golden weapon, Lord of Tawny Steeds, the golden thunder in his arms.

3.44.d: इन्द्रो हर्यन्तमर्जुनं वज्रं शुक्रैरभीवृतम् । अपावृणोद्धरिभिरद्रिभिः सुतमुद्गा हरिभिराजत ॥
3.44.e: The bright, the well-loved thunderbolt, girt with the bright, Indra disclosed,  Disclosed the Soma juice pressed out by tawny stones, with tawny steeds drave forth the kine.

3.45.d: आ मन्द्रैरिन्द्र हरिभिर्याहि मयूररोमभिः । मा त्वा के चिन्नि यमन्विं न पाशिनोऽति धन्वेव ताँ इहि ॥
3.45.e: COME hither, Indra, with Bay Steeds, joyous, with tails like peacocks' plumes.  Let no men cheek thy course as fowlers stay the bird: pass o’er them as o’er desert lands.

3.45.d: वृत्रखादो वलंरुजः पुरां दर्मो अपामजः । स्थाता रथस्य हर्योरभिस्वर इन्द्रो दृळ्हा चिदारुजः ॥
3.45.e: He who slew Vṛtra, burst the cloud, brake the strongholds and drave the floods,  Indra who mounts his chariot at his Bay Steeds' cry, shatters e’en things that stand most firm.

3.45.d: गम्भीराँ उदधीँरिव क्रतुं पुष्यसि गा इव । प्र सुगोपा यवसं धेनवो यथा ह्रदं कुल्या इवाशत ॥
3.45.e: Like pools of water deep and full, like kine thou cherishest thy might;  Like the milch-cows that go well-guarded to the mead, like water-brooks that reach the lake.

3.45.d: आ नस्तुजं रयिं भरांशं न प्रतिजानते । वृक्षं पक्वं फलमङ्कीव धूनुहीन्द्र सम्पारणं वसु ॥
3.45.e: Bring thou us wealth with power to strike, our share, 'gainst him who calls it his.  Shake, Indra, as with hooks, the tree for ripened fruit, for wealth to satisfy our wish.

3.45.d: स्वयुरिन्द्र स्वराळसि स्मद्दिष्टिः स्वयशस्तरः । स वावृधान ओजसा पुरुष्टुत भवा नः सुश्रवस्तमः ॥
3.45.e: Indra, self-ruling Lord art thou, good Leader, of most glorious fame.  So, waxen in thy strength, O thou whom many praise, be thou most swift to hear our call.

3.46.d: युध्मस्य ते वृषभस्य स्वराज उग्रस्य यूनः स्थविरस्य घृष्वेः । अजूर्यतो वज्रिणो वीर्या३णीन्द्र श्रुतस्य महतो महानि ॥
3.46.e: OF thee, the Bull, the Warrior, Sovran Ruler, joyous and fierce, ancient and ever youthful,  The undecaying One who wields the thunder, renowned and great, great are the exploits, Indra.

3.46.d: महाँ असि महिष वृष्ण्येभिर्धनस्पृदुग्र सहमानो अन्यान् । एको विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा स योधया च क्षयया च जनान् ॥
3.46.e: Great art thou, Mighty Lord, through manly vigour, O fierce One, gathering spoil, subduing others,  Thyself alone the universe's Sovran: so send forth men to combat and to rest them.

3.46.d: प्र मात्राभी रिरिचे रोचमानः प्र देवेभिर्विश्वतो अप्रतीतः । प्र मज्मना दिव इन्द्रः पृथिव्याः प्रोरोर्महो अन्तरिक्षादृजीषी ॥
3.46.e: He hath surpassed all measure in his brightness, yea, and the Gods, for none may be his equal.  Impetuous Indra in his might cxccedcth wide vast mid-air and heaven and earth together.

3.46.d: उरुं गभीरं जनुषाभ्यु१ग्रं विश्वव्यचसमवतं मतीनाम् । इन्द्रं सोमासः प्रदिवि सुतासः समुद्रं न स्रवत आ विशन्ति ॥
3.46.e: To Indra, even as rivers to the ocean, flow forth from days of old the Soma juices;  To him wide deep and mighty from his birth-time, the well of holy thoughts, aIl-comprehending.

3.46.d: यं सोममिन्द्र पृथिवीद्यावा गर्भं न माता बिभृतस्त्वाया । तं ते हिन्वन्ति तमु ते मृजन्त्यध्वर्यवो वृषभ पातवा उ ॥
3.46.e: The Soma, Indra, which the earth and heaven bear for thee as a mother bears her infant,  This they send forth to thee, this, vigorous Hero! Adhvaryus purify for thee to drink of.

3.47.d: मरुत्वाँ इन्द्र वृषभो रणाय पिबा सोममनुष्वधं मदाय । आ सिञ्चस्व जठरे मध्व ऊर्मिं त्वं राजासि प्रदिवः सुतानाम् ॥
3.47.e: DRINK, Indra, Marut-girt, as Bull, the Soma, for joy, for rapture even as thou listest.  Pour down the flood of meath within thy belly: thou from of old art King of Soma juices.

3.47.d: सजोषा इन्द्र सगणो मरुद्भिः सोमं पिब वृत्रहा शूर विद्वान् । जहि शत्रूँरप मृधो नुदस्वाथाभयं कृणुहि विश्वतो नः ॥
3.47.e: Indra, accordant, with the banded Maruts, drink Soma, Hero, as wise Vṛtra-slayer.  Slay thou our foemen, drive away assailants and make us safe on every side from danger.

3.47.d: उत ऋतुभिर्ऋतुपाः पाहि सोममिन्द्र देवेभिः सखिभिः सुतं नः । याँ आभजो मरुतो ये त्वान्वहन्वृत्रमदधुस्तुभ्यमोजः ॥
3.47.e: And, drinker at due seasons, drink in season, Indra, with friendly Gods, our pressed-out Soma.  The Maruts following, whom thou madest sharers, gave thee the victory, and thou slewest Vṛtra.

3.47.d: ये त्वाहिहत्ये मघवन्नवर्धन्ये शाम्बरे हरिवो ये गविष्टौ । ये त्वा नूनमनुमदन्ति विप्राः पिबेन्द्र सोमं सगणो मरुद्भिः ॥
3.47.e: Drink Soma, Indra, banded with the Maruts who, Maghavan, strengthened thee at Ahi's slaughter,  'Gainst Śambara, Lord of Bays! in winning cattle, and now rejoice in thee, the holy Singers.

3.47.d: मरुत्वन्तं वृषभं वावृधानमकवारिं दिव्यं शासमिन्द्रम् । विश्वासाहमवसे नूतनायोग्रं सहोदामिह तं हुवेम ॥
3.47.e: The Bull whose strength hath waxed, whom Maruts follow, free-giving Indra, the celestial Ruler,  Mighty, all-conquering, the victory-giver, him let us call to grant us new protection.

3.48.d: सद्यो ह जातो वृषभः कनीनः प्रभर्तुमावदन्धसः सुतस्य । साधोः पिब प्रतिकामं यथा ते रसाशिरः प्रथमं सोम्यस्य ॥
3.48.e: SOON as the young Bull sprang into existence he longed to taste the pressed-out Soma's liquor.  Drink thou thy fill, according to thy longing, first, of the goodly mixture blent with Soma.

3.48.d: यज्जायथास्तदहरस्य कामेंऽशोः पीयूषमपिबो गिरिष्ठाम् । तं ते माता परि योषा जनित्री महः पितुर्दम आसिञ्चदग्रे ॥
3.48.e: That day when thou wast born thou, fain to taste it, drankest the plant's milk which the mountains nourish.  That milk thy Mother first, the Dame who bare thee, poured for thee in thy mighty Father's dwelling.

3.48.d: उपस्थाय मातरमन्नमैट्ट तिग्ममपश्यदभि सोममूधः । प्रयावयन्नचरद्गृत्सो अन्यान्महानि चक्रे पुरुधप्रतीकः ॥
3.48.e: Desiring food he came unto his Mother, and on her breast beheld the pungent Soma.  Wise, he moved on, keeping aloof the others, and wrought great exploits in his varied aspects.

3.48.d: उग्रस्तुराषाळभिभूत्योजा यथावशं तन्वं चक्र एषः । त्वष्टारमिन्द्रो जनुषाभिभूयामुष्या सोममपिबच्चमूषु ॥
3.48.e: Fierce, quickly conquering, of surpassing vigour, he framed his body even as he listed.  E’en from his birth-time Indra conquered Tvaṣṭar, bore off the Soma and in beakers drank it.

3.48.d: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिन्द्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ । शृण्वन्तमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नन्तं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानाम् ॥
3.48.e: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered;  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.49.d: शंसा महामिन्द्रं यस्मिन्विश्वा आ कृष्टयः सोमपाः काममव्यन् । यं सुक्रतुं धिषणे विभ्वतष्टं घनं वृत्राणां जनयन्त देवाः ॥
3.49.e: GREAT Indra will I laud, in whom all people who drink the Soma have attained their longing;  Whom, passing wise, Gods, Heaven and Earth, engendered, formed by a Master's hand, to crush the Vṛtras.

3.49.d: यं नु नकिः पृतनासु स्वराजं द्विता तरति नृतमं हरिष्ठाम् । इनतमः सत्वभिर्यो ह शूषैः पृथुज्रया अमिनादायुर्दस्योः ॥
3.49.e: Whom, most heroic, borne by Tawny Coursers, verily none subdueth in the battle;  Who, reaching far, most vigorous, hath shortened the Dasyu's life with Warriors bold of spirit.

3.49.d: सहावा पृत्सु तरणिर्नार्वा व्यानशी रोदसी मेहनावान् । भगो न कारे हव्यो मतीनां पितेव चारुः सुहवो वयोधाः ॥
3.49.e: Victor in fight, swift mover like a warhorse, pervading both worlds, rainer down of blessings,  To he invoked in war like Bhaga, Father, as ’twere, of hymns, fair, prompt to hear, strength-giver.

3.49.d: धर्ता दिवो रजसस्पृष्ट ऊर्ध्वो रथो न वायुर्वसुभिर्नियुत्वान् । क्षपां वस्ता जनिता सूर्यस्य विभक्ता भागं धिषणेव वाजम् ॥
3.49.e: Supporting heaven, the high back of the region, his car is Vāyu with his team of Vasus.  Illumining the nights, the Sun's creator, like Dhiṣaṇā he deals forth strength and riches.

3.49.d: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिन्द्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ । शृण्वन्तमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नन्तं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानाम् ॥
3.49.e: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered;  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers treasure.

3.50.d: इन्द्रः स्वाहा पिबतु यस्य सोम आगत्या तुम्रो वृषभो मरुत्वान् । ओरुव्यचाः पृणतामेभिरन्नैरास्य हविस्तन्व१ः काममृध्याः ॥
3.50.e: LET Indra drink, All-hail! for his is Soma,—the mighty Bull come, girt by Maruts, hither.  Far-reaching, let him fill him with these viands, and let our offering sate his body's longing.

3.50.d: आ ते सपर्यू जवसे युनज्मि ययोरनु प्रदिवः श्रुष्टिमावः । इह त्वा धेयुर्हरयः सुशिप्र पिबा त्व१स्य सुषुतस्य चारोः ॥
3.50.e: I yoke thy pair of trusty Steeds for swiftness, whose faithful service from of old thou lovest.  Here, fair of cheek! let thy Bay Coursers place thee: drink of this lovely welleffused libation.

3.50.d: गोभिर्मिमिक्षुं दधिरे सुपारमिन्द्रं ज्यैष्ठ्याय धायसे गृणानाः । मन्दानः सोमं पपिवाँ ऋजीषिन्त्समस्मभ्यं पुरुधा गा इषण्य ॥
3.50.e: With milk they made Indra their good Preserver, lauding for help and rule the bounteous rainer.  Impetuous God, when thou hast drunk the Soma, enraptured send us cattle in abundance.

3.50.d: इमं कामं मन्दया गोभिरश्वैश्चन्द्रवता राधसा पप्रथश्च । स्वर्यवो मतिभिस्तुभ्यं विप्रा इन्द्राय वाहः कुशिकासो अक्रन् ॥
3.50.e: With kine and horses satisfy this longing with very splendid bounty still extend it.  Seeking the light, with hymns to thee, O Indra, the Kuśikas have brought their gift, the singers.

3.50.d: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिन्द्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ । शृण्वन्तमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नन्तं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानाम् ॥
3.50.e: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in the fight where spoil is gathered;  The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

3.51.d: चर्षणीधृतं मघवानमुक्थ्य१मिन्द्रं गिरो बृहतीरभ्यनूषत । वावृधानं पुरुहूतं सुवृक्तिभिरमर्त्यं जरमाणं दिवेदिवे ॥
3.51.e: HIGH hymns have sounded forth the praise of Maghavan, supporter of mankind, of Indra meet for lauds;  Him who hath waxen great, invoked with beauteous songs, Immortal One, whose praise each day is sung aloud.

3.51.d: शतक्रतुमर्णवं शाकिनं नरं गिरो म इन्द्रमुप यन्ति विश्वतः । वाजसनिं पूर्भिदं तूर्णिमप्तुरं धामसाचमभिषाचं स्वर्विदम् ॥
3.51.e: To Indra from all sides go forth my songs of praise, the Lord of Hundred Powers, strong, Hero, like the sea,  Swift, winner of the booty, breaker-down of forts, faithful and ever-glorious, finder of the light.

3.51.d: आकरे वसोर्जरिता पनस्यतेऽनेहसः स्तुभ इन्द्रो दुवस्यति । विवस्वतः सदन आ हि पिप्रिये सत्रासाहमभिमातिहनं स्तुहि ॥
3.51.e: Where battle's spoil is piled the singer winneth praise, for Indra taketh care of matchless worshippers.  He in Vivasvān's dwelling findeth his delight: praise thou the ever-conquering slayer of the foe.

3.51.d: नृणामु त्वा नृतमं गीर्भिरुक्थैरभि प्र वीरमर्चता सबाधः । सं सहसे पुरुमायो जिहीते नमो अस्य प्रदिव एक ईशे ॥
3.51.e: Thee, valorous, most heroic of the heroes, shall the priests glorify with songg and praises.  Full of all wondrous power he goes to conquest: worship is his, sole Lord from days aforetime.

3.51.d: पूर्वीरस्य निष्षिधो मर्त्येषु पुरू वसूनि पृथिवी बिभर्ति । इन्द्राय द्याव ओषधीरुतापो रयिं रक्षन्ति जीरयो वनानि ॥
3.51.e: Abundant are the gifts he gives to mortals: for him the earth bears a rich store of treasures.  The heavens, the growing plants, the living waters, the forest trees preserve their wealth for Indra.

3.51.d: तुभ्यं ब्रह्माणि गिर इन्द्र तुभ्यं सत्रा दधिरे हरिवो जुषस्व । बोध्या३पिरवसो नूतनस्य सखे वसो जरितृभ्यो वयो धाः ॥
3.51.e: To thee, O Indra, Lord of Bays, for ever are offered prayers and songs: accept them gladly.  As Kinsman think thou of some fresh assistance; good Friend, give strength and life to those who praise thee.

3.51.d: इन्द्र मरुत्व इह पाहि सोमं यथा शार्याते अपिबः सुतस्य । तव प्रणीती तव शूर शर्मन्ना विवासन्ति कवयः सुयज्ञाः ॥
3.51.e: Here, Indra, drink thou Soma with the Maruts, as thou didst drink the juice beside Śāryāta.  Under thy guidance, in thy keeping, Hero, the singers serve, skilled in fair sacrifices.

3.51.d: स वावशान इह पाहि सोमं मरुद्भिरिन्द्र सखिभिः सुतं नः । जातं यत्त्वा परि देवा अभूषन्महे भराय पुरुहूत विश्वे ॥
3.51.e: So eagerly desirous drink the Soma, our juice, O Indra, with thy friends the Maruts,  Since at thy birth all Deities adorned thee for the great fight, O thou invoked of many.

3.51.d: अप्तूर्ये मरुत आपिरेषोऽमन्दन्निन्द्रमनु दातिवाराः । तेभिः साकं पिबतु वृत्रखादः सुतं सोमं दाशुषः स्वे सधस्थे ॥
3.51.e: He was your comrade in your zeal, O Maruts: they, rich in noble gifts, rejoiced in Indra.  With them together let the Vṛtra-slayer drink in his home the worshipper's libation.

3.51.d: इदं ह्यन्वोजसा सुतं राधानां पते । पिबा त्व१स्य गिर्वणः ॥
3.51.e: So, Lord of affluent gifts, this juice hath been pressed for thee with strength  Drink of it, thou who lovest song.

3.51.d: यस्ते अनु स्वधामसत्सुते नि यच्छ तन्वम् । स त्वा ममत्तु सोम्यम् ॥
3.51.e: Incline thy body to this juice which suits thy Godlike nature well:  May it cheer thee who lovest it.

3.51.d: प्र ते अश्नोतु कुक्ष्योः प्रेन्द्र ब्रह्मणा शिरः । प्र बाहू शूर राधसे ॥
3.51.e: Brave Indra, let it work through both thy flanks, and through thy head by prayer,  And through thine arms, to prosper us.

3.52.e: INDRA, accept at break of day our Soma mixt with roasted corn,  With groats with cake, with eulogies.

3.52.d: पुरोळाशं पचत्यं जुषस्वेन्द्रा गुरस्व च । तुभ्यं हव्यानि सिस्रते ॥
3.52.e: Accept, O Indra, and enjoy the well-dressed sacrificial cake: Oblations are poured forth to thee.

3.52.d: पुरोळाशं च नो घसो जोषयासे गिरश्च नः । वधूयुरिव योषणाम् ॥
3.52.e: Consume our sacrificial cake, accept the songs of praise we sing,  As he who woes accepts his bride.

3.52.d: पुरोळाशं सनश्रुत प्रातःसावे जुषस्व नः । इन्द्र क्रतुर्हि ते बृहन् ॥
3.52.e: Famed from of old, accept the cake at our libation poured at dawn,  Forgreat, O Indra, is thy power.

3.52.d: माध्यंदिनस्य सवनस्य धानाः पुरोळाशमिन्द्र कृष्वेह चारुम् । प्र यत्स्तोता जरिता तूर्ण्यर्थो वृषायमाण उप गीर्भिरीट्टे ॥
3.52.e: Let roasted corn of our midday libation, and sacrificial cake here please thee, Indra,  What time the lauding singer, keen of purpose and eager as a bull, with hymns implores thee.

3.52.d: तृतीये धानाः सवने पुरुष्टुत पुरोळाशमाहुतं मामहस्व नः । ऋभुमन्तं वाजवन्तं त्वा कवे प्रयस्वन्त उप शिक्षेम धीतिभिः ॥
3.52.e: At the third sacrifice, O thou whom many praise, give glory to the roasted corn and holy cake.  With offered viands and with songs may we assist thee, Sage, whom Vāja and the Ṛbhus wait upon.

3.52.d: पूषण्वते ते चकृमा करम्भं हरिवते हर्यश्वाय धानाः । अपूपमद्धि सगणो मरुद्भिः सोमं पिब वृत्रहा शूर विद्वान् ॥
3.52.e: The groats have we prepared for thee with Pūṣan, corn for thee, Lord of Bay Steeds, with thy horses.  Eat thou the meal-cake, banded with the Maruts, wise Hero, Vṛtra-slayer, drink the Soma.

3.52.d: प्रति धाना भरत तूयमस्मै पुरोळाशं वीरतमाय नृणाम् । दिवेदिवे सदृशीरिन्द्र तुभ्यं वर्धन्तु त्वा सोमपेयाय धृष्णो ॥
3.52.e: Bring forth the roasted corn to meet him quickly, cake for the bravest Hero mid the heroes.  Indra, may hymns accordant with thee daily strengthen thee, Bold One, for the draught of Soma.

3.53.d: इन्द्रापर्वता बृहता रथेन वामीरिष आ वहतं सुवीराः । वीतं हव्यान्यध्वरेषु देवा वर्धेथां गीर्भिरिळया मदन्ता ॥
3.53.e: ON a high car, O Parvata and Indra, bring pleasant viands, with brave heroes, hither.  Enjoy the gifts, Gods, at our sacrifices wax strong by hymns, rejoice in our oblation.

3.53.d: तिष्ठा सु कं मघवन्मा परा गाः सोमस्य नु त्वा सुषुतस्य यक्षि । पितुर्न पुत्रः सिचमा रभे त इन्द्र स्वादिष्ठया गिरा शचीवः ॥
3.53.e: Stay still, O Maghavan, advance no farther. a draught of well-pressed Soma will I give thee.  With sweetest song I grasp, O Mighty Indra, thy garment's hem as a child grasps his father's.

3.53.d: शंसावाध्वर्यो प्रति मे गृणीहीन्द्राय वाहः कृणवाव जुष्टम् । एदं बर्हिर्यजमानस्य सीदाथा च भूदुक्थमिन्द्राय शस्तम् ॥
3.53.e: Adhvaryu, sing we both; sing thou in answer: make we a laud acceptable to Indra.  Upon this sacrificer's grass he seated: to Indra shall our eulogy be uttered.

3.53.d: जायेदस्तं मघवन्त्सेदु योनिस्तदित्त्वा युक्ता हरयो वहन्तु । यदा कदा च सुनवाम सोममग्निष्ट्वा दूतो धन्वात्यच्छ ॥
3.53.e: A wife, O Maghavan is home and dwelling: so let thy Bay Steeds yoked convey thee hither.  Whenever we press out for thee the Soma, let Agni as our Herald speed to call thee.

3.53.d: परा याहि मघवन्ना च याहीन्द्र भ्रातरुभयत्रा ते अर्थम् । यत्रा रथस्य बृहतो निधानं विमोचनं वाजिनो रासभस्य ॥
3.53.e: Depart, O Maghavan;again come hither: both there and here thy goat is Indra, Brother,  Where thy tall chariot hath a place to rest in, and where thqu loosest thy loud-neighing Courser.

3.53.d: अपाः सोममस्तमिन्द्र प्र याहि कल्याणीर्जाया सुरणं गृहे ते । यत्रा रथस्य बृहतो निधानं विमोचनं वाजिनो दक्षिणावत् ॥
3.53.e: Thou hast drunk Soma, Indra, turn thee homeward; thy joy is in thy home, thy racious Consort;  Where thy tall chariot hath a place to rest in, and thy strong Courser is set free with guerdon.

3.53.d: इमे भोजा अङ्गिरसो विरूपा दिवस्पुत्रासो असुरस्य वीराः । विश्वामित्राय ददतो मघानि सहस्रसावे प्र तिरन्त आयुः ॥
3.53.e: Bounteous are these, Aṅgirases, Virupas: the Asura's Heroes and the Sons of Heaven.  They, giving store of wealth to Viśvāmitra, prolong his life through countless Soma-pressings.

3.53.d: रूपंरूपं मघवा बोभवीति मायाः कृण्वानस्तन्वं१ परि स्वाम् । त्रिर्यद्दिवः परि मुहूर्तमागात्स्वैर्मन्त्रैरनृतुपा ऋतावा ॥
3.53.e: Maghavan weareth every shape at pleasure, effecting magic changes in his body,  Holy One, drinker out of season, coming thrice, in a moment, through fit prayers, from heaven.

3.53.d: महाँ ऋषिर्देवजा देवजूतोऽस्तभ्नात्सिन्धुमर्णवं नृचक्षाः । विश्वामित्रो यदवहत्सुदासमप्रियायत कुशिकेभिरिन्द्रः ॥
3.53.e: The mighty sage, God-born and God-incited, who looks on men, restrained the billowy river.  When Viśvāmitra was Sudās's escort, then Indra through the Kuśikas grew friendly.

3.53.d: हंसा इव कृणुथ श्लोकमद्रिभिर्मदन्तो गीर्भिरध्वरे सुते सचा । देवेभिर्विप्रा ऋषयो नृचक्षसो वि पिबध्वं कुशिकाः सोम्यं मधु ॥
3.53.e: Like swans, prepare a song of praise with pressing-stones, glad in your hymns with juice poured forth in sacrifice.  Ye singers, with the Gods, sages who look on men, ye Kutikas drink up the Soma's savoury meath.

3.53.d: उप प्रेत कुशिकाश्चेतयध्वमश्वं राये प्र मुञ्चता सुदासः । राजा वृत्रं जङ्घनत्प्रागपागुदगथा यजाते वर आ पृथिव्याः ॥
3.53.e: Come forward, Kuśikas, and be attentive; let loose Sudās's horse to win him riches.  East, west, and north, let the King slay the foeman, then at earth's choicest place perform his worship.

3.53.d: य इमे रोदसी उभे अहमिन्द्रमतुष्टवम् । विश्वामित्रस्य रक्षति ब्रह्मेदं भारतं जनम् ॥
3.53.e: Praises to Indra have I sung, sustainer of this earth and heaven. This prayer of Viśvāmitra keeps secure the race of Bharatas.

3.53.d: विश्वामित्रा अरासत ब्रह्मेन्द्राय वज्रिणे । करदिन्नः सुराधसः ॥
3.53.e: The Viśvāmitras have sung forth this prayer to Indra Thunder-aimed:  So let him make us prosperous.

3.53.d: किं ते कृण्वन्ति कीकटेषु गावो नाशिरं दुह्रे न तपन्ति घर्मम् । आ नो भर प्रमगन्दस्य वेदो नैचाशाखं मघवन्रन्धया नः ॥
3.53.e: Among the Kikatas what do thy cattle? They pour no milky draught, they heat no caldron.  Bring thou to us the wealth of Pramaganda;give up to us, O Maghavan, the low-born.

3.53.d: ससर्परीरमतिं बाधमाना बृहन्मिमाय जमदग्निदत्ता । आ सूर्यस्य दुहिता ततान श्रवो देवेष्वमृतमजुर्यम् ॥
3.53.e: Sasarpari, the gift of Jamadagnis, hath lowed with mighty voice dispelling famine.  The Daughter of the Sun hath spread our glory among the Gods, imperishable, deathless.

3.53.d: ससर्परीरभरत्तूयमेभ्योऽधि श्रवः पाञ्चजन्यासु कृष्टिषु । सा पक्ष्या३ नव्यमायुर्दधाना यां मे पलस्तिजमदग्नयो ददुः ॥
3.53.e: Sasarpari brought glory speedily to these, over the generations of the Fivefold Race;  Daughter of Paksa, she bestows new vital power, she whom the ancient Jamadagnis gave to me.

3.53.d: स्थिरौ गावौ भवतां वीळुरक्षो मेषा वि वर्हि मा युगं वि शारि । इन्द्रः पातल्ये ददतां शरीतोररिष्टनेमे अभि नः सचस्व ॥
3.53.e: Strong be the pair of oxen, firm the axles, let not the pole slip nor the yoke be broken.  May Indra, keep the yoke-pins from decaying: attend us, thou whose fellies are uninjured.

3.53.d: बलं धेहि तनूषु नो बलमिन्द्रानळुत्सु नः । बलं तोकाय तनयाय जीवसे त्वं हि बलदा असि ॥
3.53.e: O Indra, give our bodies strength, strength to the bulls who draw the wains,  Strength to our seed and progeny that they may live, for thou art he who giveth strength.

3.53.d: अभि व्ययस्व खदिरस्य सारमोजो धेहि स्पन्दने शिंशपायाम् । अक्ष वीळो वीळित वीळयस्व मा यामादस्मादव जीहिपो नः ॥
3.53.e: Enclose thee in the heart of Khayar timber, in the car wrought of Sinsapa put firmness.  Show thyself strong, O Axle, fixed and strengthened: throw us not from the car whereon we travel.

3.53.d: अयमस्मान्वनस्पतिर्मा च हा मा च रीरिषत् । स्वस्त्या गृहेभ्य आवसा आ विमोचनात् ॥
3.53.e: Let not this sovran of the wood leave us forlorn or injure us.  Safe may we be until we reach our homes and rest us and unyoke.

3.53.d: इन्द्रोतिभिर्बहुलाभिर्नो अद्य याच्छ्रेष्ठाभिर्मघवञ्छूर जिन्व । यो नो द्वेष्ट्यधरः सस्पदीष्ट यमु द्विष्मस्तमु प्राणो जहातु ॥
3.53.e: With various aids this day come to us, Indra, with best aids speed us, Maghavan, thou Hero.  Let him who hatcth us fall headlong downward: him whom we hate let vital breath abandon.

3.53.d: परशुं चिद्वि तपति शिम्बलं चिद्वि वृश्चति । उखा चिदिन्द्र येषन्ती प्रयस्ता फेनमस्यति ॥
3.53.e: He heats his very axe, and then cuts a mere Semal blossom off.  O Indra, like a caldron cracked and seething, so he pours out foam.

3.53.d: न सायकस्य चिकिते जनासो लोधं नयन्ति पशु मन्यमानाः । नावाजिनं वाजिना हासयन्ति न गर्दभं पुरो अश्वान्नयन्ति ॥
3.53.e: Men notice not the arrow, O ye people; they bring the red beast deeming it a bullock.  A sluggish steed men run not with the courser, nor ever lead an ass before a charger.

3.53.d: इम इन्द्र भरतस्य पुत्रा अपपित्वं चिकितुर्न प्रपित्वम् । हिन्वन्त्यश्वमरणं न नित्यं ज्यावाजं परि णयन्त्याजौ ॥
3.53.e: These men, the sons of Bhārata, O Indra, regard not severance or close connexion.  They urge their own steed as it were another's, and take him, swift as the bow's string, to battle.

3.54.d: इमं महे विदथ्याय शूषं शश्वत्कृत्व ईड्याय प्र जभ्रुः । शृणोतु नो दम्येभिरनीकैः शृणोत्वग्निर्दिव्यैरजस्रः ॥
3.54.e: To him adorable, mighty, meet for synods, this strengthening hymn, unceasing, have they offered.  May Agni hear us with his homely splendours, hear us, Eternal One, with heavenly lustre.

3.54.d: महि महे दिवे अर्चा पृथिव्यै कामो म इच्छञ्चरति प्रजानन् । ययोर्ह स्तोमे विदथेषु देवाः सपर्यवो मादयन्ते सचायोः ॥
3.54.e: To mighty Heaven and Earth I sing forth loudly: my wish goes out desirous and well knowing  Both, at whose laud in synods, showing favour, the Gods rejoice them with the living mortal.

3.54.d: युवोर्ऋतं रोदसी सत्यमस्तु महे षु णः सुविताय प्र भूतम् । इदं दिवे नमो अग्ने पृथिव्यै सपर्यामि प्रयसा यामि रत्नम् ॥
3.54.e: O Heaven and Earth, may your great law he faithful: he ye our leaders for our high advantage.  To Heaven and Earth I offer this my homage, with food, O Agni, as I pray for riches.

3.54.d: उतो हि वां पूर्व्या आविविद्र ऋतावरी रोदसी सत्यवाचः । नरश्चिद्वां समिथे शूरसातौ ववन्दिरे पृथिवि वेविदानाः ॥
3.54.e: Yea, holy Heaven and Earth, the ancient sages whose word was ever true had power to find you;  And brave men in the fightwhere heroes conquer, O Earth, have known you well and paid you honour.

3.54.d: को अद्धा वेद क इह प्र वोचद्देवाँ अच्छा पथ्या३ का समेति । ददृश्र एषामवमा सदांसि परेषु या गुह्येषु व्रतेषु ॥
3.54.e: What pathway leadeth to the Gods? Who knoweth this of a truth, and who will now declare it?  Seen are their lowest dwelling-places only, but they are in remote and secret regions.

3.54.d: कविर्नृचक्षा अभि षीमचष्ट ऋतस्य योना विघृते मदन्ती । नाना चक्राते सदनं यथा वेः समानेन क्रतुना संविदाने ॥
3.54.e: The Sage who looketh on mankind hath viewed them bedewed, rejoicing in the seat of Order.  They make a home as for a bird, though parted, with one same will finding themselves together.

3.54.d: समान्या वियुते दूरेअन्ते ध्रुवे पदे तस्थतुर्जागरूके । उत स्वसारा युवती भवन्ती आदु ब्रुवाते मिथुनानि नाम ॥
3.54.e: Partners though parted, with far-distant limits, on one firm place both stand for ever watchful,  And, being young for evermore, as sisters, speak to each other names that are united.

3.54.d: विश्वेदेते जनिमा सं विविक्तो महो देवान्बिभ्रती न व्यथेते । एजद्ध्रुवं पत्यते विश्वमेकं चरत्पतत्रि विषुणं वि जातम् ॥
3.54.e: All living things they part and keep asunder; though bearing up the mighty Gods they reel not.  One All is Lord of what is fixed and moving, that walks, that flies, this multiform creation.

3.54.d: सना पुराणमध्येम्यारान्महः पितुर्जनितुर्जामि तन्नः । देवासो यत्र पनितार एवैरुरौ पथि व्युते तस्थुरन्तः ॥
3.54.e: Afar the Ancient from of old I ponder, our kinship with our mighty Sire and Father,—  Singing the praise whereof the Gods by custom stand on the spacious far-extended pathway.

3.54.d: इमं स्तोमं रोदसी प्र ब्रवीम्यृदूदराः शृणवन्नग्निजिह्वाः । मित्रः सम्राजो वरुणो युवान आदित्यासः कवयः पप्रथानाः ॥
3.54.e: This laud, O Heaven and Earth, to you I utter: let the kind-hearted hear, whose tongue is Agni,  Young, Sovran Rulers, Varuṇa and Mitra, the wise and very glorious Ādityas.

3.54.d: हिरण्यपाणिः सविता सुजिह्वस्त्रिरा दिवो विदथे पत्यमानः । देवेषु च सवितः श्लोकमश्रेरादस्मभ्यमा सुव सर्वतातिम् ॥
3.54.e: The fair-tongued Savitar, the golden-handed, comes thrice from heaven as Lord in our assembly.  Bear to the Gods this song of praise, and send us, then, Savitar, complete and perfect safety.

3.54.d: सुकृत्सुपाणिः स्ववाँ ऋतावा देवस्त्वष्टावसे तानि नो धात् । पूषण्वन्त ऋभवो मादयध्वमूर्ध्वग्रावाणो अध्वरमतष्ट ॥
3.54.e: Deft worker, skiful-handed, helpful, holy, may Tvaṣṭar, God, give us these things to aid us,  Take your delight, Ye Ṛbhus joined with Pūṣan: ye have prepared the rite with stones adjusted.

3.54.d: विद्युद्रथा मरुत ऋष्टिमन्तो दिवो मर्या ऋतजाता अयासः । सरस्वती शृणवन्यज्ञियासो धाता रयिं सहवीरं तुरासः ॥
3.54.e: Borne on their flashing car, the spear-armed Maruts, the nimble Youths of Heaven, the Sons of Order,  The Holy, and Sarasvatī, shall hear us: ye Mighty, give us wealth with noble offspring.

3.54.d: विष्णुं स्तोमासः पुरुदस्ममर्का भगस्येव कारिणो यामनि ग्मन् । उरुक्रमः ककुहो यस्य पूर्वीर्न मर्धन्ति युवतयो जनित्रीः ॥
3.54.e: To Viṣṇu rich in marvels, songs And praises shall go as singers on the road of Bhaga,—  The Chieftain of the Mighty Stride, whose Mothers, the many young Dames, never disregard him.

3.54.d: इन्द्रो विश्वैर्वीर्यै३ः पत्यमान उभे आ पप्रौ रोदसी महित्वा । पुरंदरो वृत्रहा धृष्णुषेणः संगृभ्या न आ भरा भूरि पश्वः ॥
3.54.e: Indra, who rules through all his powers heroic, hath with his majesty filled earth and heaven.  Lord of brave hosts, Fort-crusher, Vṛtra-slayer, gather thou up and bring us store of cattle.

3.54.d: नासत्या मे पितरा बन्धुपृच्छा सजात्यमश्विनोश्चारु नाम । युवं हि स्थो रयिदौ नो रयीणां दात्रं रक्षेथे अकवैरदब्धा ॥
3.54.e: My Sires are the Nāsatyas, kind tokinsmen: the Aśvins' kinship is a glorious title.  For ye are they who give us store of riches: ye guard your gift uncheated by the bounteous.

3.54.d: महत्तद्वः कवयश्चारु नाम यद्ध देवा भवथ विश्व इन्द्रे । सख ऋभुभिः पुरुहूत प्रियेभिरिमां धियं सातये तक्षता नः ॥
3.54.e: This is, ye Wise, your great and glorious title, that all ye Deities abide in Indra.  Friend, Much-invoked! art thou with thy dear Ṛbhus: fashion ye this our hymn for our advantage.

3.54.d: अर्यमा णो अदितिर्यज्ञियासोऽदब्धानि वरुणस्य व्रतानि । युयोत नो अनपत्यानि गन्तोः प्रजावान्नः पशुमाँ अस्तु गातुः ॥
3.54.e: Aryaman, Aditi deserve our worship: the laws of Varuṇa remain unbroken.  The lot of childlessness remove ye from us, and let our course be rich in kine and offspring.

3.54.d: देवानां दूतः पुरुध प्रसूतोऽनागान्नो वोचतु सर्वताता । शृणोतु नः पृथिवी द्यौरुतापः सूर्यो नक्षत्रैरुर्व१न्तरिक्षम् ॥
3.54.e: May the Gods’ envoy, sent to many a quarter, proclaim us sinless for our perfect safety.  May Earth and Heaven, the Sun, the waters, hear us, and the wide firmament and constellations.

3.54.d: शृण्वन्तु नो वृषणः पर्वतासो ध्रुवक्षेमास इळया मदन्तः । आदित्यैर्नो अदितिः शृणोतु यच्छन्तु नो मरुतः शर्म भद्रम् ॥
3.54.e: Hear us the mouatains which distil the rain-drops, and, resting firm, rejoice in freshening moisture.  May Aditi with the Ādityas hear us, and Maruts grant us their auspicious shelter.

3.54.d: सदा सुगः पितुमाँ अस्तु पन्था मध्वा देवा ओषधीः सं पिपृक्त । भगो मे अग्ने सख्ये न मृध्या उद्रायो अश्यां सदनं पुरुक्षोः ॥
3.54.e: Soft be our path for ever, well-provisioned: with pleasant meath, O Gods, the herbs besprinkle.  Safe be my bliss, O Agni, in thy friendship: may I attain the seat of foodful. riches,

3.54.d: स्वदस्व हव्या समिषो दिदीह्यस्मद्र्य१क्सं मिमीहि श्रवांसि । विश्वाँ अग्ने पृत्सु ताञ्जेषि शत्रूनहा विश्वा सुमना दीदिही नः ॥
3.54.e: Enjoy the offering: beam thou strength upon us; combine thou for our good all kinds of glory.  Conquer in battle, Agni, all those foemen, and light us every day with loving kindness.

3.55.d: उषसः पूर्वा अध यद्व्यूषुर्महद्वि जज्ञे अक्षरं पदे गोः । व्रता देवानामुप नु प्रभूषन्महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: AT the first shining of the earliest Mornings, in the Cow's home was born the Great Eternal.  Now shall the statutes of the Gods be valid. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion -

3.55.d: मो षू णो अत्र जुहुरन्त देवा मा पूर्वे अग्ने पितरः पदज्ञाः । पुराण्योः सद्मनोः केतुरन्तर्महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Let not the Gods here injure us, O Agni, nor Fathers of old time who know the region,  Nor the sign set between two ancient dwellings. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: वि मे पुरुत्रा पतयन्ति कामाः शम्यच्छा दीद्ये पूर्व्याणि । समिद्धे अग्नावृतमिद्वदेम महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: My wishes fly abroad to many places: I glance back to the ancient sacrifices.  Let us declare the truth when fire is kindled. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: समानो राजा विभृतः पुरुत्रा शये शयासु प्रयुतो वनानु । अन्या वत्सं भरति क्षेति माता महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: King Universal, born to sundry quarters, extended through the wood be lies on couches.  One Mother rests: another feeds the Infant. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: आक्षित्पूर्वास्वपरा अनूरुत्सद्यो जातासु तरुणीष्वन्तः । अन्तर्वतीः सुवते अप्रवीता महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Lodged in old plants, he grows again in younger, swiftly within the newly-born and tender.  Though they are unimpregned, he makes them fruitful. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: शयुः परस्तादध नु द्विमाताबन्धनश्चरति वत्स एकः । मित्रस्य ता वरुणस्य व्रतानि महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Now lying far away, Child of two Mothers, he wanders unrestrained, the single youngling.  These are the laws of Varuṇa and Mitra. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: द्विमाता होता विदथेषु सम्राळन्वग्रं चरति क्षेति बुध्नः । प्र रण्यानि रण्यवाचो भरन्ते महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Child of two Mothers, Priest, sole Lord in synods, he still precedes while resting as foundation.  They who speak sweetly bring him sweet addresses. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: शूरस्येव युध्यतो अन्तमस्य प्रतीचीनं ददृशे विश्वमायत् । अन्तर्मतिश्चरति निष्षिधं गोर्महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: As to a friendly warrior when he battles, each thing that comes anear is seen to meet him.  The hymn commingles with the cow's oblation. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: नि वेवेति पलितो दूत आस्वन्तर्महाँश्चरति रोचनेन । वपूंषि बिभ्रदभि नो वि चष्टे महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Deep within these the hoary envoy pierceth; mighty, he goeth to the realm of splendour,  And looketh on us, clad in wondrous beauty. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: विष्णुर्गोपाः परमं पाति पाथः प्रिया धामान्यमृता दधानः । अग्निष्टा विश्वा भुवनानि वेद महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Viṣṇu, the guardian, keeps the loftiest station, upholding dear, immortal dwelling-places.  Agni knows well all these created beings. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: नाना चक्राते यम्या३ वपूंषि तयोरन्यद्रोचते कृष्णमन्यत् । श्यावी च यदरुषी च स्वसारौ महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Ye, variant Pair, have made yourselves twin beauties: one of the Twain is dark, bright shines the other;  And yet these two, the dark, the red, are Sisters. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: माता च यत्र दुहिता च धेनू सबर्दुघे धापयेते समीची । ऋतस्य ते सदसीळे अन्तर्महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Where the two Cows, the Mother and the Daughter, meet and give suck yielding their lordly nectar,  I praise them at the seat of law eternal. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: अन्यस्या वत्सं रिहती मिमाय कया भुवा नि दधे धेनुरूधः । ऋतस्य सा पयसापिन्वतेळा महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Loud hath she lowed, licking the other's youngling. On what world hath the Milch-cow laid her udder?  This Iḷā streameth with the milk of Order. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: पद्या वस्ते पुरुरूपा वपूंष्यूर्ध्वा तस्थौ त्र्यविं रेरिहाणा । ऋतस्य सद्म वि चरामि विद्वान्महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Earth weareth beauties manifold: uplifted, licking her Calf of eighteen months, she standeth.  Well-skilled I seek the seat of law eternal. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: पदे इव निहिते दस्मे अन्तस्तयोरन्यद्गुह्यमाविरन्यत् । सध्रीचीना पथ्या३ सा विषूची महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Within a wondrous place the Twain are treasured: the one is manifest, the other hidden.  One common pathway leads in two directions. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: आ धेनवो धुनयन्तामशिश्वीः सबर्दुघाः शशया अप्रदुग्धाः । नव्यानव्या युवतयो भवन्तीर्महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Let the milch-kine that have no calves storm downward, yielding rich nectar, streaming, unexhausted,  These who are ever new and fresh and youthful. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: यदन्यासु वृषभो रोरवीति सो अन्यस्मिन्यूथे नि दधाति रेतः । स हि क्षपावान्त्स भगः स राजा महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: What time the Bull bellows in other regions, another herd receives the genial moisture;  For he is Bhaga, King, the earth's Protector. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: वीरस्य नु स्वश्व्यं जनासः प्र नु वोचाम विदुरस्य देवाः । षोळ्हा युक्ताः पञ्चपञ्चा वहन्ति महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Let us declare the Hero's wealth in horses, O all ye folk: of this the Gods have knowledge.  Sixfold they bear him, or by fives are harnessed. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: देवस्त्वष्टा सविता विश्वरूपः पुपोष प्रजाः पुरुधा जजान । इमा च विश्वा भुवनान्यस्य महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Tvaṣṭar the God, the omniform. Creator, begets and feeds mankind in various manner.  His, verily, arc all these living creatures. Great is the Gods’ supreme dominion.

3.55.d: मही समैरच्चम्वा समीची उभे ते अस्य वसुना न्यृष्टे । शृण्वे वीरो विन्दमानो वसूनि महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: The two great meeting Bowls hath he united: each of the Pair is laden with histreasure.  The Hero is renowned for gathering riches. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: इमां च नः पृथिवीं विश्वधाया उप क्षेति हितमित्रो न राजा । पुरःसदः शर्मसदो न वीरा महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Yea, and on this our earth the All-Sustainer dwells like a King with noble friends about him.  In his protection heroes rest in safety. Great is the Cods' supreme and sole dominion.

3.55.d: निष्षिध्वरीस्त ओषधीरुतापो रयिं त इन्द्र पृथिवी बिभर्ति । सखायस्ते वामभाजः स्याम महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥
3.55.e: Rich in their gifts for thee are herbs and waters, and earth brings all her wealth for thee, O Indra.  May we as friends of thine share goodly treasures. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

3.56.d: न ता मिनन्ति मायिनो न धीरा व्रता देवानां प्रथमा ध्रुवाणि । न रोदसी अद्रुहा वेद्याभिर्न पर्वता निनमे तस्थिवांसः ॥
3.56.e: NOT men of magic skill, not men of wisdom impair the Gods’ first steadfast ordinances.  Ne’er may the earth and heaven which know not malice, nor the fixed hills, be bowed by sage devices.

3.56.d: षड्भाराँ एको अचरन्बिभर्त्यृतं वर्षिष्ठमुप गाव आगुः । तिस्रो महीरुपरास्तस्थुरत्या गुहा द्वे निहिते दर्श्येका ॥
3.56.e: One, moving not away, supports six burthens: the Cows proceed to him the true, the Highest.  Near stand three Mighty Ones who travel swiftly: two are concealed from sight, one is apparent.

3.56.d: त्रिपाजस्यो वृषभो विश्वरूप उत त्र्युधा पुरुध प्रजावान् । त्र्यनीकः पत्यते माहिनावान्त्स रेतोधा वृषभः शश्वतीनाम् ॥
3.56.e: The Bull who wears all shapes, the triple-breasted, three-uddered, with a brood in many places,  Ruleth majestic with his triple aspect, the Bull, the Everlasting Ones' impregner.

3.56.d: अभीक आसां पदवीरबोध्यादित्यानामह्वे चारु नाम । आपश्चिदस्मा अरमन्त देवीः पृथग्व्रजन्तीः परि षीमवृञ्जन् ॥
3.56.e: When nigh them, as their tracer he observed them: he called aloud the dear name of Ādityas.  The Goddesses, the Waters, stayed to meet him: they who were wandering separate enclosed him.

3.56.d: त्री षधस्था सिन्धवस्त्रिः कवीनामुत त्रिमाता विदथेषु सम्राट् । ऋतावरीर्योषणास्तिस्रो अप्यास्त्रिरा दिवो विदथे पत्यमानाः ॥
3.56.e: Streams! the wise Gods have thrice three habitations. Child of three Mothers, he is Lord in synods.  Three are the holy Ladies of the Waters, thrice here from heaven supreme in our assembly.

3.56.d: त्रिरा दिवः सवितर्वार्याणि दिवेदिव आ सुव त्रिर्नो अह्नः । त्रिधातु राय आ सुवा वसूनि भग त्रातर्धिषणे सातये धाः ॥
3.56.e: Do thou, O Savitar, from heaven thrice hither, three times a day, send down thy blessings daily.  Send us, O Bhaga, triple wealth and treasure; cause the two worlds to prosper us, Preserver!

3.56.d: त्रिरा दिवः सविता सोषवीति राजाना मित्रावरुणा सुपाणी । आपश्चिदस्य रोदसी चिदुर्वी रत्नं भिक्षन्त सवितुः सवाय ॥
3.56.e: Savitar thrice from heaven pours down abundance, and the fair-handed Kings Varuṇa, Mitra;  And spacious Heaven and Earth, yea, and the Waters, solicit wealth that Savitar may send us.

3.56.d: त्रिरुत्तमा दूणशा रोचनानि त्रयो राजन्त्यसुरस्य वीराः । ऋतावान इषिरा दूळभासस्त्रिरा दिवो विदथे सन्तु देवाः ॥
3.56.e: Three are the bright realms, best, beyond attainment, and three, the Asura's Heroes, rule as Sovrans,  Holy and vigorous, never to be injured. Thrice may the Gods from heaven attend our synod.

3.57.d: प्र मे विविक्वाँ अविदन्मनीषां धेनुं चरन्तीं प्रयुतामगोपाम् । सद्यश्चिद्या दुदुहे भूरि धासेरिन्द्रस्तदग्निः पनितारो अस्याः ॥
3.57.e: MY thought with fine discernment hath discovered the Cow who wanders free without a herdsman,  Her who hath straightway poured me food in plenty: Indra and Agni therefore are her praisers.

3.57.d: इन्द्रः सु पूषा वृषणा सुहस्ता दिवो न प्रीताः शशयं दुदुह्रे । विश्वे यदस्यां रणयन्त देवाः प्र वोऽत्र वसवः सुम्नमश्याम् ॥
3.57.e: Indra and Pūṣan, deft of hand and mighty, well-pleased have drained the heaven's exhaustless udder.  As in this praise the Gods have all delighted, may I win blessing here from you, O Vasus.

3.57.d: या जामयो वृष्ण इच्छन्ति शक्तिं नमस्यन्तीर्जानते गर्भमस्मिन् । अच्छा पुत्रं धेनवो वावशाना महश्चरन्ति बिभ्रतं वपूंषि ॥
3.57.e: Fain to lend vigour to the Bull, the siste.. with reverence recognize the germ within him.  The Cows come lowing hither to the Youngling, to him endued with great and wondrous beauties.

3.57.d: अच्छा विवक्मि रोदसी सुमेके ग्राव्णो युजानो अध्वरे मनीषा । इमा उ ते मनवे भूरिवारा ऊर्ध्वा भवन्ति दर्शता यजत्राः ॥
3.57.e: Fixing with thought, at sacrifice, the press-stones, I bid the well-formed Heaven and Earth come hither;  For these thy flames, which give men boons in plenty, rise up on high, the beautiful, the holy.

3.57.d: या ते जिह्वा मधुमती सुमेधा अग्ने देवेषूच्यत उरूची । तयेह विश्वाँ अवसे यजत्राना सादय पायया चा मधूनि ॥
3.57.e: Agni, thy meath-sweet tongue that tastes fair viands, which among Gods is called the far-extended,—  Therewith make all the Holy Odes be seated here for our help, and feed them with sweet juices.

3.57.d: या ते अग्ने पर्वतस्येव धारासश्चन्ती पीपयद्देव चित्रा । तामस्मभ्यं प्रमतिं जातवेदो वसो रास्व सुमतिं विश्वजन्याम् ॥
3.57.e: Let thy stream give us drink, O God, O Agni, wonderful and exhaustless like the rain-clouds.  Thus care for us, O Vasu Jātavedas, show us thy loving-kindness, reaching all men.

3.58.d: धेनुः प्रत्नस्य काम्यं दुहानान्तः पुत्रश्चरति दक्षिणायाः । आ द्योतनिं वहति शुभ्रयामोषसः स्तोमो अश्विनावजीगः ॥
3.58.e: THE Ancient's Milch-cow yields the things we long for: the Son of Dakṣiṇā travels between them.  She with the splendid chariot brings refulgence. The praise of Uṣas hath awoke the Aśvins.

3.58.d: सुयुग्वहन्ति प्रति वामृतेनोर्ध्वा भवन्ति पितरेव मेधाः । जरेथामस्मद्वि पणेर्मनीषां युवोरवश्चकृमा यातमर्वाक् ॥
3.58.e: They bear you hither by well-orderd statute: our sacred offerings rise as if to parents.  Destroy in us the counsel of the niggard come hitherward, for we have shown you favour.

3.58.d: सुयुग्भिरश्वैः सुवृता रथेन दस्राविमं शृणुतं श्लोकमद्रेः । किमङ्ग वां प्रत्यवर्तिं गमिष्ठाहुर्विप्रासो अश्विना पुराजाः ॥
3.58.e: With lightly-rolling car and well-yoked horses hear this, the press-stone's song, ye Wonder-Workers.  Have not the sages of old time, ye Aśvins, called you most prompt to come and stay misfortune?

3.58.d: आ मन्येथामा गतं कच्चिदेवैर्विश्वे जनासो अश्विना हवन्ते । इमा हि वां गोऋजीका मधूनि प्र मित्रासो न ददुरुस्रो अग्रे ॥
3.58.e: Remember us, and come to us, for ever men, as their wont is, invocate the Aśvins.  Friends as it were have offered you these juices, sweet, blent with milk at the first break of morning.

3.58.d: तिरः पुरू चिदश्विना रजांस्याङ्गूषो वां मघवाना जनेषु । एह यातं पथिभिर्देवयानैर्दस्राविमे वां निधयो मधूनाम् ॥
3.58.e: Even through many regions, O ye Aśvins high praise is yours among mankind, ye Mighty-  Come, helpers, on the paths which Gods have travelled: here your libations of sweet meath are ready.

3.58.d: पुराणमोकः सख्यं शिवं वां युवोर्नरा द्रविणं जह्नाव्याम् । पुनः कृण्वानाः सख्या शिवानि मध्वा मदेम सह नू समानाः ॥
3.58.e: Ancient your home, auspicious is your friendship: Heroes, your wealth is with the house of Jahnu.  Forming again with you auspicious friendship, let us rejoice with draughts of meath together.

3.58.d: अश्विना वायुना युवं सुदक्षा नियुद्भिष्च सजोषसा युवाना । नासत्या तिरोअह्न्यं जुषाणा सोमं पिबतमस्रिधा सुदानू ॥
3.58.e: O Aśvins, Very Mighty ones, with Vāyu and with his steeds, one-minded, ever-youthful,  Nāsatyas, joying in the third day's Soma, drink it, not hostile, Very Bounteous Givers.

3.58.d: अश्विना परि वामिषः पुरूचीरीयुर्गीर्भिर्यतमाना अमृध्राः । रथो ह वामृतजा अद्रिजूतः परि द्यावापृथिवी याति सद्यः ॥
3.58.e: Aśvins, to you are brought abundant viands in rivalry with sacred songs, unceasing.  Sprung from high Law your car, urged on by press-stones, goes round the earth and heaven in one brief moment.

3.58.d: अश्विना मधुषुत्तमो युवाकुः सोमस्तं पातमा गतं दुरोणे । रथो ह वां भूरि वर्पः करिक्रत्सुतावतो निष्कृतमागमिष्ठः ॥
3.58.e: Aśvins, your Soma sheds delicious sweetness: drink ye thereof and come unto our dwelling.  Your car, assuming many a shape, most often goes to the Soma-presser's place of meeting.

3.59.d: मित्रो जनान्यातयति ब्रुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्याम् । मित्रः कृष्टीरनिमिषाभि चष्टे मित्राय हव्यं घृतवज्जुहोत ॥
3.59.e: MITRA, when speaking, stirreth men to labour: Mitra sustaineth both the earth and heaven.  Mitra beholdeth men with eyes that close not. To Mitra bring, with holy oil, oblation.

3.59.d: प्र स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु प्रयस्वान्यस्त आदित्य शिक्षति व्रतेन । न हन्यते न जीयते त्वोतो नैनमंहो अश्नोत्यन्तितो न दूरात् ॥
3.59.e: Foremost be he who brings thee food, O Mitra, who strives to keep thy sacred Law, Āditya.  He whom thou helpest ne’er is slain or conquered, on him, from near or far, falls no affliction.

3.59.d: अनमीवास इळया मदन्तो मितज्ञवो वरिमन्ना पृथिव्याः । आदित्यस्य व्रतमुपक्षियन्तो वयं मित्रस्य सुमतौ स्याम ॥
3.59.e: joying in sacred food and free from sickness, with knees bent lowly on the earth's broad surface,  Following closely the Āditya's statute, may we remain in Mitra's gracious favour.

3.59.d: अयं मित्रो नमस्यः सुशेवो राजा सुक्षत्रो अजनिष्ट वेधाः । तस्य वयं सुमतौ यज्ञियस्यापि भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम ॥
3.59.e: Auspicious and adorable, this Mitra was born with fair dominion, King, Disposer.  May we enjoy the grace of him the Holy, yea, rest in his propitious loving-kindness.

3.59.d: महाँ आदित्यो नमसोपसद्यो यातयज्जनो गृणते सुशेवः । तस्मा एतत्पन्यतमाय जुष्टमग्नौ मित्राय हविरा जुहोत ॥
3.59.e: The great Āditya, to be served with wor. ship, who stirreth men, is gracious to the singer.  To Mitra, him most highly to be lauded, offer in fire oblation that he loveth.

3.59.d: मित्रस्य चर्षणीधृतोऽवो देवस्य सानसि । द्युम्नं चित्रश्रवस्तमम् ॥
3.59.e: The gainful grace of Mitra,. God, supporter of the race of man,  Gives splendour of most.glorious fame.

3.59.d: अभि यो महिना दिवं मित्रो बभूव सप्रथाः । अभि श्रवोभिः पृथिवीम् ॥
3.59.e: Mitra whose glory spreads afar, he who in might surpasses heaven,  Surpasses earth in his renown.

3.59.d: मित्राय पञ्च येमिरे जना अभिष्टिशवसे । स देवान्विश्वान्बिभर्ति ॥
3.59.e: All the Five Races have repaired to Mitra, ever strong to aid,  For he sustaineth all the Gods.

3.59.d: मित्रो देवेष्वायुषु जनाय वृक्तबर्हिषे । इष इष्टव्रता अकः ॥
3.59.e: Mitra to Gods, to living men, to him who strews the holy grass,  Gives food fulfilling sacred Law.

3.60.d: इहेह वो मनसा बन्धुता नर उशिजो जग्मुरभि तानि वेदसा । याभिर्मायाभिः प्रतिजूतिवर्पसः सौधन्वना यज्ञियं भागमानश ॥
3.60.e: HERE is your ghostly kinship, here, O Men: they came desirous to these holy rites with store of wealth,  With wondrous arts, whereby, with schemes to meet each need, Ye gained, Sudhanvan's Sons! your share in sacrifice.

3.60.d: याभिः शचीभिश्चमसाँ अपिंशत यया धिया गामरिणीत चर्मणः । येन हरी मनसा निरतक्षत तेन देवत्वमृभवः समानश ॥
3.60.e: The mighty powers wherewith. ye formed the chalices, the thought by which ye drew the cow from out the hide,  The intellect wherewith ye wrought the two Bay Steeds,—through these, O Ṛbhus, ye attained divinity.

3.60.d: इन्द्रस्य सख्यमृभवः समानशुर्मनोर्नपातो अपसो दधन्विरे । सौधन्वनासो अमृतत्वमेरिरे विष्ट्वी शमीभिः सुकृतः सुकृत्यया ॥
3.60.e: Friendship with Indra have the Ṛbhus, fully gained: grandsons of Manu, they skilfully urged the work.  Sudhanvan's Children won them everlasting life, serving with holy rites, pious with noble acts.  4:In company with Indra come ye to the juice, then gloriously shall your wishes be fulfilled.  Not to be paragoned, ye Priests, are your good deeds, nor your heroic acts, Ṛbhus, Sudhanvan's Sons.

3.60.d: इन्द्रेण याथ सरथं सुते सचाँ अथो वशानां भवथा सह श्रिया । न वः प्रतिमै सुकृतानि वाघतः सौधन्वना ऋभवो वीर्याणि च ॥
3.60.e: :In company with Indra come ye to the juice, then gloriously shall your wishes be fulfilled. Not to be paragoned, ye Priests, are your good deeds, nor your heroic acts, Ṛbhus, Sudhanvan's Sons.

3.60.d: इन्द्र ऋभुभिर्वाजवद्भिः समुक्षितं सुतं सोममा वृषस्वा गभस्त्योः । धियेषितो मघवन्दाशुषो गृहे सौधन्वनेभिः सह मत्स्वा नृभिः ॥
3.60.e: O Indra, with the Ṛbhus, Mighty Ones, pour down the Soma juice effused, well-blent, from both thy hands.  Maghalan, urged by song, in the drink-offerer's house rejoice thee with the Heroes, with Sudhanvan's Sons.

3.60.d: इन्द्र ऋभुमान्वाजवान्मत्स्वेह नोऽस्मिन्त्सवने शच्या पुरुष्टुत । इमानि तुभ्यं स्वसराणि येमिरे व्रता देवानां मनुषश्च धर्मभिः ॥
3.60.e: With Ṛbhu near, and Vāja, Indra, here exult, with Saci, praised of many, in the juice we pour.  These homes wherein we dwell have turned themselves to thee, -devotions to the Gods, as laws of men ordain.

3.60.d: इन्द्र ऋभुभिर्वाजिभिर्वाजयन्निह स्तोमं जरितुरुप याहि यज्ञियम् । शतं केतेभिरिषिरेभिरायवे सहस्रणीथो अध्वरस्य होमनि ॥
3.60.e: Come with the mighty Ṛbhus, Indra, come to us, strengthening with thy help the singer's holy praise;  At hundred eager calls come to the living man, with thousand arts attend the act of sacrifice.

3.61.d: उषो वाजेन वाजिनि प्रचेताः स्तोमं जुषस्व गृणतो मघोनि । पुराणी देवि युवतिः पुरंधिरनु व्रतं चरसि विश्ववारे ॥
3.61.e: O Uṣas, strong with strength, endowed witli knowledge, accept the singer's praise, O wealthy Lady.  Thou, Goddess, ancient, young, and full of wisdom, movest, all-bounteous! as the Law ordaineth.

3.61.d: उषो देव्यमर्त्या वि भाहि चन्द्ररथा सूनृता ईरयन्ती । आ त्वा वहन्तु सुयमासो अश्वा हिरण्यवर्णां पृथुपाजसो ये ॥
3.61.e: Shine forth, O Morning, thou auspicious Goddess, on thy bright car awaking pleasant voices.  Let docile horses of far-reaching splendour convey thee hitherward, the goldencoloured.

3.61.d: उषः प्रतीची भुवनानि विश्वोर्ध्वा तिष्ठस्यमृतस्य केतुः । समानमर्थं चरणीयमाना चक्रमिव नव्यस्या ववृत्स्व ॥
3.61.e: Thou, Morning, turning thee to every creature, standest on high as ensign of the Immortal,  To one same goal ever and ever wending now, like a wheel, O newly-born, roll hi ther.

3.61.d: अव स्यूमेव चिन्वती मघोन्युषा याति स्वसरस्य पत्नी । स्व१र्जनन्ती सुभगा सुदंसा आन्ताद्दिवः पप्रथ आ पृथिव्याः ॥
3.61.e: Letting her reins drop downward, Morning cometh, the wealthy Dame, the Lady of the dwelling;  Bringing forth light, the Wonderful, the Blessed hath spread her from the bounds of earth and heaven.

3.61.d: अच्छा वो देवीमुषसं विभातीं प्र वो भरध्वं नमसा सुवृक्तिम् । ऊर्ध्वं मधुधा दिवि पाजो अश्रेत्प्र रोचना रुरुचे रण्वसंदृक् ॥
3.61.e: Hither invoke the radiant Goddess Morning, and bring with reverence your hymn to praise her.  She, dropping sweets, hath set in heaven her brightness, and, fair to look on, hath beamed forth her splendour.

3.61.d: ऋतावरी दिवो अर्कैरबोध्या रेवती रोदसी चित्रमस्थात् । आयतीमग्न उषसं विभातीं वाममेषि द्रविणं भिक्षमाणः ॥
3.61.e: From heaven, with hymns, the Holy One was wakened: brightly to both worlds came the wealthy Lady.  To Morning, Agni, when she comes refulgent, thou goest forth soliciting fair riches.

3.61.d: ऋतस्य बुध्न उषसामिषण्यन्वृषा मही रोदसी आ विवेश । मही मित्रस्य वरुणस्य माया चन्द्रेव भानुं वि दधे पुरुत्रा ॥
3.61.e: On Law's firm base the speeder of the Mornings, the Bull, hath entered mighty earth and heaven.  Great is the power of Varuṇa and Mitra, which, bright, hath spread in every place its splendour.

3.62.d: इमा उ वां भृमयो मन्यमाना युवावते न तुज्या अभूवन् । क्व१ त्यदिन्द्रावरुणा यशो वां येन स्मा सिनं भरथः सखिभ्यः ॥
3.62.e: YOUR well-known prompt activities aforetime needed no impulse from your faithful servant.  Where, Indra-Varuṇa, is now that glory wherewith ye brought support to those who loved you?

3.62.d: अयमु वां पुरुतमो रयीयञ्छश्वत्तममवसे जोहवीति । सजोषाविन्द्रावरुणा मरुद्भिर्दिवा पृथिव्या शृणुतं हवं मे ॥
3.62.e: This man, most diligent, seeking after riches, incessantly invokes you for your favour.  Accordant, Indra-Varuṇa, with Maruts, with Heaven and Earth, hear ye mine invocation.

3.62.d: अस्मे तदिन्द्रावरुणा वसु ष्यादस्मे रयिर्मरुतः सर्ववीरः । अस्मान्वरूत्रीः शरणैरवन्त्वस्मान्होत्रा भारती दक्षिणाभिः ॥
3.62.e: O Indra-Varuṇa, ours be this treasure ours be wealth, Maruts, with full store of heroes.  May the Varūtrīs with their shelter aid us, and Bhāratī and Hotrā with the Mornings.

3.62.d: बृहस्पते जुषस्व नो हव्यानि विश्वदेव्य । रास्व रत्नानि दाशुषे ॥
3.62.e: Be pleased! with our oblations, thou loved of all Gods, Bṛhaspati:  Give wealth to him who brings thee gifts.
At sacrifices, with your hymns worship the pure Bṛhaspati—  I pray for power which none may bend—
The Bull of men, whom none deceive, the wearer of each shape at will,  Bṛhaspati Most Excellent.

3.62.d: इयं ते पूषन्नाघृणे सुष्टुतिर्देव नव्यसी । अस्माभिस्तुभ्यं शस्यते ॥
3.62.e: Divine, resplendent Pūṣan, this our newest hymn of eulogy,  By us is chanted forth to thee.

3.62.d: तां जुषस्व गिरं मम वाजयन्तीमवा धियम् । वधूयुरिव योषणाम् ॥
3.62.e: Accept with favour this my song, be gracious to the earnest thought,  Even as a bridegroom to his bride.

3.62.d: यो विश्वाभि विपश्यति भुवना सं च पश्यति । स नः पूषाविता भुवत् ॥
3.62.e: May he who sees all living things, see, them together at a glance,—  May he, may Pūṣan be our help.

3.62.d: तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि । धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् ॥
3.62.e: May we attain that excellent glory of Savitar the God:  So May he stimulate our prayers.

3.62.d: देवस्य सवितुर्वयं वाजयन्तः पुरंध्या । भगस्य रातिमीमहे ॥
3.62.e: With understanding, earnestly, of Savitar the God we crave  Our portion of prosperity.

3.62.d: देवं नरः सवितारं विप्रा यज्ञैः सुवृक्तिभिः । नमस्यन्ति धियेषिताः ॥
3.62.e: Men, singers worship Savitar the God with hymn and holy rites,  Urged by the impulse of their thoughts.

3.62.d: सोमो जिगाति गातुविद्देवानामेति निष्कृतम् । ऋतस्य योनिमासदम् ॥
3.62.e: Soma who gives success goes forth, goes to the gathering place of Gods,  To seat him at the seat of Law.

3.62.d: सोमो अस्मभ्यं द्विपदे चतुष्पदे च पशवे । अनमीवा इषस्करत् ॥
3.62.e: To us and to our cattle may Soma give salutary food,  To biped and to quadruped.
May Soma, strengthening our power of life, and conquering our foes,  In our assembly take his seat.

3.62.d: आ नो मित्रावरुणा घृतैर्गव्यूतिमुक्षतम् । मध्वा रजांसि सुक्रतू ॥
3.62.e: May Mitra-Varuṇa, sapient Pair, bedew our pasturage with oil,  With meatb the regions of the air.

3.62.d: उरुशंसा नमोवृधा मह्ना दक्षस्य राजथः । द्राघिष्ठाभिः शुचिव्रता ॥
3.62.e: Far-ruling, joyful when adored, ye reign through majesty of might,  With pure laws everlastingly.

3.62.d: गृणाना जमदग्निना योनावृतस्य सीदतम् । पातं सोममृतावृधा ॥
3.62.e: Lauded by Jamadagni's song, sit in the place of holy Law: Drink Soma, ye who strengthen Law.

4.1.d: त्वां ह्यग्ने सदमित्समन्यवो देवासो देवमरतिं न्येरिर इति क्रत्वा न्येरिरे । अमर्त्यं यजत मर्त्येष्वा देवमादेवं जनत प्रचेतसं विश्वमादेवं जनत प्रचेतसम् ॥
4.1.e: 1, THEE Agni, have the Gods, ever of one accord, sent hither down, a God, appointed messenger, yea, with their wisdom sent thee down.  The Immortal, O thou Holy One, mid mortal men, the God-devoted God, the wise, have they brought forth, brought forth the omnipresent God-devoted Sage.

4.1.d: स भ्रातरं वरुणमग्न आ ववृत्स्व देवाँ अच्छा सुमती यज्ञवनसं ज्येष्ठं यज्ञवनसम् । ऋतावानमादित्यं चर्षणीधृतं राजानं चर्षणीधृतम् ॥
4.1.e: As such, O Agni, bring with favour to the Gods thy Brother Varuṇa who loveth sacrifice,  True to the Law, the Āditya who supporteth men, the King, supporter of mankind.

4.1.d: सखे सखायमभ्या ववृत्स्वाशुं न चक्रं रथ्येव रंह्यास्मभ्यं दस्म रंह्या । अग्ने मृळीकं वरुणे सचा विदो मरुत्सु विश्वभानुषु । तोकाय तुजे शुशुचान शं कृध्यस्मभ्यं दस्म शं कृधि ॥
4.1.e: Do thou, O Friend, turn hither him who is our Friend, swift as a wheel, like two car-steeds in rapid course, Wondrous! to us in rapid course.  O Agni, find thou grace for us with Varuṇa, with Maruts who illumine all.  Bless us, thou Radiant One, for seed and progeny, yea, bless us, O thou Wondrous God.

4.1.d: त्वं नो अग्ने वरुणस्य विद्वान्देवस्य हेळोऽव यासिसीष्ठाः । यजिष्ठो वह्नितमः शोशुचानो विश्वा द्वेषांसि प्र मुमुग्ध्यस्मत् ॥
4.1.e: Do thou who knowest Varuṇa, O Agni, put far away from us the God's displeasure.  Best Sacrificer, brightest One, refulgent remove thou far from us all those who hate us.

4.1.d: स त्वं नो अग्नेऽवमो भवोती नेदिष्ठो अस्या उषसो व्युष्टौ । अव यक्ष्व नो वरुणं रराणो वीहि मृळीकं सुहवो न एधि ॥
4.1.e: Be thou, O Agni, nearest us with succour, our closest Friend while now this Morn is breaking.  Reconcile to us Varuṇa, be bounteous enjoy the gracious juice; be swift to hear us.

4.1.d: अस्य श्रेष्ठा सुभगस्य संदृग्देवस्य चित्रतमा मर्त्येषु । शुचि घृतं न तप्तमघ्न्यायाः स्पार्हा देवस्य मंहनेव धेनोः ॥
4.1.e: Excellent is the glance, of brightest splendour, which the auspicious God bestows on mortals-  The God's glance, longed-for even as the butter, pure, heated, of the cow, the milch-cow's bounty.

4.1.d: त्रिरस्य ता परमा सन्ति सत्या स्पार्हा देवस्य जनिमान्यग्नेः । अनन्ते अन्तः परिवीत आगाच्छुचिः शुक्रो अर्यो रोरुचानः ॥
4.1.e: Three are those births, the true, the most exalted, eagerly longed-for, of the God, of Agni.  He came invested in the boundless region, pure, radiant, friendly, mightily resplendent.

4.1.d: स दूतो विश्वेदभि वष्टि सद्मा होता हिरण्यरथो रंसुजिह्वः । रोहिदश्वो वपुष्यो विभावा सदा रण्वः पितुमतीव संसत् ॥
4.1.e: This envoy joyeth in all seats of worship, borne on his golden car, sweet-tongued Invoker:  Lovely to look on, with red steeds, effulgent, like a feast rich in food, joyous for ever.

4.1.d: स चेतयन्मनुषो यज्ञबन्धुः प्र तं मह्या रशनया नयन्ति । स क्षेत्यस्य दुर्यासु साधन्देवो मर्तस्य सधनित्वमाप ॥
4.1.e: Allied by worship, let him give man knowledge: by an extended cord they lead him onward.  He stays, effectual in this mortal's dwelling, and the God wins a share in his possessions.

4.1.d: स तू नो अग्निर्नयतु प्रजानन्नच्छा रत्नं देवभक्तं यदस्य । धिया यद्विश्वे अमृता अकृण्वन्द्यौष्पिता जनिता सत्यमुक्षन् ॥
4.1.e: Let Agni -for he knows the way- conduct us to all that he enjoys of God-sent riches,  What all the Immortals have prepared with wisdom, Dyaus, Sire, Begetter, raining down true blessings.

4.1.d: स जायत प्रथमः पस्त्यासु महो बुध्ने रजसो अस्य योनौ । अपादशीर्षा गुहमानो अन्तायोयुवानो वृषभस्य नीळे ॥
