4.1.e: In houses first he sprang into existence, at great heaven's base, and in this region's bosom;  Footless and headless, both his ends concealing, in his Bull's lair drawing himself together.

4.1.d: प्र शर्ध आर्त प्रथमं विपन्याँ ऋतस्य योना वृषभस्य नीळे । स्पार्हो युवा वपुष्यो विभावा सप्त प्रियासोऽजनयन्त वृष्णे ॥
4.1.e: Wondrously first he rose aloft, defiant, in the Bull's lair, the homeof holy Order,  Longed-for, young, beautiful, and far-resplendent: and sevendear frieuds sprang up unto the Mighty.

4.1.d: अस्माकमत्र पितरो मनुष्या अभि प्र सेदुर्ऋतमाशुषाणाः । अश्मव्रजाः सुदुघा वव्रे अन्तरुदुस्रा आजन्नुषसो हुवानाः ॥
4.1.e: Here did our human fathers take their places, fain to fulfil the sacred Law of worship.  Forth drave they, with loud call, Dawn's teeming Milch-kine bid in the mountainstable, in the cavern.

4.1.d: ते मर्मृजत ददृवांसो अद्रिं तदेषामन्ये अभितो वि वोचन् । पश्वयन्त्रासो अभि कारमर्चन्विदन्त ज्योतिश्चकृपन्त धीभिः ॥
4.1.e: Splendid were they when they had rent the mountain: others, around, shall tell forth this their exploit.  They sang their song, prepared to free the cattle: they found the light; with holy hymns they worshipped.

4.1.d: ते गव्यता मनसा दृध्रमुब्धं गा येमानं परि षन्तमद्रिम् । दृळ्हं नरो वचसा दैव्येन व्रजं गोमन्तमुशिजो वि वव्रुः ॥
4.1.e: Eager, with thought intent upon the booty, the men with their celestial speech threw open,  The solid mountain firm, compact, enclosing, confining Cows, the stable full of cattle.

4.1.d: ते मन्वत प्रथमं नाम धेनोस्त्रिः सप्त मातुः परमाणि विन्दन् । तज्जानतीरभ्यनूषत व्रा आविर्भुवदरुणीर्यशसा गोः ॥
4.1.e: The Milch-cow's earliest name they comprehended: they found the Mother's thrice-seven noblest titles.  This the bands knew, and sent forth acclamation:with the Bull's sheen the Red One was apparent.

4.1.d: नेशत्तमो दुधितं रोचत द्यौरुद्देव्या उषसो भानुरर्त । आ सूर्यो बृहतस्तिष्ठदज्राँ ऋजु मर्तेषु वृजिना च पश्यन् ॥
4.1.e: The turbid darkness fled, the heaven was sp, endid! up rose the bright beam of celestial Morning.  Sūrya ascended to the wide expanses, beholding deeds of men both good and evil.

4.1.d: आदित्पश्चा बुबुधाना व्यख्यन्नादिद्रत्नं धारयन्त द्युभक्तम् । विश्वे विश्वासु दुर्यासु देवा मित्र धिये वरुण सत्यमस्तु ॥
4.1.e: Then, afterwards they looked around, awakened, when first they held that Heaven allotted treasure.  Now all the Gods abide in all their dwellings. Varuṇa, Mitra, be the prayer effective.

4.1.d: अच्छा वोचेय शुशुचानमग्निं होतारं विश्वभरसं यजिष्ठम् । शुच्यूधो अतृणन्न गवामन्धो न पूतं परिषिक्तमंशोः ॥
4.1.e: I will call hither brightly-beaming Agni, the Herald, all-supporting, best at worship.  He hath disclosed, like the milch cows' pure udder, the Sorria's juice when cleansed and poured from beakers.

4.1.d: विश्वेषामदितिर्यज्ञियानां विश्वेषामतिथिर्मानुषाणाम् । अग्निर्देवानामव आवृणानः सुमृळीको भवतु जातवेदाः ॥
4.1.e: The freest God of all who should be worshipped, the guest who is received in all men's houses, Agni who hath secured the Gods' high favour,– may he be gracious, to us Jātavedas.

4.2.d: यो मर्त्येष्वमृत ऋतावा देवो देवेष्वरतिर्निधायि । होता यजिष्ठो मह्ना शुचध्यै हव्यैरग्निर्मनुष ईरयध्यै ॥
4.2.e: THE, Faithful One, Immortal among mortals, a God among the Gods, appointed envoy,  Priest, best at worship, must shine forth in glory . Agni shall be raised high with man's oblations.

4.2.d: इह त्वं सूनो सहसो नो अद्य जातो जाताँ उभयाँ अन्तरग्ने । दूत ईयसे युयुजान ऋष्व ऋजुमुष्कान्वृषणः शुक्राँश्च ॥
4.2.e: Born for us here this day, O Son of Vigour, between both races of born beings, Agni,  Thou farest as an envoy, having harnessed, Sublime One! thy strong-muscled radiant stallions.

4.2.d: अत्या वृधस्नू रोहिता घृतस्नू ऋतस्य मन्ये मनसा जविष्ठा । अन्तरीयसे अरुषा युजानो युष्माँश्च देवान्विश आ च मर्तान् ॥
4.2.e: I laud the ruddy steeds who pour down blessing, dropping oil, flectest through the thoualit of Order.  Yoking red horses to and fro thou goest between you Deities and mortal races.

4.2.d: अर्यमणं वरुणं मित्रमेषामिन्द्राविष्णू मरुतो अश्विनोत । स्वश्वो अग्ने सुरथः सुराधा एदु वह सुहविषे जनाय ॥
4.2.e: Aryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa, and Indra with Viṣṇu, of the Gods, Maruts and Aśvins-  These, Agni, with good car and steeds, bring hither, most bountiful, to folk with fair oblations.

4.2.d: गोमाँ अग्नेऽविमाँ अश्वी यज्ञो नृवत्सखा सदमिदप्रमृष्यः । इळावाँ एषो असुर प्रजावान्दीर्घो रयिः पृथुबुध्नः सभावान् ॥
4.2.e: Agni, be this our sacrifice eternal, with brave friends, rich in kine and sheep and horses,  Rich, Asura! in sacred food and children, in full assembly, wealth broad-based and during.

4.2.d: यस्त इध्मं जभरत्सिष्विदानो मूर्धानं वा ततपते त्वाया । भुवस्तस्य स्वतवाँः पायुरग्ने विश्वस्मात्सीमघायत उरुष्य ॥
4.2.e: The man who, sweating, brings for thee the fuel, and makes his head to ache, thy faithful servant,—  Agni, to him be a self-strong Protector guard him from all who seek to do him mischief.

4.2.d: यस्ते भरादन्नियते चिदन्नं निशिषन्मन्द्रमतिथिमुदीरत् । आ देवयुरिनधते दुरोणे तस्मिन्रयिर्ध्रुवो अस्तु दास्वान् ॥
4.2.e: Who brings thee food, though thou hast food in plenty, welcomes his cheerful guest and speeds him onward,  Who kindles thee devoutly in his dwelling,to him be wealth secure and freely giving.

4.2.d: यस्त्वा दोषा य उषसि प्रशंसात्प्रियं वा त्वा कृणवते हविष्मान् । अश्वो न स्वे दम आ हेम्यावान्तमंहसः पीपरो दाश्वांसम् ॥
4.2.e: Whoso sings praise to thee at eve or morning, and, with oblation, doth the thing thou lovest,—  In his own home, even as a goId-girt courser, rescue him from distress, the bounteous giver.

4.2.d: यस्तुभ्यमग्ने अमृताय दाशद्दुवस्त्वे कृणवते यतस्रुक् । न स राया शशमानो वि योषन्नैनमंहः परि वरदघायोः ॥
4.2.e: Whoso brings gifts to thee Immortal, Agni, and doth thee service with uplifted ladle,—  Let him not, sorely toiling, lose his riches; let not the sinner's wickedness enclose him.

4.2.d: यस्य त्वमग्ने अध्वरं जुजोषो देवो मर्तस्य सुधितं रराणः । प्रीतेदसद्धोत्रा सा यविष्ठासाम यस्य विधतो वृधासः ॥
4.2.e: Whose well-wrought worship thou acceptest, Agni, thou God a mortal's gift, thou liberal Giver,—  Dear be his sacrifice to thee, Most Youthful! and may we strengthen him when he adores thee.

4.2.d: चित्तिमचित्तिं चिनवद्वि विद्वान्पृष्ठेव वीता वृजिना च मर्तान् । राये च नः स्वपत्याय देव दितिं च रास्वादितिमुरुष्य ॥
4.2.e: May he who knows distinguish sense and folly of men, like straight and crooked backs of horses.  Lead us, O God, to wealth and noble offspring: keep penury afar and grant us plenty.

4.2.d: कविं शशासुः कवयोऽदब्धा निधारयन्तो दुर्यास्वायोः । अतस्त्वं दृश्याँ अग्न एतान्पड्भिः पश्येरद्भुताँ अर्य एवैः ॥
4.2.e: This Sage the Sages, ne’er deceived, commanded, setting him down in dwellings of the living.  Hence mayst thou, friendly God, with rapid footsteps behold the Gods, wonderful, fair to look on.

4.2.d: त्वमग्ने वाघते सुप्रणीतिः सुतसोमाय विधते यविष्ठ । रत्नं भर शशमानाय घृष्वे पृथु श्चन्द्रमवसे चर्षणिप्राः ॥
4.2.e: Good guidance hast thou for the priest, O Agni, who, Youngest God! with outpoured Soma serves thee.  Ruler of men, thou joyous God, bring treasure splendid and plentiful to aid the toiler.

4.2.d: अधा ह यद्वयमग्ने त्वाया पड्भिर्हस्तेभिश्चकृमा तनूभिः । रथं न क्रन्तो अपसा भुरिजोर्ऋतं येमुः सुध्य आशुषाणाः ॥
4.2.e: Now all that we, thy faithful servants, Agni, have done with feet, with hands, and with our bodies,  The wise, with toil, the holy rite have guided, as those who frame a car with manual cunning.

4.2.d: अधा मातुरुषसः सप्त विप्रा जायेमहि प्रथमा वेधसो नॄन् । दिवस्पुत्रा अङ्गिरसो भवेमाद्रिं रुजेम धनिनं शुचन्तः ॥
4.2.e: May we, seven sages first in rank, engender, from Dawn the Mother, men to be ordainers.  May we, Aṅgirases, be sons of Heaven, and, radiant, burst the wealth-containing mountain.

4.2.d: अधा यथा नः पितरः परासः प्रत्नासो अग्न ऋतमाशुषाणाः । शुचीदयन्दीधितिमुक्थशासः क्षामा भिन्दन्तो अरुणीरप व्रन् ॥
4.2.e: As in the days of old our ancient Fathers, speeding the work of holy worship, Agni,  Sought pure light and devotion, singing praises; they cleft the ground and made red Dawns apparent.

4.2.d: सुकर्माणः सुरुचो देवयन्तोऽयो न देवा जनिमा धमन्तः । शुचन्तो अग्निं ववृधन्त इन्द्रमूर्वं गव्यं परिषदन्तो अग्मन् ॥
4.2.e: Gods, doing holy acts, devout, resplendent, smelting like ore their human generations.  Enkindling Agni and exalting Indra, they came encompassing the stall of cattle.

4.2.d: आ यूथेव क्षुमति पश्वो अख्यद्देवानां यज्जनिमान्त्युग्र । मर्तानां चिदुर्वशीरकृप्रन्वृधे चिदर्य उपरस्यायोः ॥
4.2.e: Strong One! he marked them-and the Gods before them-like herds of cattle in a foodful pasture.  There they moaned forth their strong desire for mortals, to aid the True, the nearest One, the Living.

4.2.d: अकर्म ते स्वपसो अभूम ऋतमवस्रन्नुषसो विभातीः । अनूनमग्निं पुरुधा सुश्चन्द्रं देवस्य मर्मृजतश्चारु चक्षुः ॥
4.2.e: We have worked for thee, we have laboured nobly-bright Dawns have shed their light upon our worship-  Adding a beauty to the perfect Agni, and the God's beauteous eye that shines for ever.

4.2.d: एता ते अग्न उचथानि वेधोऽवोचाम कवये ता जुषस्व । उच्छोचस्व कृणुहि वस्यसो नो महो रायः पुरुवार प्र यन्धि ॥
4.2.e: Agni, Disposer, we have sung these praises to thee the Wise: do thou accept them gladly.  Blaze up on high and ever make us richer. Give us great wealth, O thou whose boons are many.

4.3.d: आ वो राजानमध्वरस्य रुद्रं होतारं सत्ययजं रोदस्योः । अग्निं पुरा तनयित्नोरचित्ताद्धिरण्यरूपमवसे कृणुध्वम् ॥
4.3.e: WIN, to assist you, Rudra, Lord of worship, Priest of both worlds, effectual  Sacrificer,  Agni, invested with his golden colours, before the thunder strike and lay you senseless.

4.3.d: अयं योनिश्चकृमा यं वयं ते जायेव पत्य उशती सुवासाः । अर्वाचीनः परिवीतो नि षीदेमा उ ते स्वपाक प्रतीचीः ॥
4.3.e: This shrine have we made ready for thy coming, as the fond dame attires her for her husband.  Performer of good work, sit down before us, invested while these flames incline to meet thee.

4.3.d: आशृण्वते अदृपिताय मन्म नृचक्षसे सुमृळीकाय वेधः । देवाय शस्तिममृताय शंस ग्रावेव सोता मधुषुद्यमीळे ॥
4.3.e: A hymn, O Priest, to him who hears, the gentle, to him who looks on men, exceeding gracious,  A song of praise sing to the God Immortal, whom the stone, presser of the sweet juice, worships.

4.3.d: त्वं चिन्नः शम्या अग्ने अस्या ऋतस्य बोध्यृतचित्स्वाधीः । कदा त उक्था सधमाद्यानि कदा भवन्ति सख्या गृहे ते ॥
4.3.e: Even as true knower of the Law, O Agni, to this our solemn rite he thou attentive.  When shall thy songs of festival be sung thee? When is thy friendship shown within our dwelling?

4.3.d: कथा ह तद्वरुणाय त्वमग्ने कथा दिवे गर्हसे कन्न आगः । कथा मित्राय मीळ्हुषे पृथिव्यै ब्रवः कदर्यम्णे कद्भगाय ॥
4.3.e: Why this complaint to Varuṇa, O Agni? And why to Heaven? for what is our transgression?  How wilt thou speak to Earth and bounteous Mitra? What wilt thou say to Aryaman and Bhaga?

4.3.d: कद्धिष्ण्यासु वृधसानो अग्ने कद्वाताय प्रतवसे शुभंये । परिज्मने नासत्याय क्षे ब्रवः कदग्ने रुद्राय नृघ्ने ॥
4.3.e: What, when thou blazest on the lesser altars, what to the mighty Wind who comes to bless us,  True, circumambient? what to Earth, O Agni, what wilt thou say to man-destroying Rudra?

4.3.d: कथा महे पुष्टिम्भराय पूष्णे कद्रुद्राय सुमखाय हविर्दे । कद्विष्णव उरुगायाय रेतो ब्रवः कदग्ने शरवे बृहत्यै ॥
4.3.e: How to great Pūṣan who promotes our welfare,—to honoured Rudra what, who gives oblations?  What sin of ours to the far-striding Viṣṇu, what, Agni, wilt thou tell the Lofty Arrow.

4.3.d: कथा शर्धाय मरुतामृताय कथा सूरे बृहते पृच्छ्यमानः । प्रति ब्रवोऽदितये तुराय साधा दिवो जातवेदश्चिकित्वान् ॥
4.3.e: What wilt thou tell the truthful band of Maruts, how answer the great Sun when thou art questioned?  Before the Free, before the Swift, defend us: fulfil heaven's work, all-knowing Jātavedas.

4.3.d: ऋतेन ऋतं नियतमीळ आ गोरामा सचा मधुमत्पक्वमग्ने । कृष्णा सती रुशता धासिनैषा जामर्येण पयसा पीपाय ॥
4.3.e: I crave the cow's true gift arranged by Order: though raw, she hath the sweet ripe juice, O Agni.  Though she is black of hue with milk she teemeth, nutritious, brightly shining, all-sustaining.

4.3.d: ऋतेन हि ष्मा वृषभश्चिदक्तः पुमाँ अग्निः पयसा पृष्ठ्येन । अस्पन्दमानो अचरद्वयोधा वृषा शुक्रं दुदुहे पृश्निरूधः ॥
4.3.e: Agni the Bull, the manly, hath been sprinkled with oil upon his back, by Law eternal.  He who gives vital power goes on unswerving. Pṛśni the Bull hath milked the pure wiiite udder.

4.3.d: ऋतेनाद्रिं व्यसन्भिदन्तः समङ्गिरसो नवन्त गोभिः । शुनं नरः परि षदन्नुषासमाविः स्वरभवज्जाते अग्नौ ॥
4.3.e: By Law the Aṅgirases cleft the rock asunder, and sang their hymns together with the cattle.  Bringing great bliss the men encompassed Morning: light was apparent at the birth of Agni.

4.3.d: ऋतेन देवीरमृता अमृक्ता अर्णोभिरापो मधुमद्भिरग्ने । वाजी न सर्गेषु प्रस्तुभानः प्र सदमित्स्रवितवे दधन्युः ॥
4.3.e: By Law the Immortal Goddesses the Waters, with meath-rich waves, O Agni, and uninjured,  Like a strong courser lauded in his running, sped to flow onward swiftly and for ever.

4.3.d: मा कस्य यक्षं सदमिद्धुरो गा मा वेशस्य प्रमिनतो मापेः । मा भ्रातुरग्ने अनृजोर्ऋणं वेर्मा सख्युर्दक्षं रिपोर्भुजेम ॥
4.3.e: Go never to the feast of one who harms us, the treacherous neighbour or unworthy kinsman.  Punish us not for a false brother's trespass. Let us not feel the might of friend or foeman.

4.3.d: रक्षा णो अग्ने तव रक्षणेभी रारक्षाणः सुमख प्रीणानः । प्रति ष्फुर वि रुज वीड्वंहो जहि रक्षो महि चिद्वावृधानम् ॥
4.3.e: O Agni, keep us safe with thy protection, loving us, honoured God! and ever guarding.  Beat thou away,  destroy  severe affliction slay e’en the demon when he waxes mighty.

4.3.d: एभिर्भव सुमना अग्ने अर्कैरिमान्त्स्पृश मन्मभिः शूर वाजान् । उत ब्रह्माण्यङ्गिरो जुषस्व सं ते शस्तिर्देववाता जरेत ॥
4.3.e: Through these our songs of praise be gracious, Agni; moved by our prayers, O Hero, touch our viands.  Accept, O Aṅgiras, these our devotions, and let the praise which Gods desire address thee.

4.3.d: एता विश्वा विदुषे तुभ्यं वेधो नीथान्यग्ने निण्या वचांसि । निवचना कवये काव्यान्यशंसिषं मतिभिर्विप्र उक्थैः ॥
4.3.e: To thee who knowest, Agni, thou Disposer, all these wise secret speeches have I uttered,  Sung to thee, Sage, the charming words of wisdom, to thee, O Singer, with. my thoughts and Praises.

4.4.d: कृणुष्व पाजः प्रसितिं न पृथ्वीं याहि राजेवामवाँ इभेन । तृष्वीमनु प्रसितिं द्रूणानोऽस्तासि विध्य रक्षसस्तपिष्ठैः ॥
4.4.e: PUT forth like a wide-spreading net thy vigour; go like a mighty King with his attendants.  Thou, following thy swift net, shootest arrows: transfix the fiends with darts that burn most fiercely.

4.4.d: तव भ्रमास आशुया पतन्त्यनु स्पृश धृषता शोशुचानः । तपूंष्यग्ने जुह्वा पतंगानसंदितो वि सृज विष्वगुल्काः ॥
4.4.e: Forth go in rapid flight thy whirling weapons: follow them closely, glowing in thy fury.  Spread with thy tongue the winged flames, O Agni; unfettered, cast thy firebrands all around thee.

4.4.d: प्रति स्पशो वि सृज तूर्णितमो भवा पायुर्विशो अस्या अदब्धः । यो नो दूरे अघशंसो यो अन्त्यग्ने माकिष्टे व्यथिरा दधर्षीत् ॥
4.4.e: Send thy spies forward, fleetest in thy motion; be, ne’er deceived, the guardian of this people  From him who, near or far, is bent on evil, and let no trouble sent from thee o’ercome us.

4.4.d: उदग्ने तिष्ठ प्रत्या तनुष्व न्य१मित्राँ ओषतात्तिग्महेते । यो नो अरातिं समिधान चक्रे नीचा तं धक्ष्यतसं न शुष्कम् ॥
4.4.e: Rise up, O Agni, spread thee out before us: burn down our foes, thou who hast sharpened arrows.  Him, blazing Agni! who hath worked us mischief, consume thou utterly like dried-up stubble.

4.4.d: ऊर्ध्वो भव प्रति विध्याध्यस्मदाविष्कृणुष्व दैव्यान्यग्ने । अव स्थिरा तनुहि यातुजूनां जामिमजामिं प्र मृणीहि शत्रून् ॥
4.4.e: Rise, Agni, drive off those who fight against us: make manifest thine own celestial vigour.  Slacken the strong bows of the demon-driven: destroy our foemen whether kin or stranger.

4.4.d: स ते जानाति सुमतिं यविष्ठ य ईवते ब्रह्मणे गातुमैरत् । विश्वान्यस्मै सुदिनानि रायो द्युम्नान्यर्यो वि दुरो अभि द्यौत् ॥
4.4.e: Most Youthful God, he knoweth well thy favour who gave an impulse to this high devotion.  All fair days and magnificence of riches hast thou beamed forth upon the good man's portals.

4.4.d: सेदग्ने अस्तु सुभगः सुदानुर्यस्त्वा नित्येन हविषा य उक्थैः । पिप्रीषति स्व आयुषि दुरोणे विश्वेदस्मै सुदिना सासदिष्टिः ॥
4.4.e: Blest, Agni, be the man, the liberal giver, who with his lauds and regular oblation  Is fain to please thee for his life and dwelling. May all his days be bright: be this his longing.

4.4.d: अर्चामि ते सुमतिं घोष्यर्वाक्सं ते वावाता जरतामियं गीः । स्वश्वास्त्वा सुरथा मर्जयेमास्मे क्षत्राणि धारयेरनु द्यून् ॥
4.4.e: I praise thy gracious favour: sing in answer. May this my song sing like a loved one with thee.  Lords of good steeds and cars may we adorn thee, and day by day vouchsafe thou us dominion.

4.4.d: इह त्वा भूर्या चरेदुप त्मन्दोषावस्तर्दीदिवांसमनु द्यून् । क्रीळन्तस्त्वा सुमनसः सपेमाभि द्युम्ना तस्थिवांसो जनानाम् ॥
4.4.e: Here of free choice let each one serve thee richly, resplendent day by day at eve and morning.  So may we honour thee, content and joyous, passing beyond the glories of the people.

4.4.d: यस्त्वा स्वश्वः सुहिरण्यो अग्न उपयाति वसुमता रथेन । तस्य त्राता भवसि तस्य सखा यस्त आतिथ्यमानुषग्जुजोषत् ॥
4.4.e: Whoso with good steeds and fine gold, O Agni, comes nigh thee on a car laden with treasure,  His Friend art thou, yea, thou art his Protector whose joy it is to entertain thee duly.

4.4.d: महो रुजामि बन्धुता वचोभिस्तन्मा पितुर्गोतमादन्वियाय । त्वं नो अस्य वचसश्चिकिद्धि होतर्यविष्ठ सुक्रतो दमूनाः ॥
4.4.e: Through words and kinship I destroy the mighty: this power I have from Gotama my father.  Mark thou this speech of ours, O thou Most Youthful, Friend of the House, exceeding wise, Invoker.

4.4.d: अस्वप्नजस्तरणयः सुशेवा अतन्द्रासोऽवृका अश्रमिष्ठाः । ते पायवः सध्र्यञ्चो निषद्याग्ने तव नः पान्त्वमूर ॥
4.4.e: Knowing no slumber, speedy and propitious, alert and ever friendly, most unwearied,  May thy protecting powers, unerring Agni, taking their places here, combined, preserve us.

4.4.d: ये पायवो मामतेयं ते अग्ने पश्यन्तो अन्धं दुरितादरक्षन् । ररक्ष तान्त्सुकृतो विश्ववेदा दिप्सन्त इद्रिपवो नाह देभुः ॥
4.4.e: Thy guardian rays, O Agni, when they saw him, preserved blind Māmateya from affliction.  Lord of all riches, he preserved the pious: the fees who fain would harm them did no mischief

4.4.d: त्वया वयं सधन्य१स्त्वोतास्तव प्रणीत्यश्याम वाजान् । उभा शंसा सूदय सत्यतातेऽनुष्ठुया कृणुह्यह्रयाण ॥
4.4.e: Aided by thee with thee may we be wealthy, may we gain strength with thee to guide us onward.  Fulfil the words of both, O Ever Truthful: straightway do this, thou God whom power emboldens.

4.4.d: अया ते अग्ने समिधा विधेम प्रति स्तोमं शस्यमानं गृभाय । दहाशसो रक्षसः पाह्य१स्मान्द्रुहो निदो मित्रमहो अवद्यात् ॥
4.4.e: O Agni, with this fuel will we serve thee; accept the laud we sing to thee with favour  Destroy the cursing Rākṣasas: preserve us, O rich in friends, from guile and scorn and slander.

4.5.d: वैश्वानराय मीळ्हुषे सजोषाः कथा दाशेमाग्नये बृहद्भाः । अनूनेन बृहता वक्षथेनोप स्तभायदुपमिन्न रोधः ॥
4.5.e: How shall we give with one accord oblation to Agni, to Vaiśvānara the Bounteous?  Great light, with full high growth hath he uplifted, and, as a pillar bears the roof, sustains it.

4.5.d: मा निन्दत य इमां मह्यं रातिं देवो ददौ मर्त्याय स्वधावान् । पाकाय गृत्सो अमृतो विचेता वैश्वानरो नृतमो यह्वो अग्निः ॥
4.5.e: Reproach not him who, God and self-reliant, vouchsafed this bounty unto me a mortal,—  Deathless, discerner, wise, to me the simple, Vaiśvānara most manly, youthful Agni.

4.5.d: साम द्विबर्हा महि तिग्मभृष्टिः सहस्ररेता वृषभस्तुविष्मान् । पदं न गोरपगूळ्हं विविद्वानग्निर्मह्यं प्रेदु वोचन्मनीषाम् ॥
4.5.e: Sharp-pointed, powerful, strong, of boundless vigour, Agni who knows the lofty hymn, kept secret  As the lost milch-cow's track, the doubly Mighty,—he hath declared to me this hidden knowledge.

4.5.d: प्र ताँ अग्निर्बभसत्तिग्मजम्भस्तपिष्ठेन शोचिषा यः सुराधाः । प्र ये मिनन्ति वरुणस्य धाम प्रिया मित्रस्य चेततो ध्रुवाणि ॥
4.5.e: May he with sharpened teeth, the Bounteous Giver, Agni, consume with flame most fiercely glowing.  Those who regard not Varuṇa's commandments and the dear stedfast laws of sapient Mitra.

4.5.d: अभ्रातरो न योषणो व्यन्तः पतिरिपो न जनयो दुरेवाः । पापासः सन्तो अनृता असत्या इदं पदमजनता गभीरम् ॥
4.5.e: Like youthful women without brothers, straying, like dames who hate their lords, of evil conduct,  They who are full of sin, untrue, unfaithful, they have engendered this abysmal station.

4.5.d: इदं मे अग्ने कियते पावकामिनते गुरुं भारं न मन्म । बृहद्दधाथ धृषता गभीरं यह्वं पृष्ठं प्रयसा सप्तधातु ॥
4.5.e: To me, weak, innocent, thou, luminous Agni, hast boldly given as ’twere a heavy burthen,  This Pṛṣṭha hymn, profound and strong and mighty, of seven elements, and with offered dainties.

4.5.d: तमिन्न्वे३व समना समानमभि क्रत्वा पुनती धीतिरश्याः । ससस्य चर्मन्नधि चारु पृश्नेरग्रे रुप आरुपितं जबारु ॥
4.5.e: So may our song that purifies, through wisdom reach in a moment him the Universal,  Established on the height, on earth's best station, above the beauteous grassy skin of Pṛśni.

4.5.d: प्रवाच्यं वचसः किं मे अस्य गुहा हितमुप निणिग्वदन्ति । यदुस्रियाणामप वारिव व्रन्पाति प्रियं रुपो अग्रं पदं वेः ॥
4.5.e: Of this my speech what shall I utter further? They indicate the milk stored up in secret  When they have thrown as ’twere the cows' stalls open. The Bird protects earths’ best and well-loved station.

4.5.d: इदमु त्यन्महि महामनीकं यदुस्रिया सचत पूर्व्यं गौः । ऋतस्य पदे अधि दीद्यानं गुहा रघुष्यद्रघुयद्विवेद ॥
4.5.e: This is the Great Ones’ mighty apparition which from of old the radiant Cow hath followed.  This, shining brightly in the place of Order, swift, hasting on in secret, she discovered.

4.5.d: अध द्युतानः पित्रोः सचासामनुत गुह्यं चारु पृश्नेः । मातुष्पदे परमे अन्ति षद्गोर्वृष्णः शोचिषः प्रयतस्य जिह्वा ॥
4.5.e: He then who shone together with his Parents remembered Pṛśni's fair and secret treasure,  Which, in the Mother Cow's most lofty station, the Bull's tongue, of the flame bent forward, tasted.

4.5.d: ऋतं वोचे नमसा पृच्छ्यमानस्तवाशसा जातवेदो यदीदम् । त्वमस्य क्षयसि यद्ध विश्वं दिवि यदु द्रविणं यत्पृथिव्याम् ॥
4.5.e: With reverence I declare the Law, O Agni; what is, comes by thine order, Jātavedas.  Of this, whate’er it be, thou art the Sovran, yea, all the wealth that is in earth or  heaven.

4.5.d: किं नो अस्य द्रविणं कद्ध रत्नं वि नो वोचो जातवेदश्चिकित्वान् । गुहाध्वनः परमं यन्नो अस्य रेकु पदं न निदाना अगन्म ॥
4.5.e: What is our wealth therefrom, and what our treasure? Tell us O Jātavedas, for thou  knowest,  What is our best course in this secret passage: we, unreproached, have reached a place far distant.

4.5.d: का मर्यादा वयुना कद्ध वाममच्छा गमेम रघवो न वाजम् । कदा नो देवीरमृतस्य पत्नीः सूरो वर्णेन ततनन्नुषासः ॥
4.5.e: What is the limit, what the rules, the guerdon? Like fleet-foot coursers speed we to the contest.  When will the Goddesses, the Immortal's Spouses, the Dawns, spread over us the Sun-God's splendour?

4.5.d: अनिरेण वचसा फल्ग्वेन प्रतीत्येन कृधुनातृपासः । अधा ते अग्ने किमिहा वदन्त्यनायुधास आसता सचन्ताम् ॥
4.5.e: Unsatisfied, with speech devoid of vigour, scanty and frivolous and inconclusive,  Wherefore do they address thee here, O Agni? Let these who have no weapons suffer sorrow.

4.5.d: अस्य श्रिये समिधानस्य वृष्णो वसोरनीकं दम आ रुरोच । रुशद्वसानः सुदृशीकरूपः क्षितिर्न राया पुरुवारो अद्यौत् ॥
4.5.e: The majesty of him the Good, the Mighty, aflame, hath shone for glory in the dwelling.  He, clothed in light, hath shone most fair to look on, wealthy in boons, as a home shines with riches.

4.6.d: ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु णो अध्वरस्य होतरग्ने तिष्ठ देवताता यजीयान् । त्वं हि विश्वमभ्यसि मन्म प्र वेधसश्चित्तिरसि मनीषाम् ॥
4.6.e: PRIEST of our rite, stand up erect, O Agni, in the Gods’ service best of sacrificers,  For over evei y thought thou art the Ruler: thou furtherest e’en the wisdom of the pious.

4.6.d: अमूरो होता न्यसादि विक्ष्व१ग्निर्मन्द्रो विदथेषु प्रचेताः । ऊर्ध्वं भानुं सवितेवाश्रेन्मेतेव धूमं स्तभायदुप द्याम् ॥
4.6.e: He was set down mid men as Priest unerring, Agni, wise, welcome in our holy synods.  Like Savitar he hath lifted up his splendour, and like a builder raised his smoke to heaven.

4.6.d: यता सुजूर्णी रातिनी घृताची प्रदक्षिणिद्देवतातिमुराणः । उदु स्वरुर्नवजा नाक्रः पश्वो अनक्ति सुधितः सुमेकः ॥
4.6.e: The glowing ladle, filled with oil, is lifted; choosing Gods’ service to the right he circles.  Eager he rises like the new-wrought pillar which, firmly set and fixed, anoints the victims.

4.6.d: स्तीर्णे बर्हिषि समिधाने अग्ना ऊर्ध्वो अध्वर्युर्जुजुषाणो अस्थात् । पर्यग्निः पशुपा न होता त्रिविष्ट्येति प्रदिव उराणः ॥
4.6.e: When sacred grass is strewn and Agni kindled, the Adhvaryu rises to, his task rejoicing.  Agni the Priest, like one who tends the cattle, goes three times round, as from of old he wills it.

4.6.d: परि त्मना मितद्रुरेति होताग्निर्मन्द्रो मधुवचा ऋतावा । द्रवन्त्यस्य वाजिनो न शोका भयन्ते विश्वा भुवना यदभ्राट् ॥
4.6.e: Agni himself, the Priest, with measured motion, goes round, with sweet speech, cheerful, true to Order.  His fulgent flames run forth like vigorous horses; all creatures are affrighted when he blazes.

4.6.d: भद्रा ते अग्ने स्वनीक संदृग्घोरस्य सतो विषुणस्य चारुः । न यत्ते शोचिस्तमसा वरन्त न ध्वस्मानस्तन्वी३ रेप आ धुः ॥
4.6.e: Beautiful and auspicious is thine aspect, O lovely Agni, terrible when spreading.  Thy splendours are not covered by the darkness: detraction leaves no stain upon thy body.

4.6.d: न यस्य सातुर्जनितोरवारि न मातरापितरा नू चिदिष्टौ । अधा मित्रो न सुधितः पावको३ऽग्निर्दीदाय मानुषीषु विक्षु ॥
4.6.e: Naught hindered his production, Bounteous Giver: his Mother and his Sire were free to send him.  Then as Friend benevolent, refulgent, Agni shone forth in human habitations.

4.6.d: द्विर्यं पञ्च जीजनन्त्संवसानाः स्वसारो अग्निं मानुषीषु विक्षु । उषर्बुधमथर्यो३ न दन्तं शुक्रं स्वासं परशुं न तिग्मम् ॥
4.6.e: He, Agni, whom the twice-five sisters, dwelling together, in the homes of men engendered,  Bright like a spear's tooth, wakened in the morning, with powerful mouth and like an axe well-sharpened.

4.6.d: तव त्ये अग्ने हरितो घृतस्ना रोहितास ऋज्वञ्चः स्वञ्चः । अरुषासो वृषण ऋजुमुष्का आ देवतातिमह्वन्त दस्माः ॥
4.6.e: These thy Bay Coursers, Agni, dropping fatness, ruddy vigorous, speeding straightly forward,  And red steeds, wonderful, of mighty muscle, are to this service of the Gods invited:

4.6.d: ये ह त्ये ते सहमाना अयासस्त्वेषासो अग्ने अर्चयश्चरन्ति । श्येनासो न दुवसनासो अर्थं तुविष्वणसो मारुतं न शर्धः ॥
4.6.e: These brightly-shining games of thine, O Agni, that move for ever restless, all-subduing,  Like falcons hasting eagerly to the quarry, roar loudly like the army of the Maruts.

4.6.d: अकारि ब्रह्म समिधान तुभ्यं शंसात्युक्थं यजते व्यू धाः । होतारमग्निं मनुषो नि षेदुर्नमस्यन्त उशिजः शंसमायोः ॥
4.6.e: To thee, O flaming God, hath prayer been offered. Let the priest laud thee: give to him who worships.  Men have established Agni as Invoker, fain to adore the glory of the living.

4.7.d: अयमिह प्रथमो धायि धातृभिर्होता यजिष्ठो अध्वरेष्वीड्यः । यमप्नवानो भृगवो विरुरुचुर्वनेषु चित्रं विभ्वं विशेविशे ॥
4.7.e: HERE by ordainers was this God appointed first Invoker, best at worship, to be praised at rites:  Whom Apnavāna, and the Bhṛgus caused to shine bright-coloured in the wood, spreading from home to home.

4.7.d: अग्ने कदा त आनुषग्भुवद्देवस्य चेतनम् । अधा हि त्वा जगृभ्रिरे मर्तासो विक्ष्वीड्यम् ॥
4.7.e: When shall thy glory as a God, Agni, be suddenly shown forth.  For mortal men have held thee fast, adorable in all their homes,

4.7.d: ऋतावानं विचेतसं पश्यन्तो द्यामिव स्तृभिः । विश्वेषामध्वराणां हस्कर्तारं दमेदमे ॥
4.7.e: Seeing thee faithful to the Law, most sapient, like the starry heaven,  Illumining with cheerful ray each solemn rite in every house.

4.7.d: आशुं दूतं विवस्वतो विश्वा यश्चर्षणीरभि । आ जभ्रुः केतुमायवो भृगवाणं विशेविशे ॥
4.7.e: Vivasvān's envoy living men have taken as their ensign, swift,  The ruler over all mankind, moving like Bhṛgu in each home.

4.7.d: तमीं होतारमानुषक्चिकित्वांसं नि षेदिरे । रण्वं पावकशोचिषं यजिष्ठं सप्त धामभिः ॥
4.7.e: Him the intelligent have they placed duly as Invoking Priest,  Welcome, with sanctifying flame, best worshipper, with sevenfold might;

4.7.d: तं शश्वतीषु मातृषु वन आ वीतमश्रितम् । चित्रं सन्तं गुहा हितं सुवेदं कूचिदर्थिनम् ॥
4.7.e: In his Eternal Mothers, in the wood, concealed and unapproached,  Kept secret though his flames are bright seeking on all sides, quickly found.

4.7.d: ससस्य यद्वियुता सस्मिन्नूधन्नृतस्य धामन्रणयन्त देवाः । महाँ अग्निर्नमसा रातहव्यो वेरध्वराय सदमिदृतावा ॥
4.7.e: That as food spreads forth in this earthly udder, Gods may rejoice them in the home of Order,  Great Agni, served with reverence and oblation, flies ever to the sacrifice, the Faithful.

4.7.d: वेरध्वरस्य दूत्यानि विद्वानुभे अन्ता रोदसी संचिकित्वान् । दूत ईयसे प्रदिव उराणो विदुष्टरो दिव आरोधनानि ॥
4.7.e: Bird of each rite, skilled in an envoy's duties, knowing both worlds and that which lies between them,  Thou goest from of old a willing Herald, knowing full well heaven's innermost recesses.

4.7.d: कृष्णं त एम रुशतः पुरो भाश्चरिष्ण्व१र्चिर्वपुषामिदेकम् । यदप्रवीता दधते ह गर्भं सद्यश्चिज्जातो भवसीदु दूतः ॥
4.7.e: Bright God, thy path is black: light is before thee: thy moving splendour is the chief of wonders.  When she, yet unimpregnate, hath conceived thee, even when newly born thou art an envoy.

4.7.d: सद्यो जातस्य ददृशानमोजो यदस्य वातो अनुवाति शोचिः । वृणक्ति तिग्मामतसेषु जिह्वां स्थिरा चिदन्ना दयते वि जम्भैः ॥
4.7.e: Yet newly born, his vigour is apparent when the wind blows upon his fiery splendour,  His sharpened tongue he layeth on the brushwood, and with his teeth e’en solid food consumeth.

4.7.d: तृषु यदन्ना तृषुणा ववक्ष तृषुं दूतं कृणुते यह्वो अग्निः । वातस्य मेळिं सचते निजूर्वन्नाशुं न वाजयते हिन्वे अर्वा ॥
4.7.e: When he hath borne off food with swift flame swiftly, strong Agni makes himself a speedy envoy,  Follows the rustling of the wind, consuming, and courser-like, speeds, drives the swift horse onward.

4.8.d: दूतं वो विश्ववेदसं हव्यवाहममर्त्यम् । यजिष्ठमृञ्जसे गिरा ॥
4.8.e: YOUR envoy who possesses all, Immortal, bearer of your gifts,  Best worshipper, I woo with song.

4.8.d: स हि वेदा वसुधितिं महाँ आरोधनं दिवः । स देवाँ एह वक्षति ॥
4.8.e: He, Mighty, knows the gift of wealth, he knows the deep recess of heaven:  He shall bring hitherward the Gods.

4.8.d: स वेद देव आनमं देवाँ ऋतायते दमे । दाति प्रियाणि चिद्वसु ॥
4.8.e: He knows, a God himself, to guide Gods to the righteous in his home:  He gives e’en treasures that we love.

4.8.d: स होता सेदु दूत्यं चिकित्वाँ अन्तरीयते । विद्वाँ आरोधनं दिवः ॥
4.8.e: He is the Herald: well-informed, he doth his errand to and fro,  Knowing the deep recess of heaven.

4.8.d: ते स्याम ये अग्नये ददाशुर्हव्यदातिभिः । य ईं पुष्यन्त इन्धते ॥
4.8.e: May we be they who gratify Agni with sacrificial gifts,  Who cherish and enkindle him.

4.8.d: ते राया ते सुवीर्यैः ससवांसो वि शृण्विरे । ये अग्ना दधिरे दुवः ॥
4.8.e: Illustrious for wealth are they, and hero deeds, victorious,  Who have served Agni reverently.

4.8.d: अस्मे रायो दिवेदिवे सं चरन्तु पुरुस्पृहः । अस्मे वाजास ईरताम् ॥
4.8.e: So unto us, day after day, may riches craved by many come,  And power and might spring up for us.

4.8.d: स विप्रश्चर्षणीनां शवसा मानुषाणाम् । अति क्षिप्रेव विध्यति ॥
4.8.e: That holy Singer in his strength shoots forth his arrows swifter than  The swift shafts of the tribes of men.

4.9.d: अग्ने मृळ महाँ असि य ईमा देवयुं जनम् । इयेथ बर्हिरासदम् ॥
4.9.e: AGNI, show favour: great art thou who to this pious man art come,  To seat thee on the sacred grass.

4.9.d: स मानुषीषु दूळभो विक्षु प्रावीरमर्त्यः । दूतो विश्वेषां भुवत् ॥
4.9.e: May he the Immortal, Helper, bard to be deceived among mankind,  Become the messenger of all.

4.9.d: स सद्म परि णीयते होता मन्द्रो दिविष्टिषु । उत पोता नि षीदति ॥
4.9.e: Around the altar is he led, welcome Chief Priest at solemn rites,  Or as the Potar sits him down.

4.9.d: उत ग्ना अग्निरध्वर उतो गृहपतिर्दमे । उत ब्रह्मा नि षीदति ॥
4.9.e: Agni in fire at sacrifice, and in the house as Lord thereof,  And as a Brahman takes his seat.

4.9.d: वेषि ह्यध्वरीयतामुपवक्ता जनानाम् । हव्या च मानुषाणाम् ॥
4.9.e: Thou comest as the guide of folk who celebrate a sacrifice,  And to oblations brought by men.

4.9.d: वेषीद्वस्य दूत्यं१ यस्य जुजोषो अध्वरम् । हव्यं मर्तस्य वोळ्हवे ॥
4.9.e: Thou servest as his messenger whose sacrifice thou lovest well,  To bear the mortal's gifts to heaven.

4.9.d: अस्माकं जोष्यध्वरमस्माकं यज्ञमङ्गिरः । अस्माकं शृणुधी हवम् ॥
4.9.e: Accept our solemn rite; be pleased, Aṅgiras, with our sacrifice:  Give ear and listen to our call.

4.9.d: परि ते दूळभो रथोऽस्माँ अश्नोतु विश्वतः । येन रक्षसि दाशुषः ॥
4.9.e: May thine inviolable car, wherewith thou guardest those who give,  Come near to us from every side.

4.10.d: अग्ने तमद्याश्वं न स्तोमैः क्रतुं न भद्रं हृदिस्पृशम् । ऋध्यामा त ओहैः ॥
4.10.e: This day with praises, Agni, we bring thee that which thou lovest.  Right judgment, like a horse, with our devotions.

4.10.d: अधा ह्यग्ने क्रतोर्भद्रस्य दक्षस्य साधोः । रथीर्ऋतस्य बृहतो बभूथ ॥
4.10.e: For thou hast ever been the Car-driver, Agni, of noble  Strength, lofty sacrifice, and rightful judgment.

4.10.d: एभिर्नो अर्कैर्भवा नो अर्वाङ्स्व१र्ण ज्योतिः । अग्ने विश्वेभिः सुमना अनीकैः ॥
4.10.e: Through these our praises come thou to meet us, bright as the sunlight,  O Agni, well disposed, with all thine aspects.

4.10.d: आभिष्टे अद्य गीर्भिर्गृणन्तोऽग्ने दाशेम । प्र ते दिवो न स्तनयन्ति शुष्माः ॥
4.10.e: Now may we serve thee singing these lauds this day to thee, Agni.  Loud as the voice of Heaven thy blasts are roaring.

4.10.d: तव स्वादिष्ठाग्ने संदृष्टिरिदा चिदह्न इदा चिदक्तोः । श्रिये रुक्मो न रोचत उपाके ॥
4.10.e: Just at this time of the day and the night thy look is the sweetest:  It shineth near us even as gold for glory.

4.10.d: घृतं न पूतं तनूररेपाः शुचि हिरण्यम् । तत्ते रुक्मो न रोचत स्वधावः ॥
4.10.e: Spotless thy body, brilliant as gold, like clarified butter:  This gleams like gold on thee, O Self. dependent.

4.10.d: कृतं चिद्धि ष्मा सनेमि द्वेषोऽग्न इनोषि मर्तात् । इत्था यजमानादृतावः ॥
4.10.e: All hate and mischief, yea, if committed, Agni, thou turnest,  Holy One, from the man who rightly worships.

4.10.d: शिवा नः सख्या सन्तु भ्रात्राग्ने देवेषु युष्मे । सा नो नाभिः सदने सस्मिन्नूधन् ॥
4.10.e: Agni, with you Gods, prosperous be our friendships and kinships.  Be this our bond here by this place, thine altar.

4.11.d: भद्रं ते अग्ने सहसिन्ननीकमुपाक आ रोचते सूर्यस्य । रुशद्दृशे ददृशे नक्तया चिदरूक्षितं दृश आ रूपे अन्नम् ॥
4.11.e: THY blessed majesty, victorious Agni, shines brightly in the neighbourhood of Sūrya.  Splendid to see, it shows even at nighttime, and food is fair to look on in thy beauty.

4.11.d: वि षाह्यग्ने गृणते मनीषां खं वेपसा तुविजात स्तवानः । विश्वेभिर्यद्वावनः शुक्र देवैस्तन्नो रास्व सुमहो भूरि मन्म ॥
4.11.e: Agni, disclose his thought for him who singeth, the well, Strong God! while thou art praised with fervour.  Vouchsafe to us that powerful hymn, O Mighty, which, Radiant One! with all the Gods thou lovest.

4.11.d: त्वदग्ने काव्या त्वन्मनीषास्त्वदुक्था जायन्ते राध्यानि । त्वदेति द्रविणं वीरपेशा इत्थाधिये दाशुषे मर्त्याय ॥
4.11.e: From thee, O Agni, springs poetic wisdom, from thee come thoughts and hymns of praise that prosper;  From thee flows wealth, with heroes to adorn it, to the true-hearted man who gives oblation.

4.11.d: त्वद्वाजी वाजम्भरो विहाया अभिष्टिकृज्जायते सत्यशुष्मः । त्वद्रयिर्देवजूतो मयोभुस्त्वदाशुर्जूजुवाँ अग्ने अर्वा ॥
4.11.e: From thee the hero springs who wins the booty, bringer of help, mighty, of real courage.  From thee comes wealth, sent by the Gods, bliss-giving; Agni, from thee the fleet impetuous charger.

4.11.d: त्वामग्ने प्रथमं देवयन्तो देवं मर्ता अमृत मन्द्रजिह्वम् । द्वेषोयुतमा विवासन्ति धीभिर्दमूनसं गृहपतिममूरम् ॥
4.11.e: Immortal Agni, thee whose voice is pleasant, as first in rank, as God, religious mortals  Invite with hymns; thee who removest hatred, Friend of the Home, the household's Lord, unerring.

4.11.d: आरे अस्मदमतिमारे अंह आरे विश्वां दुर्मतिं यन्निपासि । दोषा शिवः सहसः सूनो अग्ने यं देव आ चित्सचसे स्वस्ति ॥
4.11.e: Far from us thou removest want and sorrow, far from us all ill-will when thou protectest.  Son of Strength, Agni, blest is he at evening, whom thou as God attendest for his welfare.

4.12.d: यस्त्वामग्न इनधते यतस्रुक्त्रिस्ते अन्नं कृणवत्सस्मिन्नहन् । स सु द्युम्नैरभ्यस्तु प्रसक्षत्तव क्रत्वा जातवेदश्चिकित्वान् ॥
4.12.e: WHOSO enkindles thee, with lifted ladle, and thrice this day offers thee food, O Agni,  May he excel, triumphant through thy splendours, wise through thy mental power, O Jātavedas.

4.12.d: इध्मं यस्ते जभरच्छश्रमाणो महो अग्ने अनीकमा सपर्यन् । स इधानः प्रति दोषामुषासं पुष्यन्रयिं सचते घ्नन्नमित्रान् ॥
4.12.e: Whoso with toil and trouble brings thee fuel, serving the majesty of mighty Agni,  He, kindling thee at evening and at morning, prospers, and comes to wealth, and slays his foemen.

4.12.d: अग्निरीशे बृहतः क्षत्रियस्याग्निर्वाजस्य परमस्य रायः । दधाति रत्नं विधते यविष्ठो व्यानुषङ्मर्त्याय स्वधावान् ॥
4.12.e: Agni is Master of sublime dominion, Agni is Lord of strength and lofty riches.  Straightway the self-reliant God, Most Youthful, gives treasures to the mortal who adores him.

4.12.d: यच्चिद्धि ते पुरुषत्रा यविष्ठाचित्तिभिश्चकृमा कच्चिदागः । कृधी ष्व१स्माँ अदितेरनागान्व्येनांसि शिश्रथो विष्वगग्ने ॥
4.12.e: Most Youthful God, whatever sin, through folly, we here, as human beings, have committed,  In sight of Aditi make thou us sinless remit, entirely, Agni, our offences.

4.12.d: महश्चिदग्न एनसो अभीक ऊर्वाद्देवानामुत मर्त्यानाम् । मा ते सखायः सदमिद्रिषाम यच्छा तोकाय तनयाय शं योः ॥
4.12.e: Even in the presence of great sin, O Agni, free us from prison of the Gods or mortals.  Never may we who are thy friends be injured: grant health and strength unto our seed and offspring.

4.12.d: यथा ह त्यद्वसवो गौर्यं चित्पदि षिताममुञ्चता यजत्राः । एवो ष्व१स्मन्मुञ्चता व्यंहः प्र तार्यग्ने प्रतरं न आयुः ॥
4.12.e: Even as ye here, Gods Excellent and Holy, have loosed the cow that by the foot was tethered,  So also set us free from this affliction long let our life, O Agni, be extended.

4.13.d: प्रत्यग्निरुषसामग्रमख्यद्विभातीनां सुमना रत्नधेयम् । यातमश्विना सुकृतो दुरोणमुत्सूर्यो ज्योतिषा देव एति ॥
4.13.e: AGNI hath looked, benevolently-minded, on the wealth-giving spring of radiant Mornings.  Come, Aśvins, to the dwelling of the pious: Sūrya the God is rising with his splendour.

4.13.d: ऊर्ध्वं भानुं सविता देवो अश्रेद्द्रप्सं दविध्वद्गविषो न सत्वा । अनु व्रतं वरुणो यन्ति मित्रो यत्सूर्यं दिव्यारोहयन्ति ॥
4.13.e: Savitar, God, hath spread on high his lustre, waving his flag like a spoil-seeking hero.  Their stablished way go Varuṇa and Mitra, what time they make the Sun ascend the heaven.

4.13.d: यं सीमकृण्वन्तमसे विपृचे ध्रुवक्षेमा अनवस्यन्तो अर्थम् । तं सूर्यं हरितः सप्त यह्वीः स्पशं विश्वस्य जगतो वहन्ति ॥
4.13.e: Him whom they made to drive away the darkness, Lords of sure mansions, constant to their object,  Him who beholds the universe, the Sun-God, seven strong and youthful Coursers carry onward.

4.13.d: वहिष्ठेभिर्विहरन्यासि तन्तुमवव्ययन्नसितं देव वस्म । दविध्वतो रश्मयः सूर्यस्य चर्मेवावाधुस्तमो अप्स्व१न्तः ॥
4.13.e: Spreading thy web with mightiest Steeds thou comest, rending apart, thou God, the black-hued mantle.  The rays of Sūrya tremulously shining sink, like a hide, the darkness in the waters.

4.13.d: अनायतो अनिबद्धः कथायं न्यङ्ङुत्तानोऽव पद्यते न । कया याति स्वधया को ददर्श दिवः स्कम्भः समृतः पाति नाकम् ॥
4.13.e: How is it that, unbound and not supported, he falleth not although directed downward?  By what self power moves he? Who hath seen it? He guards the vault of heaven, a close-set pillar.

4.14.d: प्रत्यग्निरुषसो जातवेदा अख्यद्देवो रोचमाना महोभिः । आ नासत्योरुगाया रथेनेमं यज्ञमुप नो यातमच्छ ॥
4.14.e: THE God hath looked, even Agni Jātavedas, to meet the Dawns refulgent in their glories.  Come on your chariot, ye who travel widely, come to this sacrifice of ours, Nāsatyas.

4.14.d: ऊर्ध्वं केतुं सविता देवो अश्रेज्ज्योतिर्विश्वस्मै भुवनाय कृण्वन् । आप्रा द्यावापृथिवी अन्तरिक्षं वि सूर्यो रश्मिभिश्चेकितानः ॥
4.14.e: Producing light for all the world of creatures, God Savitar hath raised aloft his banner.  Making his presence known by sunbeams, Sūrya hath filled the firmament and earth and heaven.

4.14.d: आवहन्त्यरुणीर्ज्योतिषागान्मही चित्रा रश्मिभिश्चेकिताना । प्रबोधयन्ती सुविताय देव्यु१षा ईयते सुयुजा रथेन ॥
4.14.e: Red Dawn is come, riding with brightness onward, distinguished by her beams, gay-hued and mighty.  Dawn on her nobly-harnessed car, the Goddess, awaking men to happiness, approacheth.

4.14.d: आ वां वहिष्ठा इह ते वहन्तु रथा अश्वास उषसो व्युष्टौ । इमे हि वां मधुपेयाय सोमा अस्मिन्यज्ञे वृषणा मादयेथाम् ॥
4.14.e: May those most powerful steeds and chariot bring you, O Aśvins, hither at the break of morning.  Here for your draught of meath are Soma juices: at this our sacrifice rejoice, ye Mighty.

4.14.d: अनायतो अनिबद्धः कथायं न्यङ्ङुत्तानोऽव पद्यते न । कया याति स्वधया को ददर्श दिवः स्कम्भः समृतः पाति नाकम् ॥
4.14.e: How is it that, unbound and unsupported, he falleth not although directed downward?  By what self-power moves he? Who hath seen it? He guards the vault of heaven, a close-set pillar?

4.15.d: अग्निर्होता नो अध्वरे वाजी सन्परि णीयते । देवो देवेषु यज्ञियः ॥
4.15.e: AGNI the Herald, like a horse, is led forth at our solemn rite,  God among Gods adorable.

4.15.d: परि त्रिविष्ट्यध्वरं यात्यग्नी रथीरिव । आ देवेषु प्रयो दधत् ॥
4.15.e: Three times unto our solemn rite comes Agni like a charioteer,  Bearing the viands to the Gods.
Round the oblations hath he paced, Agni the Wise, the Lord of Strength,  Giving the offerer precious boons.

4.15.d: अयं यः सृञ्जये पुरो दैववाते समिध्यते । द्युमाँ अमित्रदम्भनः ॥
4.15.e: He who is kindled eastward for Sṛñjaya, Devāvata's son,  Resplendent, tamer of the foe.

4.15.d: अस्य घा वीर ईवतोऽग्नेरीशीत मर्त्यः । तिग्मजम्भस्य मीळ्हुषः ॥
4.15.e: So mighty be the Agni whom the mortal hero shall command,  With sharpened teeth and bountiful.

4.15.d: तमर्वन्तं न सानसिमरुषं न दिवः शिशुम् । मर्मृज्यन्ते दिवेदिवे ॥
4.15.e: Day after day they dress him, as they clean a horse who wins the prize.  Dress the red Scion of the Sky.

4.15.d: बोधद्यन्मा हरिभ्यां कुमारः साहदेव्यः । अच्छा न हूत उदरम् ॥
4.15.e: When Sahadeva's princely son with two bay horses thought of me,  Summoned by him I drew not back.

4.15.d: उत त्या यजता हरी कुमारात्साहदेव्यात् । प्रयता सद्य आ ददे ॥
4.15.e: And truly those two noble bays I straightway took when offered me,  From Sahadeva's princely son.

4.15.d: एष वां देवावश्विना कुमारः साहदेव्यः । दीर्घायुरस्तु सोमकः ॥
4.15.e: Long, O ye Aśvins, may he live, your care, ye Gods, the princely son.  Of Sahadeva, Somaka.

4.15.d: तं युवं देवावश्विना कुमारं साहदेव्यम् । दीर्घायुषं कृणोतन ॥
4.15.e: Cause him the youthful prince, the son of Sahadeva, to enjoy  Long life, O Aśvins, O ye Gods.

4.16.d: आ सत्यो यातु मघवाँ ऋजीषी द्रवन्त्वस्य हरय उप नः । तस्मा इदन्धः सुषुमा सुदक्षमिहाभिपित्वं करते गृणानः ॥
4.16.e: IMPETUOUS, true, let Maghavan come hither, and let his Tawny Coursers speed to reach us.  For him have we pressed juice exceeding potent: here, praised with song, let him effect his visit.

4.16.d: अव स्य शूराध्वनो नान्तेऽस्मिन्नो अद्य सवने मन्दध्यै । शंसात्युक्थमुशनेव वेधाश्चिकितुषे असुर्याय मन्म ॥
4.16.e: Unyoke, as at thy journey's end, O Hero, to gladden thee today at this libation.  Like Uśanā, the priest a laud shall utter, a hymn to thee, the Lord Divine, who markest.

4.16.d: कविर्न निण्यं विदथानि साधन्वृषा यत्सेकं विपिपानो अर्चात् । दिव इत्था जीजनत्सप्त कारूनह्ना चिच्चक्रुर्वयुना गृणन्तः ॥
4.16.e: When the Bull, quaffing, praises our libation, as a sage paying holy rites in secret,  Seven singers here from heaven hath he begotten, who e’en by day have wrought their works while singing.

4.16.d: स्व१र्यद्वेदि सुदृशीकमर्कैर्महि ज्योती रुरुचुर्यद्ध वस्तोः । अन्धा तमांसि दुधिता विचक्षे नृभ्यश्चकार नृतमो अभिष्टौ ॥
4.16.e: When heaven's fair light by hymns was made apparent (they made great splendour shine at break of morning),  He with his succour, best of Heroes, scattered the blinding darkness so that men saw clearly.

4.16.d: ववक्ष इन्द्रो अमितमृजीष्यु१भे आ पप्रौ रोदसी महित्वा । अतश्चिदस्य महिमा वि रेच्यभि यो विश्वा भुवना बभूव ॥
4.16.e: Indra, Impetuous One, hath waxed immensely: he with his vastness hath filled earth and heaven.  E’en beyond this his majesty extendeth who hath exceeded all the worlds in greatness.

4.16.d: विश्वानि शक्रो नर्याणि विद्वानपो रिरेच सखिभिर्निकामैः । अश्मानं चिद्ये बिभिदुर्वचोभिर्व्रजं गोमन्तमुशिजो वि वव्रुः ॥
4.16.e: Śakra who knoweth well all human actions hath with his eager Friends let loose the waters.  They with their songs cleft e’en the mountain open and willingly disclosed the stall of cattle.

4.16.d: अपो वृत्रं वव्रिवांसं पराहन्प्रावत्ते वज्रं पृथिवी सचेताः । प्रार्णांसि समुद्रियाण्यैनोः पतिर्भवञ्छवसा शूर धृष्णो ॥
4.16.e: He smote away the floods' obstructer, Vṛtra; Earth, conscious, lent her aid to speed thy thunder.  Thou sentest forth the waters of the ocean, as Lord through power and might, O daring Hero.

4.16.d: अपो यदद्रिं पुरुहूत दर्दराविर्भुवत्सरमा पूर्व्यं ते । स नो नेता वाजमा दर्षि भूरिं गोत्रा रुजन्नङ्गिरोभिर्गृणानः ॥
4.16.e: When, Much-invoked! the water's rock thou cleftest, Saramā showed herself and went before thee.  Hymned by Aṅgirases, bursting the cow-stalls, much strength thou foundest for us as our leader.

4.16.d: अच्छा कविं नृमणो गा अभिष्टौ स्वर्षाता मघवन्नाधमानम् । ऊतिभिस्तमिषणो द्युम्नहूतौ नि मायावानब्रह्मा दस्युरर्त ॥
4.16.e: Come, Maghavan, Friend of Man, to aid the singer imploring thee in battle for the sunlight.  Speed him with help in his inspired invokings: down sink the sorcerer, the prayerless Dasyu.

4.16.d: आ दस्युघ्ना मनसा याह्यस्तं भुवत्ते कुत्सः सख्ये निकामः । स्वे योनौ नि षदतं सरूपा वि वां चिकित्सदृतचिद्ध नारी ॥
4.16.e: Come to our home resolved to slay the Dasyu: Kutsa longed eagerly to win thy friendship.  Alike in form ye both sate in his dwelling the faithful Lady was in doubt between you.

4.16.d: यासि कुत्सेन सरथमवस्युस्तोदो वातस्य हर्योरीशानः । ऋज्रा वाजं न गध्यं युयूषन्कविर्यदहन्पार्याय भूषात् ॥
4.16.e: Thou comest, fain to succour him, with Kutsa,—a goad that masters both the Wind-God's horses,  That, holding the brown steeds like spoil for capture, the sage may on the final day be present.

4.16.d: कुत्साय शुष्णमशुषं नि बर्हीः प्रपित्वे अह्नः कुयवं सहस्रा । सद्यो दस्यून्प्र मृण कुत्स्येन प्र सूरश्चक्रं वृहतादभीके ॥
4.16.e: For Kutsa, with thy thousand, thou at day-break didst hurl down greedy Śuṣṇa, foe of harvest.  Quickly with Kutsa's friend destroy the Dasyus, and roll the chariot-wheel of Sūrya near us.

4.16.d: त्वं पिप्रुं मृगयं शूशुवांसमृजिश्वने वैदथिनाय रन्धीः । पञ्चाशत्कृष्णा नि वपः सहस्रात्कं न पुरो जरिमा वि दर्दः ॥
4.16.e: Thou to the son of Vidathin, Ṛjiśvan, gavest up mighty Mṛgaya and Pipru.  Thou smotest down the swarthy fifty thousand, and rentest forts as age consumes a garment.

4.16.d: सूर उपाके तन्वं१ दधानो वि यत्ते चेत्यमृतस्य वर्पः । मृगो न हस्ती तविषीमुषाणः सिंहो न भीम आयुधानि बिभ्रत् ॥
4.16.e: What time thou settest near the Sun thy body, thy form, Immortal One, is seen expanding:  Thou a wild elephant with might invested. like a dread lion as thou wieldest weapons.

4.16.d: इन्द्रं कामा वसूयन्तो अग्मन्त्स्वर्मीळ्हे न सवने चकानाः । श्रवस्यवः शशमानास उक्थैरोको न रण्वा सुदृशीव पुष्टिः ॥
4.16.e: Wishes for wealth have gone to Indra, longing for him in war for light and at libation,  Eager for glory, labouring with praisesongs: he is like home, like sweet and fair nutrition.

4.16.d: तमिद्व इन्द्रं सुहवं हुवेम यस्ता चकार नर्या पुरूणि । यो मावते जरित्रे गध्यं चिन्मक्षू वाजं भरति स्पार्हराधाः ॥
4.16.e: Call we for you that Indra, prompt to listen, him who hath done so much for men's advantage;  Who, Lord of envied bounty, to a singer like me brings quickly booty worth the capture.

4.16.d: तिग्मा यदन्तरशनिः पताति कस्मिञ्चिच्छूर मुहुके जनानाम् । घोरा यदर्य समृतिर्भवात्यध स्मा नस्तन्वो बोधि गोपाः ॥
4.16.e: When the sharp-pointed arrow, O thou Hero, flieth mid any conflict of the people,  When, Faithful One, the dread encounter cometh, then be thou the Protector of our body.

4.16.d: भुवोऽविता वामदेवस्य धीनां भुवः सखावृको वाजसातौ । त्वामनु प्रमतिमा जगन्मोरुशंसो जरित्रे विश्वध स्याः ॥
4.16.e: Further the holy thoughts of Vamadeva be thou a guileless Friend in fight for booty.  We come to thee whose providence protects us: wide be thy sway for ever for thy singer.

4.16.d: एभिर्नृभिरिन्द्र त्वायुभिष्ट्वा मघवद्भिर्मघवन्विश्व आजौ । द्यावो न द्युम्नैरभि सन्तो अर्यः क्षपो मदेम शरदश्च पूर्वीः ॥
4.16.e: O Indra, with these men who love thee truly, free givers, Maghavan, in every battle,  May we rejoice through many autumns, quelling our foes, as days subdue the nights with splendour.

4.16.d: एवेदिन्द्राय वृषभाय वृष्णे ब्रह्माकर्म भृगवो न रथम् । नू चिद्यथा नः सख्या वियोषदसन्न उग्रोऽविता तनूपाः ॥
4.16.e: Now, as the Bhṛgus wrought a car, for Indra the Strong, the Mighty, we our prayer have fashioned,  That he may, ne’er withdraw from us his friendship, but be our bodies' guard and strong defender.

4.16.d: नू ष्टुत इन्द्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो३ न पीपेः । अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
4.16.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell. high like rivers for the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.17.d: त्वं महाँ इन्द्र तुभ्यं ह क्षा अनु क्षत्रं मंहना मन्यत द्यौः । त्वं वृत्रं शवसा जघन्वान्त्सृजः सिन्धूँरहिना जग्रसानान् ॥
4.17.e: GREAT art thou, Indra; yea, the earth, with gladness, and heaven confess to thee thine high dominion.  Thou in thy vigour having slaughtered Vṛtra didst free the floods arrested by the Dragon.

4.17.d: तव त्विषो जनिमन्रेजत द्यौ रेजद्भूमिर्भियसा स्वस्य मन्योः । ऋघायन्त सुभ्व१ः पर्वतास आर्दन्धन्वानि सरयन्त आपः ॥
4.17.e: Heaven trembled at the birth of thine effulgence; Earth trembled at the fear of thy displeasure.  The stedfast mountains shook in agitation . the waters flowed, and desert spots were flooded.

4.17.d: भिनद्गिरिं शवसा वज्रमिष्णन्नाविष्कृण्वानः सहसान ओजः । वधीद्वृत्रं वज्रेण मन्दसानः सरन्नापो जवसा हतवृष्णीः ॥
4.17.e: Hurling his bolt with might he cleft the mountain, while, putting forth his strength, he showed his vigour.  He slaughtered Vṛtra with his bolt, exulting, and, their lord slain, forth flowed the waters swiftly.

4.17.d: सुवीरस्ते जनिता मन्यत द्यौरिन्द्रस्य कर्ता स्वपस्तमो भूत् । य ईं जजान स्वर्यं सुवज्रमनपच्युतं सदसो न भूम ॥
4.17.e: Thy Father Dyaus esteemed himself a hero: most noble was the work of Indra's Maker,  His who begat the strong bolt's Lord who roareth, immovable like earth from her foundation.

4.17.d: य एक इच्च्यावयति प्र भूमा राजा कृष्टीनां पुरुहूत इन्द्रः । सत्यमेनमनु विश्वे मदन्ति रातिं देवस्य गृणतो मघोनः ॥
4.17.e: He who alone o’erthrows the world of creatures, Indra the peoples' King, invoked of many-  Verily all rejoice in him, extolling the boons which Maghavan the God hath sent them.

4.17.d: सत्रा सोमा अभवन्नस्य विश्वे सत्रा मदासो बृहतो मदिष्ठाः । सत्राभवो वसुपतिर्वसूनां दत्रे विश्वा अधिथा इन्द्र कृष्टीः ॥
4.17.e: All Soma juices are his own for ever, most gladdening draughts are ever his, the Mighty,  Thou ever wast the Treasure-Lord of treasures: Indra, thou lettest all folk share thy bounty.

4.17.d: त्वमध प्रथमं जायमानोऽमे विश्वा अधिथा इन्द्र कृष्टीः । त्वं प्रति प्रवत आशयानमहिं वज्रेण मघवन्वि वृश्चः ॥
4.17.e: Moreover, when thou first wast born, O Indra, thou struckest terror into all the people.  Thou, Maghavan, rentest with thy bolt the Dragon who lay against the waterfloods of heaven.

4.17.d: सत्राहणं दाधृषिं तुम्रमिन्द्रं महामपारं वृषभं सुवज्रम् । हन्ता यो वृत्रं सनितोत वाजं दाता मघानि मघवा सुराधाः ॥
4.17.e: The ever-slaying, bold and furious Indra, the bright bolt's Lord, infinite, strong and mighty,  Who slayeth Vṛtra and acquireth booty, giver of blessings, Maghavan the bounteous:

4.17.d: अयं वृतश्चातयते समीचीर्य आजिषु मघवा शृण्व एकः । अयं वाजं भरति यं सनोत्यस्य प्रियासः सख्ये स्याम ॥
4.17.e: Alone renowned as Maghavan in battles, he frighteneth away assembled armies.  He bringeth us the booty that he winneth may we, well-loved, continue in his friendship.

4.17.d: अयं शृण्वे अध जयन्नुत घ्नन्नयमुत प्र कृणुते युधा गाः । यदा सत्यं कृणुते मन्युमिन्द्रो विश्वं दृळ्हं भयत एजदस्मात् ॥
4.17.e: Renowned is he when conquering and when slaying: 'fis he who winneth cattle in the combat.  When Indra hardeneth his indignation all that is fixed and all that moveth fear him.

4.17.d: समिन्द्रो गा अजयत्सं हिरण्या समश्विया मघवा यो ह पूर्वीः । एभिर्नृभिर्नृतमो अस्य शाकै रायो विभक्ता सम्भरश्च वस्वः ॥
4.17.e: Indra hath won all kine, all gold, all horses,—Maghavan, he who breaketh forts in pieces;  Most manly with these men of his who help him, dealing out wealth and gathering the treasure.

4.17.d: कियत्स्विदिन्द्रो अध्येति मातुः कियत्पितुर्जनितुर्यो जजान । यो अस्य शुष्मं मुहुकैरियर्ति वातो न जूतः स्तनयद्भिरभ्रैः ॥
4.17.e: What is the care of Indra for his Mother, what cares he for the Father who begat him?  His care is that which speeds his might in conflicts, like wind borne onward by the clouds that thunder.

4.17.d: क्षियन्तं त्वमक्षियन्तं कृणोतीयर्ति रेणुं मघवा समोहम् । विभञ्जनुरशनिमाँ इव द्यौरुत स्तोतारं मघवा वसौ धात् ॥
4.17.e: Maghavan makes the settled man unsettled: he scatters dust that he hath swept together,  Breaking in pieces like Heaven armed with lightning: Maghavan shall enrich the man who lauds h;m.

4.17.d: अयं चक्रमिषणत्सूर्यस्य न्येतशं रीरमत्ससृमाणम् । आ कृष्ण ईं जुहुराणो जिघर्ति त्वचो बुध्ने रजसो अस्य योनौ ॥
4.17.e: He urged the chariot-wheel of Sūrya forward: Etaśa, speeding on his way, he rested.  Him the black undulating cloud bedeweth, in this mid-air's depth, at the base of darkness,

4.17.d: असिक्न्यां यजमानो न होता ॥
4.17.e: As in the night the sacrificing priest.

4.17.d: गव्यन्त इन्द्रं सख्याय विप्रा अश्वायन्तो वृषणं वाजयन्तः । जनीयन्तो जनिदामक्षितोतिमा च्यावयामोऽवते न कोशम् ॥
4.17.e: Eager for booty, craving strength and horses, we-singers stir Indra, the strong, for friendship,  Who gives the wives we seek, whose succour fails not, to hasten, like a pitcher to the fountain.

4.17.d: त्राता नो बोधि ददृशान आपिरभिख्याता मर्डिता सोम्यानाम् । सखा पिता पितृतमः पितॄणां कर्तेमु लोकमुशते वयोधाः ॥
4.17.e: Be thou our guardian, show thyself our kinsman, watching and blessing those who pour the Soma;  As Friend, as Sire, most fatherly of fathers giving the suppliant vital strength and freedom.

4.17.d: सखीयतामविता बोधि सखा गृणान इन्द्र स्तुवते वयो धाः । वयं ह्या ते चकृमा सबाध आभिः शमीभिर्महयन्त इन्द्र ॥
4.17.e: Be helping Friend of those who seek thy friendship . give life, when lauded, Indra, to the singer.  For, Indra, we the priests have paid thee worship, exalting thee with these our sacrifices.

4.17.d: स्तुत इन्द्रो मघवा यद्ध वृत्रा भूरीण्येको अप्रतीनि हन्ति । अस्य प्रियो जरिता यस्य शर्मन्नकिर्देवा वारयन्ते न मर्ताः ॥
4.17.e: Alone, when Indra Maghavan is lauded, he slayeth many ne’er-resisted Vṛtras.  Him in whose keeping is the well-loved singer never do Gods or mortals stay or hinder.

4.17.d: एवा न इन्द्रो मघवा विरप्शी करत्सत्या चर्षणीधृदनर्वा । त्वं राजा जनुषां धेह्यस्मे अधि श्रवो माहिनं यज्जरित्रे ॥
4.17.e: E’en so let Maghavan, the loud-voiced Indra, give us true blessings, foeless, men's upholder.  King of all creatures, give us glory amply, exalted glory due to him who lauds thee.

4.17.d: नू ष्टुत इन्द्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो३ न पीपेः । अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
4.17.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell high like rivers for the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays! is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.18.d: अयं पन्था अनुवित्तः पुराणो यतो देवा उदजायन्त विश्वे । अतश्चिदा जनिषीष्ट प्रवृद्धो मा मातरममुया पत्तवे कः ॥
4.18.e: THIS is the ancient and accepted pathway by which all Gods have come into existence.  Hereby could one be born though waxen mighty. Let him not, otherwise, destroy his Mother.

4.18.d: नाहमतो निरया दुर्गहैतत्तिरश्चता पार्श्वान्निर्गमाणि । बहूनि मे अकृता कर्त्वानि युध्यै त्वेन सं त्वेन पृच्छै ॥
4.18.e: Not this way go I forth: hard is the passage. Forth from the side obliquely will I issue.  Much that is yet undone must I accomplish; one must I combat and the other question.

4.18.d: परायतीं मातरमन्वचष्ट न नानु गान्यनु नू गमानि । त्वष्टुर्गृहे अपिबत्सोममिन्द्रः शतधन्यं चम्वोः सुतस्य ॥
4.18.e: He bent his eye upon the dying Mother: My word I now withdraw. That way I follow.  In Tvaṣṭar's dwelling India drank the Soma, a hundredworth of juice pressed from the mortar.

4.18.d: किं स ऋधक्कृणवद्यं सहस्रं मासो जभार शरदश्च पूर्वीः । नही न्वस्य प्रतिमानमस्त्यन्तर्जातेषूत ये जनित्वाः ॥
4.18.e: What strange act shall he do, he whom his Mother bore for a thousand months and many autumns?  No peer hath he among those born already, nor among those who shall be born hereafter.

4.18.d: अवद्यमिव मन्यमाना गुहाकरिन्द्रं माता वीर्येणा न्यृष्टम् । अथोदस्थात्स्वयमत्कं वसान आ रोदसी अपृणाज्जायमानः ॥
4.18.e: Deeming him a reproach, his mother hid him, Indra, endowed with all heroic valour.  Then up he sprang himself, assumed his vesture, and filled, as soon as born, the earth and heaven.

4.18.d: एता अर्षन्त्यललाभवन्तीर्ऋतावरीरिव संक्रोशमानाः । एता वि पृच्छ किमिदं भनन्ति कमापो अद्रिं परिधिं रुजन्ति ॥
4.18.e: With lively motion onward flow these waters, the Holy Ones, shouting, as ’twere, together.  Ask them to. tell thee what the floods are saying, what girdling rock the waters burst asunder.

4.18.d: किमु ष्विदस्मै निविदो भनन्तेन्द्रस्यावद्यं दिधिषन्त आपः । ममैतान्पुत्रो महता वधेन वृत्रं जघन्वाँ असृजद्वि सिन्धून् ॥
4.18.e: Are they addressing him with words of welcome? Will the floods take on them the shame of Indra?  With his great thunderbolt my Son hath slaughtered Vṛtra, and set these rivers free to wander.

4.18.d: ममच्चन त्वा युवतिः परास ममच्चन त्वा कुषवा जगार । ममच्चिदापः शिशवे ममृड्युर्ममच्चिदिन्द्रः सहसोदतिष्ठत् ॥
4.18.e: I cast thee from me, mine,—thy youthful mother: thee, mine own offspring, Kusava hath swallowed.  To him, mine infant, were the waters gracious. Indra, my Son, rose up in conquering vigour.

4.18.d: ममच्चन ते मघवन्व्यंसो निविविध्वाँ अप हनू जघान । अधा निविद्ध उत्तरो बभूवाञ्छिरो दासस्य सं पिणग्वधेन ॥
4.18.e: Thou art mine own, O Maghavan, whom Vyaṁsa struck to the ground and smote thy jaws in pieces.  But, smitten through, the mastery thou wonnest, and with thy bolt the Dāsa's head thou crushedst.

4.18.d: गृष्टिः ससूव स्थविरं तवागामनाधृष्यं वृषभं तुम्रमिन्द्रम् । अरीळ्हं वत्सं चरथाय माता स्वयं गातुं तन्व इच्छमानम् ॥
4.18.e: The Heifer hath brought forth the Strong, the Mighty, the unconquerable Bull, the furious Indra.  The Mother left her unlicked Calf to wander, seeking himself, the path that he would follow.

4.18.d: उत माता महिषमन्ववेनदमी त्वा जहति पुत्र देवाः । अथाब्रवीद्वृत्रमिन्द्रो हनिष्यन्त्सखे विष्णो वितरं वि क्रमस्व ॥
4.18.e: Then to her mighty Child the Mother turned her, saying, My son, these Deities forsake thee.  Then Indra said, about to slaughter Vṛtra, O my friend Vṛtra, stride full boldly forward.

4.18.d: कस्ते मातरं विधवामचक्रच्छयुं कस्त्वामजिघांसच्चरन्तम् । कस्ते देवो अधि मार्डीक आसीद्यत्प्राक्षिणाः पितरं पादगृह्य ॥
4.18.e: Who was he then who made thy Mother widow? Who sought to stay thee lying still or moving?  What God, when by the foot thy Sire thou tookest and slewest, was at hand to give thee comfort?

4.18.d: अवर्त्या शुन आन्त्राणि पेचे न देवेषु विविदे मर्डितारम् । अपश्यं जायाममहीयमानामधा मे श्येनो मध्वा जभार ॥
4.18.e: In deep distress I cooked a dog's intestines. Among the Gods I found not one to comfort.  My consort I beheld in degradation. The Falcon then brought me the pleasant Soma.

4.19.d: एवा त्वामिन्द्र वज्रिन्नत्र विश्वे देवासः सुहवास ऊमाः । महामुभे रोदसी वृद्धमृष्वं निरेकमिद्वृणते वृत्रहत्ये ॥
4.19.e: THEE, verily, O Thunder-wielding Indra, all the Gods here, the Helpers swift to listen,  And both the worlds elected, thee the Mighty, High, waxen strong, alone to slaughter Vṛtra.

4.19.d: अवासृजन्त जिव्रयो न देवा भुवः सम्राळिन्द्र सत्ययोनिः । अहन्नहिं परिशयानमर्णः प्र वर्तनीररदो विश्वधेनाः ॥
4.19.e: The Gods, as worn witheld, relaxed their efforts: thou, Indra, born of truth, wast Sovran Ruler.  Thou slewest Ahi who besieged the waters, and duggest out their all-supporting channels.

4.19.d: अतृप्णुवन्तं वियतमबुध्यमबुध्यमानं सुषुपाणमिन्द्र । सप्त प्रति प्रवत आशयानमहिं वज्रेण वि रिणा अपर्वन् ॥
4.19.e: The insatiate one, extended, hard to waken, who slumbered in perpetual sleep, O Indra,—  The Dragon stretched against the seven prone rivers, where no joint was, thou rentest with thy thunder.

4.19.d: अक्षोदयच्छवसा क्षाम बुध्नं वार्ण वातस्तविषीभिरिन्द्रः । दृळ्हान्यौभ्नादुशमान ओजोऽवाभिनत्ककुभः पर्वतानाम् ॥
4.19.e: Indra with might shook earth and her foundation as the wind stirs the water with its fury.  Striving, with strength he burst the firm asunder, and tore away the summits of the mountains.

4.19.d: अभि प्र दद्रुर्जनयो न गर्भं रथा इव प्र ययुः साकमद्रयः । अतर्पयो विसृत उब्ज ऊर्मीन्त्वं वृताँ अरिणा इन्द्र सिन्धून् ॥
4.19.e: They ran to thee as mothers to their offspring: the clouds, like chariots, hastened forth together.  Thou didst refresh the streams and force the billows: thou, Indra, settest free obstructed rivers.

4.19.d: त्वं महीमवनिं विश्वधेनां तुर्वीतये वय्याय क्षरन्तीम् । अरमयो नमसैजदर्णः सुतरणाँ अकृणोरिन्द्र सिन्धून् ॥
4.19.e: Thou for the sake of Vayya and Turvīti didst stay the great stream, flowing, all-sustaining:  Yea, at their prayer didst check the rushing river and make the floods easy to cross, O Indra.

4.19.d: प्राग्रुवो नभन्वो३ न वक्वा ध्वस्रा अपिन्वद्युवतीर्ऋतज्ञाः । धन्वान्यज्राँ अपृणक्तृषाणाँ अधोगिन्द्रः स्तर्यो३ दंसुपत्नीः ॥
4.19.e: He let the young Maids skilled in Law, unwedded, like fountains, bubbling, flow forth streaming onward.  He inundated thirsty plains and deserts, and milked the dry Cows of the mighty master.

4.19.d: पूर्वीरुषसः शरदश्च गूर्ता वृत्रं जघन्वाँ असृजद्वि सिन्धून् । परिष्ठिता अतृणद्बद्बधानाः सीरा इन्द्रः स्रवितवे पृथिव्या ॥
4.19.e: Through many a morn and many a lovely autumn, having slain Vṛtra, he set free the rivers.  Indra hath set at liberty to wander on earth the streams encompassed pressed together.

4.19.d: वम्रीभिः पुत्रमग्रुवो अदानं निवेशनाद्धरिव आ जभर्थ । व्य१न्धो अख्यदहिमाददानो निर्भूदुखच्छित्समरन्त पर्व ॥
4.19.e: Lord of Bay Steeds, thou broughtest from the ant-hill the unwedded damsel's son whom ants were eating.  The blind saw clearly, as he grasped the serpent, rose, brake the jar: his joints again united.

4.19.d: प्र ते पूर्वाणि करणानि विप्राविद्वाँ आह विदुषे करांसि । यथायथा वृष्ण्यानि स्वगूर्तापांसि राजन्नर्याविवेषीः ॥
4.19.e: To the wise man, O Sage and Sovran Ruler, the man who knoweth all thine ancient exploits.  Hath told these deeds of might as thou hast wrought them, great acts, spontaneous, and to man's advantage.

4.19.d: नू ष्टुत इन्द्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो३ न पीपेः । अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
4.19.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let powers swell high, like rivers, for the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays! is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.20.d: आ न इन्द्रो दूरादा न आसादभिष्टिकृदवसे यासदुग्रः । ओजिष्ठेभिर्नृपतिर्वज्रबाहुः संगे समत्सु तुर्वणिः पृतन्यून् ॥
4.20.e: FROM near or far away may mighty Indra giver of succour, come for our protection  Lord of men, armed with thunder, with the Strongest, slaying his foes in conflict, in the battles.

4.20.d: आ न इन्द्रो हरिभिर्यात्वच्छार्वाचीनोऽवसे राधसे च । तिष्ठाति वज्री मघवा विरप्शीमं यज्ञमनु नो वाजसातौ ॥
4.20.e: May Indra come to us with Tawny Coursers, inclined to us, to favour and enrich us.  May Maghavan, loud-voiced and wielding thunder, stand by us at this sacrifice, in combat.

4.20.d: इमं यज्ञं त्वमस्माकमिन्द्र पुरो दधत्सनिष्यसि क्रतुं नः । श्वघ्नीव वज्रिन्त्सनये धनानां त्वया वयमर्य आजिं जयेम ॥
4.20.e: Thou, honouring this our sacrifice, O Indra, shalt give us strength and fill us full of courage.  To win the booty, Thunder-armed! like hunters may we with thee subdue in fight our foemen.

4.20.d: उशन्नु षु णः सुमना उपाके सोमस्य नु सुषुतस्य स्वधावः । पा इन्द्र प्रतिभृतस्य मध्वः समन्धसा ममदः पृष्ठ्येन ॥
4.20.e: Loving us well, benevolent, close beside us, drink, Godlike Indra, of the well-pressed Soma.  Drink of the meath we offer, and delight thee with food that cometh from the mountain ridges.

4.20.d: वि यो ररप्श ऋषिभिर्नवेभिर्वृक्षो न पक्वः सृण्यो न जेता । मर्यो न योषामभि मन्यमानोऽच्छा विवक्मि पुरुहूतमिन्द्रम् ॥
4.20.e: Him who is sung aloud by recent sages, like a ripe-fruited tree, a scythe-armed victor,—  I, like a bridegroom thinking of his consort, call hither Indra, him invoked of many;

4.20.d: गिरिर्न यः स्वतवाँ ऋष्व इन्द्रः सनादेव सहसे जात उग्रः । आदर्ता वज्रं स्थविरं न भीम उद्नेव कोशं वसुना न्यृष्टम् ॥
4.20.e: Him who in native strength is like a mountain, the lofty Indra born or old for conquest,  Terrific wielder of the ancient thunder. filled full with splendour as a jar with water.

4.20.d: न यस्य वर्ता जनुषा न्वस्ति न राधस आमरीता मघस्य । उद्वावृषाणस्तविषीव उग्रास्मभ्यं दद्धि पुरुहूत रायः ॥
4.20.e: Whom from of old there is not one to hinder, none to curtail the riches of his bounty.  Pouring forth freely, O thou Strong and Mighty, vouchsafe us riches, God invoked of many!

4.20.d: ईक्षे रायः क्षयस्य चर्षणीनामुत व्रजमपवर्तासि गोनाम् । शिक्षानरः समिथेषु प्रहावान्वस्वो राशिमभिनेतासि भूरिम् ॥
4.20.e: Of wealth and homes of men thou art the ruler, and opener of the stable of the cattle.  Helper of men, winner of spoil in combats, thou leadest to an ample heap of riches.

4.20.d: कया तच्छृण्वे शच्या शचिष्ठो यया कृणोति मुहु का चिदृष्वः । पुरु दाशुषे विचयिष्ठो अंहोऽथा दधाति द्रविणं जरित्रे ॥
4.20.e: By what great might is he renowned as strongest, wherewith the Lofty One stirs up wild battles?  Best soother of the worshipper's great sorrow, he gives possessions to the man who lauds him.

4.20.d: मा नो मर्धीरा भरा दद्धि तन्नः प्र दाशुषे दातवे भूरि यत्ते । नव्ये देष्णे शस्ते अस्मिन्त उक्थे प्र ब्रवाम वयमिन्द्र स्तुवन्तः ॥
4.20.e: Slay us not; bring, bestow onus the ample gift which thou hast to give to him who offers.  At this new gift, with this laud sung before thee, extolling thee, we, Indra, will declare it.

4.20.d: नू ष्टुत इन्द्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो३ न पीपेः । अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
4.20.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell high, like rivers, for the singer.  A new hymn, Lord of Bays! for thee is fashioned. May we, car-born, through song be victors ever.

4.21.d: आ यात्विन्द्रोऽवस उप न इह स्तुतः सधमादस्तु शूरः । वावृधानस्तविषीर्यस्य पूर्वीर्द्यौर्न क्षत्रमभिभूति पुष्यात् ॥
4.21.e: MAY Indra come to us for our protection; here be the Hero, praised, our feast-companion.  May he whose powers are many, waxen mighty, cherish, like Dyaus, his own supreme dominion.

4.21.d: तस्येदिह स्तवथ वृष्ण्यानि तुविद्युम्नस्य तुविराधसो नॄन् । यस्य क्रतुर्विदथ्यो३ न सम्राट् साह्वान्तरुत्रो अभ्यस्ति कृष्टीः ॥
4.21.e: Here magnify his great heroic exploits, most glorious One, enriching men with bounties,  Whose will is like a Sovran in assembly, who rules the people, Conqueror, all-surpassing.

4.21.d: आ यात्विन्द्रो दिव आ पृथिव्या मक्षू समुद्रादुत वा पुरीषात् । स्वर्णरादवसे नो मरुत्वान्परावतो वा सदनादृतस्य ॥
4.21.e: Hither let Indra come from earth or heaven, hither with speech from firmament or ocean;  With Maruts, from the realm of light to aid us, or from a distance, from the seat of Order.

4.21.d: स्थूरस्य रायो बृहतो य ईशे तमु ष्टवाम विदथेष्विन्द्रम् । यो वायुना जयति गोमतीषु प्र धृष्णुया नयति वस्यो अच्छ ॥
4.21.e: That Indra will we laud in our assemblies, him who is Lord of great and lasting riches,  Victor with Vāyu where the herds are gathered, who leads with boldness on to higher fortune.

4.21.d: उप यो नमो नमसि स्तभायन्नियर्ति वाचं जनयन्यजध्यै । ऋञ्जसानः पुरुवार उक्थैरेन्द्रं कृण्वीत सदनेषु होता ॥
4.21.e: May the Priest, Lord of many blessings, striving,—who fixing reverence on reverence, giving  Vent to his voice, inciteth men to worship—with lauds bring Indra hither to our dwellings.

4.21.d: धिषा यदि धिषण्यन्तः सरण्यान्त्सदन्तो अद्रिमौशिजस्य गोहे । आ दुरोषाः पास्त्यस्य होता यो नो महान्त्संवरणेषु वह्निः ॥
4.21.e: When sitting pondering in deep devotion in Auśija's abode they ply the press-stone,  May he whose wrath is fierce, the mighty bearer, come as the house-lord's priest within our chambers.

4.21.d: सत्रा यदीं भार्वरस्य वृष्णः सिषक्ति शुष्मः स्तुवते भराय । गुहा यदीमौशिजस्य गोहे प्र यद्धिये प्रायसे मदाय ॥
4.21.e: Surely the power of Bhārvara the mighty for ever helpeth to support the singer;  That which in Auśija's abode lies hidden, to come forth for delight and for devotion.

4.21.d: वि यद्वरांसि पर्वतस्य वृण्वे पयोभिर्जिन्वे अपां जवांसि । विदद्गौरस्य गवयस्य गोहे यदी वाजाय सुध्यो३ वहन्ति ॥
4.21.e: When he unbars the spaces of the mountains, and quickens with his floods the water-torrents,  He finds in lair the buffalo and wild-ox when the wise lead him on to vigorous exploit.

4.21.d: भद्रा ते हस्ता सुकृतोत पाणी प्रयन्तारा स्तुवते राध इन्द्र । का ते निषत्तिः किमु नो ममत्सि किं नोदुदु हर्षसे दातवा उ ॥
4.21.e: Auspicious are thy hands, thine arms well-fashioned which proffer bounty, Indra, to thy praiser.  What sloth is this? Why dost thou not rejoice thee? Why dost thou not delight thyself with giving?

4.21.d: एवा वस्व इन्द्रः सत्यः सम्राड्ढन्ता वृत्रं वरिवः पूरवे कः । पुरुष्टुत क्रत्वा नः शग्धि रायो भक्षीय तेऽवसो दैव्यस्य ॥
4.21.e: So Indra is the truthful Lord of treasure. Freedom he gave to man by slaying Vṛtra.  Much-lauded! help us with thy power to riches: may I be sharer of thy Godlike favour.

4.21.d: नू ष्टुत इन्द्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो३ न पीपेः । अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
4.21.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell high, like rivers, for the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays! is fashioned. May we, care-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.22.d: यन्न इन्द्रो जुजुषे यच्च वष्टि तन्नो महान्करति शुष्म्या चित् । ब्रह्म स्तोमं मघवा सोममुक्था यो अश्मानं शवसा बिभ्रदेति ॥
4.22.e: THAT gift of ours which Indra loves and welcomes, even that he makes for us, the Great and Strong One.  He who comes wielding in his might the thunder, Maghavan, gives prayer, praise, and laud, and Soma.

4.22.d: वृषा वृषन्धिं चतुरश्रिमस्यन्नुग्रो बाहुभ्यां नृतमः शचीवान् । श्रिये परुष्णीमुषमाण ऊर्णां यस्याः पर्वाणि सख्याय विव्ये ॥
4.22.e: Bull, hurler of the four-edged rain-producer with both his arms, strong, mighty, most heroic;  Wearing as wool Paruṣṇī for adornment, whose joints for sake of friendship he hath covered.

4.22.d: यो देवो देवतमो जायमानो महो वाजेभिर्महद्भिश्च शुष्मैः । दधानो वज्रं बाह्वोरुशन्तं द्याममेन रेजयत्प्र भूम ॥
4.22.e: God who of all the Gods was born divinest, endowed with ample strength and mighty powers,  And bearing in his arms the yearning thunder, with violent rush caused heaven and earth to tremble.

4.22.d: विश्वा रोधांसि प्रवतश्च पूर्वीर्द्यौर्ऋष्वाज्जनिमन्रेजत क्षाः । आ मातरा भरति शुष्म्या गोर्नृवत्परिज्मन्नोनुवन्त वाताः ॥
4.22.e: Before the High God, at his birth, heaven trembled, earth, many floods and all the precipices.  The Strong One bringeth nigh the Bull's two Parents: loud sing the winds, like men, in air's mid-region.

4.22.d: ता तू त इन्द्र महतो महानि विश्वेष्वित्सवनेषु प्रवाच्या । यच्छूर धृष्णो धृषता दधृष्वानहिं वज्रेण शवसाविवेषीः ॥
4.22.e: These are thy great deeds, Indra, thine, the Mighty, deeds to be told aloud at all libations,  That thou, O Hero, bold and boldly daring, didst with thy bolt, by strength, destroy the Dragon.

4.22.d: ता तू ते सत्या तुविनृम्ण विश्वा प्र धेनवः सिस्रते वृष्ण ऊध्नः । अधा ह त्वद्वृषमणो भियानाः प्र सिन्धवो जवसा चक्रमन्त ॥
4.22.e: True are all these thy deeds, O Most Heroic. The Milch-kine issued from the streaming udder.  In fear of thee, O thou of manly spirit, the rivers swiftly set themselves in motion.

4.22.d: अत्राह ते हरिवस्ता उ देवीरवोभिरिन्द्र स्तवन्त स्वसारः । यत्सीमनु प्र मुचो बद्बधाना दीर्घामनु प्रसितिं स्यन्दयध्यै ॥
4.22.e: With joy, O Indra, Lord of Tawny Coursers, the Sisters then, these Goddesses, extolled thee,  When thou didst give the prisoned ones their freedom to wander at their will in long succession.

4.22.d: पिपीळे अंशुर्मद्यो न सिन्धुरा त्वा शमी शशमानस्य शक्तिः । अस्मद्र्यक्छुशुचानस्य यम्या आशुर्न रश्मिं तुव्योजसं गोः ॥
4.22.e: Pressed is the gladdening stalk as ’twere a river: so let the rite, the toiler's power, attract thee  To us-ward, of the Bright One, as the courser strains his. exceedingly strong leather bridle.

4.22.d: अस्मे वर्षिष्ठा कृणुहि ज्येष्ठा नृम्णानि सत्रा सहुरे सहांसि । अस्मभ्यं वृत्रा सुहनानि रन्धि जहि वधर्वनुषो मर्त्यस्य ॥
4.22.e: Ever by us perform thy most heroic, thine highest, best victorious deeds, O Victor.  For us make Vṛtras easy to be conquered: destroy the weapon of our mortal foeman.

4.22.d: अस्माकमित्सु शृणुहि त्वमिन्द्रास्मभ्यं चित्राँ उप माहि वाजान् । अस्मभ्यं विश्वा इषणः पुरंधीरस्माकं सु मघवन्बोधि गोदाः ॥
4.22.e: Graciously listen to our prayer, O Indra, and strength of varied sort bestow thou on us.  Send to us all intelligence arid wisdom O Maghavan, be he who gives us cattle.

4.22.d: नू ष्टुत इन्द्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो३ न पीपेः । अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
4.22.e: Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let wealth swell high like rivers to the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

4.23.d: कथा महामवृधत्कस्य होतुर्यज्ञं जुषाणो अभि सोममूधः । पिबन्नुशानो जुषमाणो अन्धो ववक्ष ऋष्वः शुचते धनाय ॥
4.23.e: How, what priest's sacrifice hath he made mighty, rejoicing in the Soma and its fountain?  Delighting in juice, eagerly drinking, the Lofty One hath waxed for splendid riches.

4.23.d: को अस्य वीरः सधमादमाप समानंश सुमतिभिः को अस्य । कदस्य चित्रं चिकिते कदूती वृधे भुवच्छशमानस्य यज्योः ॥
4.23.e: What hero hath been made his feast-companion? Who hath been partner in his loving-kindness?  What know we of his wondrous acts? How often comes he to aid and speed the pious toiler?

4.23.d: कथा शृणोति हूयमानमिन्द्रः कथा शृण्वन्नवसामस्य वेद । का अस्य पूर्वीरुपमातयो ह कथैनमाहुः पपुरिं जरित्रे ॥
4.23.e: How heareth Indra offered invocation? How, hearing, marketh he the invoker's wishes?  What are his ancient acts of bounty? Wherefore call they him One who filleth full the singer?

4.23.d: कथा सबाधः शशमानो अस्य नशदभि द्रविणं दीध्यानः । देवो भुवन्नवेदा म ऋतानां नमो जगृभ्वाँ अभि यज्जुजोषत् ॥
4.23.e: How doth the priest who laboureth, ever longing, win for himself the wealth which he possesseth?  May he, the God, mark well my truthful praises, having received the homage which he loveth.

4.23.d: कथा कदस्या उषसो व्युष्टौ देवो मर्तस्य सख्यं जुजोष । कथा कदस्य सख्यं सखिभ्यो ये अस्मिन्कामं सुयुजं ततस्रे ॥
4.23.e: How, and what bond of friendship with a mortal hath the God chosen as this morn is breaking?  How, and what love hath he for those who love him, who have entwined in him their firm affection?

4.23.d: किमादमत्रं सख्यं सखिभ्यः कदा नु ते भ्रात्रं प्र ब्रवाम । श्रिये सुदृशो वपुरस्य सर्गाः स्व१र्ण चित्रतममिष आ गोः ॥
4.23.e: Is then thy friendship with thy friends most mighty? Thy brotherhood with us,—when may we tell it?  The streams of milk move, as most wondrous sunlight, the beauty of the Lovely One for glory.

4.23.d: द्रुहं जिघांसन्ध्वरसमनिन्द्रां तेतिक्ते तिग्मा तुजसे अनीका । ऋणा चिद्यत्र ऋणया न उग्रो दूरे अज्ञाता उषसो बबाधे ॥
4.23.e: About to stay the Indra-less destructive spirit he sharpens his keen arms to strike her.  Whereby the Strong, although our debts’ exactor, drives in the distant mornings that we know not.

4.23.d: ऋतस्य हि शुरुधः सन्ति पूर्वीर्ऋतस्य धीतिर्वृजिनानि हन्ति । ऋतस्य श्लोको बधिरा ततर्द कर्णा बुधानः शुचमान आयोः ॥
4.23.e: Eternal Law hath varied food that strengthens; thought of eternal Law, removes transgressions.  The praise-hymn of eternal Law, arousing, glowing, hath oped the deaf ears of the living.

4.23.d: ऋतस्य दृळ्हा धरुणानि सन्ति पुरूणि चन्द्रा वपुषे वपूंषि । ऋतेन दीर्घमिषणन्त पृक्ष ऋतेन गाव ऋतमा विवेशुः ॥
4.23.e: Firm-seated are eternal Law's foundations in its fair form are many splendid beauties.  By holy Law long lasting food they bring us; by holy Law have cows come to our worship.

4.23.d: ऋतं येमान ऋतमिद्वनोत्यृतस्य शुष्मस्तुरया उ गव्युः । ऋताय पृथ्वी बहुले गभीरे ऋताय धेनू परमे दुहाते ॥
4.23.e: Fixing eternal Law he, too, upholds it swift moves the might of Law and wins the booty.  To Law belong the vast deep Earth and Heaven: Milch-kine supreme, to Law their milk they render.

4.23.d: नू ष्टुत इन्द्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो३ न पीपेः । अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
4.23.e: Now, Indra! lauded,—glorified with praises, let power swell high like rivers to the singer.  For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.
